News.title: Miracle moment pregnant woman is pulled from rubble of deadly New York City building collapse as husband is live on TV
News.content:
Next

A PREGNANT woman has been pulled alive from the rubble of a New York City building collapse in a miracle moment caught on camera.

The daring rescue was made just moments after her desperate husband was filmed live on television frantically trying to find her.



At least two people have been killed and 17 injured, including seven children, after the three-story building in Brooklyn collapsed just after 4pm on Wednesday.

More than 250 emergency responders attended the scene and the search for survivors continues with the help of dog and drone units.





Footage from the scene shows the moment a sniffer dog alerted officials to a victim underneath the mountain of rubble.

The woman, who is six months pregnant, was pulled out on a stretcher, with one clip showing her protectively pulling her top over her bump before being covered with a blue blanket.

read more on news TRAGIC LOSS General Hospital star dies aged 75 as tributes flood in for ‘charming’ actor

CBS News New York’s Allen Devlin told the news outlet how he had noticed a man looking particularly frantic and distressed at the scene, before learning that his wife was inside and unaccounted for.

“This is tough, man. He’s looking for his pregnant wife, and she’s not picking up the phone,” New York City Public Advocate Jumaane Williams said from the scene.



Devlin saw the man repeatedly dial his wife’s number to a phone that continually went dead.

The CBS reporter detailed how the man continued to pace and pray while begging officials to help find his wife as the news station’s chopper captured footage of a rescue.

It was then that Devin was told a woman was being pulled from the rubble at around 6:30pm, which was all caught on camera.

“I got a photo from the feed from you guys there in the newsroom that showed me the woman, and it ended up that she was pregnant,” Devlin said.



“We approached the gentleman on the side of the road and said look, they just pulled someone out from the rubble, this does not mean it is your wife but it is a pregnant woman. Do you recognize her?

“He stopped, he stared at the phone and said yes.”



The unidentified man, who collapsed into tears with relief after a grueling two-hour wait for news, was supported by Williams as his wife received medical attention.

“I have an update. She is alive, she is still alive. I am very happy,” he said, per ABC News.

“I’m very happy. I want to thank all of you guys,” he told first responders at the scene.

According to City Councilwoman Farah Louis, the woman who was wheeled into an ambulance at the scene was in critical condition as of Wednesday night, CBS News reported.

The cause of the building collapse remains unknown and under investigation, the New York Fire Department confirmed.



At the time of the collapse, the building which consisted of apartments on top of a ground-floor business was on the edge of a construction site where another one-story building had been demolished.

“That particular lot has been vacant for a long time. It used to be a senior, adult day care,” New York State Representative Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn told NY1.

“They were waiting for a permit to build affordable housing. We don’t know the details in terms of why the building collapsed but all I know is it’s probably been neglected.”

As the search for survivors continues, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani asked New Yorkers to “join in holding our neighbors and the members of this community in our hearts.”

“My heart breaks for the family who lost a loved one in today’s building collapse in Brooklyn,” New York Governor Kathy Hochul added.

“I’m keeping them in my thoughts and praying for everyone affected.

“My administration has reached out and offered its full support as authorities investigate what happened.”

News.title: Putin’s top colonel blown up as car bomb explodes in second ambush on Russian military in months in St Petersburg
News.content:
Next

A WARMONGERING Vladimir Putin colonel has been killed in a car bomb blast suspected to be a Ukrainian assassination plot.

The commander, believed to be Dmitry Lobodin, was killed when a remote-control explosive detonated as his SUV pulled out of a residential block courtyard in St. Petersburg.



It marks the second such attack in the city in just three months, as attacks on Putin’s top brass mount.

Lobodin, 57, was a senior figure in the tyrant’s air force, serving as the chief navigator of the 6th Guards Air Force and Air Defence Army.



His house was reportedly located just 1300 feet from the blast site.

The device had reportedly been attached to the underside of his vehicle.



Ukraine’s secret services were immediately suspected to be behind the attack and a formal probe has been launched into the colonel’s death.

Russia has blamed Kyiv’s spooks for a succession of car bombings targeting military and security figures.



CCTV footage of the assassination shows the explosion illuminate the night sky in St. Petersburg’s Pushkin district.

Traffic was blocked as police and paramedics rushed to the scene, where Sechkov, whose legs were blown off in the blast, was pronounced dead.

Pro-war Telegram channel Voevoda said today: “Another vehicle blown up. Another terrorist attack targeting a service member.



“Relevant authorities — are you actually going to do anything about this?

“I’m not even talking about a reciprocal response. But what about basic protection, at the very least?”

The Russian Investigative Committee has launched a criminal case into “the murder of a military officer”.

The 6th Guards Air Force and Air Defence Army is one of Russia‘s most strategically important aviation divisions.

It is responsible for protecting the skies over St Petersburg and vast stretches of the country’s northwestern border with Nato states.



Its aircraft and air defence systems operate across a region extending towards the Arctic and the Baltic enclave of Kaliningrad.

They have also participated in Putin’s illegal war against Ukraine.

It comes as Donald Trump‘s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witcoff touch down in Moscow to meet Putin after two days of crunch peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

“One of the positives is we agreed that we’re going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners,” Kushner said.

“We’re going to finalise the numbers tomorrow.”

Kushner and Witkoff are expected to address the issue of including European partners in the current trilateral format.

After meeting Putin, they are expected to make their way to Ireland for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

News.title: Seven women ‘sexually assaulted’ in 30 minutes at UK university – as cops arrest 29-year-old man
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

UNI HORROR Seven women ‘sexually assaulted’ in 30 minutes at UK university – as cops arrest 29-year-old man







Next

SEVEN women were allegedly sexually assaulted within just 30 minutes in a shocking attack spree near a university.

The victims were reportedly targeted by a suspect prowling around the University of Huddersfield grounds on Tuesday evening.

Cops say all seven women managed to get away from the man after he advanced and sexually touched them.

Officers rushed to the university that evening after a call from its security office.





They established the alleged assaults had taken place between 6pm and 6.30pm.

The force has now confirmed that they have arrested a 29-year-old man on suspicion of sexual assault offences.

He remains in police custody for questioning.

Kirklees Police has remained in close contact with the university.

They say the University of Huddersfield is supporting those affected by the incident and also working to support cops investigating.

Detective Inspector Sarah Bradley, of the Kirklees District Safeguarding Unit, has sought to reassure the community.

She said: “We fully recognise the distress and concern this incident has caused and can confirm a comprehensive investigation remains ongoing into these offences.

“We continue to work closely with our partners at the University to provide reassurance to students and staff and remain fully committed to supporting victims and safeguarding those who live, study and work in Huddersfield.”



Anyone with information is urged to contact police, quoting reference 1367 of 10/11/2026.

News.title: Traffic grinds to a halt on the M60 due to horror crash with 30-minute delays and 5 miles of congestion
News.content:
Next

TRAFFIC has ground to a halt on the M60 after a horror crash – as cops rush to the scene.

Commuters have been warned of 30-minute delays and five miles of congestion following the smash in Greater Manchester this morning.



Emergency crews have been scrambled to the anticlockwise carriageway at Junction 15, for the M61 Swinton Interchange.

Huge queues of traffic have been spotted building on the busy stretch as motorists are held following the 6.45am crash.



Cars are understood to be held as far back at Junction 18, for Simister Island, according to traffic alert service Inrix.

The nature of the accident is not yet known.

The clockwise side of the M60 has also since closed between Junction 13, for Worsley, and Junction 15.

Congestion is running back all the way to Junction nine, for Trafford Park.

National Highways: “Traffic is being held on the M60 anticlockwise within J15 M61 junction due to a collision.

“Greater Manchester Police are on scene. There are 30 minute delays and 5 miles of congestion on the approach.”

News.title: Teen girl, 13, was ‘on her way to school’ before ‘attempted rape’ in woods – as cops hunt suspect
News.content:
WOODLAND HORROR Teen girl, 13, was ‘on her way to school’ before ‘attempted rape’ in woods – as cops hunt suspect







Next

A 13-YEAR-OLD girl was on her way to school before fighting off an attempted rape, cops said – as they hunt a suspect.

The teen was allegedly sexually assaulted after being targeted in Nunnery Wood in Worcester, Worcestershire, on Tuesday morning.



The alleged attacker was reported to have pulled the schoolgirl into the trees around 8.15am.

During the horror, she managed to fend off her attacker and flag a dog walker who then raised the alarm.



Nunnery Wood High School has since warned its students to walk and cycle to school with others.

And the nearby Worcester Sixth Form College has urged students to “take sensible precautions”.



The suspect is believed to have been wearing all black clothing during the alleged attack, Safer Neighbourhood Chief Inspector Dan Pilkington said.

The attacker was not known to the girl, it is understood.

He said: “A significant number of officers were sent to the area and completed searches of woods and surrounding areas.

“Enquiries are ongoing to identify the suspect, who was described as mixed race or Asian, a teenager – believed to be between 16 and 18 years of age – and was wearing all black.



“Officers will be continuing to carry out enquiries, collating CCTV to progress the investigation and will be providing a visible presence in the area.

“We thank local residents for their cooperation yesterday and extend our appreciation to the public for getting in contact with us and sharing our appeal.”

Pilkington told the BBC there would be a visible police presence around the woods, but said they “remain a safe place to be”.

He added: “If you can avoid walking, particularly alone, during the hours of darkness or take main routes, ie, not cut through the woods at those times, that would be the best advice that I can give.”

News.title: Manhunt launched after two prisoners, 31 and 37, abscond from jail late at night in silver vehicle
News.content:

JAIL BREAK Manhunt launched after two prisoners, 31 and 37, abscond from jail late at night in silver vehicle







Next

COPS have launched an urgent hunt for two lags who absconded from jail late at night.

Billy Smith, 37, and John Loveridge, 31, are understood to have fled HMP Hollesley Bay near, Woodbridge, Suffolk, in a silver vehicle.



The pair are serving a combined 13 years behind bars at the Category D prison.

Suffolk Police confirmed they missed the 11pm roll call on Tuesday.



Prison chiefs were then alerted to their disappearance in the early hours of yesterday.

Smith is serving a six-year sentence for burglary, theft and ABH offences – and is believed to have links to the Bedford area.

Meanwhile, Loveridge is serving seven years for six counts of conspiring to commit burglary and has links to the Essex area.

Issuing a statement, the force said: “Smith is serving a six-year sentence for burglary, theft and ABH offences.

“Loveridge is serving a seven-year-sentence for six counts of conspiring to commit burglary.

“Smith is described as white, 6ft 1ins tall, of medium build, black hair, a full beard. He has links to the Bedford area.



“Loveridge is described as white, approximately 5ft 7ins tall, of proportionate build with blonde hair and a full beard.

“He has links to the Harlow area of Essex.

“It is believed that the men may have left together in a silver vehicle, which was seen in the area that evening.

“Police are asking for anyone who has seen the men, or who has information regarding their whereabouts to call 101 quoting CAD 16 of today, 11 November.”

News.title: How a furious Labour row is brewing over PM’s EU love-in as he won’t resist a chance to further dream to rejoin bloc
News.content:
POLITICS FIX How a furious Labour row is brewing over PM’s EU love-in as he won’t resist a chance to further dream to rejoin bloc







Next

ANDY Burnham flies into Dublin today to cosy up to political leaders at his first major European summit.

Officially, the gathering of the European Political Community will be dominated by crucial issues like Ukraine, energy and migration.



But you can bet your bottom Euro that Britain’s Prime Minister will be unable to resist the chance to further his dream of rejoining the EU.

Mr Burnham, after all, has never been one to hide his ambitions. He wants to rejoin the bloc in his lifetime and is flirting with hated policies like freedom of movement.



And Dublin will be the perfect chance for the PM to test the water ahead of the main event next week at the UK-EU summit in Brussels.

Do not be fooled by all the jolly handshakes and smiles. Back home a furious Labour row is brewing.



Publicly, Labour MPs are giving Mr Burnham a free pass – for now.

But behind closed doors, frustration is mounting over Mr Burnham’s EU love-in.

Rejoining was never on the ballot when voters backed Labour at Sir Keir Starmer‘s landslide in 2024.

Many Labour seats voted to leave the EU in 2016, including Mr Burnham’s Makerfield constituency which backed Brexit by 65 per cent.



It is hard to see how his current policies align with the PM’s own “Makerfield test” that he set himself.

Some Cabinet ministers are acutely aware of this and are already at pains to answer questions over whether Britain should rejoin the bloc.

In future months they may have difficult decisions to make over points of principle.

Voters and politicians aside, it is hard to see the EU would welcome us back without bludgeoning us as a warning to others.

Michel Barnier – the EU’s former Brexit negotiator – has warned the UK cannot pick and choose our relationship “à la carte”.



Summits can be very boring. But in the margins, Mr Burnham will be having conversations that could soon reshape the future of the UK’s relationship with the EU.

News.title: US Army colonel arrested for ‘spying’ had access to Nato secrets that could cause ‘serious damage’ in hostile hands
News.content:
'SPY' PROBE US Army colonel arrested for ‘spying’ had access to Nato secrets that could cause ‘serious damage’ in hostile hands







Next

A U.S. soldier arrested in Britain on ­suspicion of ­spying for Russia lives in a quiet cul-de-sac with other military families.

Evidence tents were set up outside his four-bed home near his Nato base yesterday, with shocked neighbours saying they felt betrayed.



The married lieutenant colonel, 41, worked in human resources at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester, home to Nato’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps.

Top Army sources confirmed he was cleared to read material classified “Nato Secret”, which could potentially cause “serious damage” in hostile hands.



It is unclear if he had access to soldiers’ addresses and service histories.

He was arrested on Tuesday by UK counter-terror police backed by MI5, the FBI and military spy catchers here and in the US.

Plain-clothes cops were seen at his home yesterday, with his office at the base also apparently being searched. Sources said they were confident the suspect “didn’t share anything with any genuine Russians”.

One said: “He was intercepted before any damage could be done.”

But families on his estate told of their shock. A woman in her 40s whose husband works at the Nato base said there is a “wonderful international community here”.

She added: “It makes me feel sick in my stomach to think that someone could betray all that we stand for.”



Another neighbour added: “It’s absolutely chilling.”

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting hailed police and intelligence services for an “exemplary operation”.

Counter Terrorism Policing London said the arrest was under sections of the National Security Act 2023 relating to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

News.title: Boy, 3, diagnosed with lethal illness after symptoms dismissed as winter colds
News.content:
Boy, 3, diagnosed with lethal illness after symptoms dismissed as winter colds

Manraj Singh Hans began suffering regular colds along with high temperatures which he struggled to shake

View 5 Images Manraj Singh Hans kept falling ill over winter (Image: SWNS)

A three-year-old boy was diagnosed with a lethal illness after his parents originally dismissed the symptoms as being winter bugs picked up at nursery. Manraj Singh Hans began suffering regular colds along with having high temperatures, which he’d struggle to shift, but his mum and dad thought he was just tired "because it was winter."

‌



‌



Dad, Narinder, 47, and mum, Parm, 42, took him to the doctors but were sent on their way with antibiotics after being told he most likely had an infection. Manraj's symptoms went on to be repeatedly dismissed before he was eventually diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL).

‌



Narinder, of Biggleswade, said: “We'd give him Calpol and they (the symptoms) would go away, but then come back a week or so later and go on a little bit longer.

‌



"We just thought, ‘It's the winter season, we’re going to be getting colds and bugs’. He was at nursery, too, so we thought he was picking stuff up there.

View 5 Images Manraj Singh Hans pictured recently (Image: SWNS)

“We took him to the GP to get checked out and were told he could potentially have a urine infection. We were given some antibiotics, but that didn’t seem to help.

‌



“Soon after, Parm also took him to the hospital to have him looked at because he was saying his legs were hurting. They checked him and said it could be to do with the urine infection or some sort of other infection, and we were sent on our way.

“We realised afterwards that also around this time, we converted his cot into a cot bed so he could come to us in the night if needed, but he wasn't doing that. Instead, he was just calling us to come and get him. We didn't really think much of it, we just thought he was tired because it was winter.”

‌



As Manraj’s temperatures continued, Narinder and Parm made several more visits to the GPs, but his symptoms were again put down to seasonal illnesses and infections.

However, when Narinder noticed blood in his nappy, they were eventually taken more seriously. Narinder, who works as a strategic customer success manager for a tech company, added: “I took his nappy down one day and he had a little speck of blood in it.

‌



"So, we booked an appointment for him that afternoon at the GP again. Parm and I picked him up from school and we both took him. On that day, I think that the doctor we saw must have known what the symptoms could potentially be.

“We explained to her that he was, by then, also walking with a limp. This GP told us to go to straight to A&E to get a blood test, and she made the arrangements for us to go and do it.”

‌



View 5 Images Manraj Singh Hans and Ariya (Image: SWNS)

The youngster was diagnosed with ALL, a type of blood cancer which affects around 400 children in the UK each year, in February 2023. Narinder said: “I remember the hospital being very busy and we waited around for a long time, still making plans for the next day, for one of his best friends to come over for a sleepover.

‌



"We thought we’d be out of there soon, but then the night doctor came on and said we’d have to wait overnight. We did the blood test and ended up staying in one of the rooms there that night, the three of us.

"And we were thinking, ‘All right, in the morning, they'll come and tell us what they found, and then we can go home from there’. But the next morning, a doctor came around and said, ‘I'm sorry to be the bearer of the bad news, but your son has leukaemia’.

‌



“Within a few hours we were being transferred to from Bedford Hospital to Addenbrookes in Cambridge, but we didn't really have anything with us that we needed. We didn't even have a night bag, because when we went to A&E, we didn't think we’d be staying. It was obviously a huge shock.”

View 5 Images Manraj Singh Hans while undergoing treatment (Image: SWNS)

‌



Manraj underwent two years of gruelling treatment and procedures, including intensive chemotherapy, steroids, and lumbar punctures, during which he suffered a number of side effects and complications.

Narinder said: “Once he started taking some of the steroids and chemo, you could see a change in his energy. He was sleeping a lot; he lost his appetite as well.

‌



“He lost all the strength in his legs, too, they just couldn't move for very long. Even now, he still struggles on long walks.

“And one day, he had a seizure, caused by one of the drugs he was on. I remember the red button being pushed and the room suddenly filling up with doctors when it was happening. It was all really scary. It was a really traumatic time for him.”

‌



View 5 Images Manraj Singh Hans and his family at Disney World (Image: SWNS)

Now cancer-free, kind-hearted Manraj, now seven, has raised £7,000 for the CCLG: The Children & Young People’s Cancer Association. Proud dad Narinder said: “Manraj has really driven it all and made us stick to our promise of raising money each September for Childhood Cancer Awareness Month.

‌



“The fundraising is something we’ll continue to do as it’s really important to us, and the awareness side, too.”

Manraj has been in remission since March 2025 and is being monitored with regular follow-up appointments. Narinder said he is “doing really well”, adding: “He’s getting back into activities that he enjoyed doing before (cancer treatment).

‌



“He’s been getting on with his swimming and been playing football in a team regularly as well. He’s not quite at the same pace as everyone else, but he never gives up.”

The CCLG is now urging the public to recognise the signs and symptoms of cancer in children. Some of the signs and symptoms of ALL include: becoming tired and lethargic, developing bruises, taking longer to stop bleeding, bleeding gums or heavy nosebleeds, a purplish rash on the skin that does not disappear when you press a glass against it, having infections, fevers and sweating (especially at night), swollen lymph glands, and pain in the bones or joints.

News.title: UK’s best pizza named by National Pizza Awards - but there's a catch if you want to visit
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: UK’s best pizza named by National Pizza Awards - but there's a catch if you want to visit

A London pizzeria has won the award for the 'Best Pizza in the UK' at the 2026 National Pizza Awards – all before actually opening its doors to the public.

View 4 Images A London pizzeria has the best pizza in the UK (Image: Five Feet Instagram )

Tracking down the ultimate pizza in a country as vast and gastronomically rich as the UK is no mean feat, with countless top contenders battling it out for the coveted title. Mouth-watering slices of 'za can be found in every corner of the UK, making the competition an incredibly fierce contest.

‌



‌



On November 3, the National Pizza Awards, hosted by Dine Out magazine, crowned the Best Pizza in the UK — but there was one enormous catch: the winning pizzeria hadn't even opened its doors to the public yet.

‌



In a surprising yet thoroughly deserved victory, a London pizzeria on Bermondsey's Tanner Street, set to officially open on November 11, scooped the top prize for Best Pizza in the UK for its Sausage and Broccoli pizza — a Sicilian/Grandma-style pie featuring vodka sauce, pecorino, oregano, chilli, sausage, fior di latte, provolone, friarelli, pickled chillies, ricotta and Coolea.

‌



Five Feet saw off stiff competition from some of the UK's biggest pizza names and independent pizzerias to claim the crown. The National Pizza Awards are open to chefs from across the restaurant, quick-service, bar, pub, and hotel industries, and Five Feet proved itself the very best of the bunch, reports MyLondon.

View 4 Images A London pizzeria has beaten stiff competition to emerge as the winner (Image: Five Feet Instagram )

We spoke to Five Feet's head chef and owner, Jack Ellingham, to hear his thoughts on the remarkable victory. The gifted Jack, who previously worked as a baker at London's Dusty Knuckle, also picked up an individual accolade, being named National Pizza Chef of the Year.

‌



Jack said: "It was a massive surprise to me. It was my first time competing at the Pizza Awards, and I did not know what to expect, to be honest. Winning the competition was absolutely huge and means more than I can express. Five Feet has been a couple of years in the making, and I've been developing the pizza we will be serving for three years."

He adds: "The opening delays mean I haven't been able to serve any customers yet. So, being able to cook a Five Feet pizza for the judges and take home the top prize felt monumental and made me even more excited to open the doors and start serving guests."

‌



View 4 Images (Pictured) Jack Ellingham's Five Feet has won the Best Pizza in the UK award (Image: Supplied )

The National Pizza Chef of the Year reckons it's crucial to "know how to make a banging pizza when you run a pizzeria", and the evidence is (quite literally) in the pie for this National Pizza Award-winning venue.

‌



In a live cooking battle against 16 of Britain's top pizzaiolos, Jack Ellingham's Five Feet - co-owned with Jay Patel, founder of Michelin Guide restaurant Legare and backed by the founder of coffee shop brand WatchHouse - triumphed over tough competition from well-known finalists including Bad Boy Pizza Society, Franco Manca, Pizza Pilgrims and Zizzi.

Speaking about why he believes Five Feet's pizzas have the upper hand over rivals, Jack said: "Five Feet brings something a little different to the table. You've got this super light, delicate dough proofed in generously oiled black iron pans for around six hours. As it bakes, the result is almost focaccia-esque, the bottom lightly fries in the extra virgin olive oil making it crisp while the interior stays soft and airy.

‌



"We also stone mill the flour for the dough using Grains grown about 30 miles from the pizzeria. The wholegrains and freshly milled flour add something pretty special to the mix, if you can find me another pizzeria stone milling its own flour let me know!"

View 4 Images The National Pizza Award winner has been crowned - but there's one surprising catch (Image: Five Feet Instagram )

‌



Jack believes there's one crucial reason Five Feet sets itself apart: "At the moment, the London pizza scene is filled with a lot of great thin and crispy pizza, so I think the pan pizza at Five Feet is a welcome addition to the market and stands in its own lane."

So, all that remains is for the National Pizza Chef of the Year to tackle the most burning question of all - what can customers look forward to from Five Feet when it finally throws open its doors to the public this November?

Article continues below

"Crispy, crunchy, fluffy, light pan pizza made from in-house milled flour, topped with outrageously good quality ingredients from incredible UK-based farmers, growers and producers (except the insanely good olive oil and tomatoes from further afield). All served up in a beautiful spot with warm hospitality, good music, good drinks - just a place where you want to hang out, eat pizza and be happy."

All 2026 winners will now be invited to take part in the National Pizza Awards Champion of Champions cook-off in February next year, as the competition marks its 10th anniversary by bringing together 30 winners from the past decade.

News.title: Early Alzheimer's warning sign may appear 'long before noticeable memory problems'
News.content:
Early Alzheimer's warning sign may appear 'long before noticeable memory problems'

Scientists say Alzheimer’s may start affecting the body earlier than some people think

View 3 Images Some people with Alzheimer’s may develop walking, balance or coordination problems "long before noticeable memory problems emerge" (Image: Getty)

A new study has found that Alzheimer's may affect one part of the body years before memory loss starts. Research published by the University of Central Florida (UCF) suggests "Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain."

‌



‌



Researchers at the UCF found that gene mutations linked to Alzheimer’s may disrupt the peripheral nerves that control muscle movement, even without any direct involvement of the brain or spinal cord. The team says this could help explain why some people with Alzheimer’s develop walking, balance or coordination problems "long before noticeable memory problems emerge."

‌



It adds that this discovery, published on November 9, 2026, "raises the possibility that movement difficulties could provide earlier warning signs of the disease and that treatments focused exclusively on the brain may overlook important problems elsewhere in the body."

‌



' Motor deficits may be earlier indication'

View 3 Images Alzheimer's isn't just about memory loss, researchers say (Image: Getty | Franziska & Tom Werner)

The study was led by James Hickman and Xiufang “Nadine” Guo at the UCF, with researchers from healthcare tech company Hesperos. Guo said: " Motor deficits may be an earlier indication [of Alzheimer's}. If we can detect those changes and intervene earlier, that could help delay the onset of central nervous system symptoms."

Why do some Alzheimer's symptoms appear before memory loss

Alzheimer's is best known for causing worsening memory loss, confusion and other thinking problems. But doctors have also seen that some people develop physical changes - such as problems with balance, coordination and the way they walk - years before obvious cognitive symptoms appear.

‌



Science Daily reports that "to investigate, the UCF team focused on familial Alzheimer's, a rare inherited form of the disease that typically develops earlier in life (from 40 to 65 years of age) than the more common form.

"Their experiments revealed that motor neurons carrying mutations linked to familial Alzheimer's could disrupt the connections responsible for controlling muscles, even when the brain and spinal cord were completely absent from the experimental system.

‌



"Motor neurons are specialized nerve cells that transmit signals to muscles, telling them when to contract and produce movement. The new findings suggest that Alzheimer's mutations can interfere with this process directly, rather than affecting movement only through damage to the brain."

Hickman says: "This is the first time it's been demonstrated that deficits in the peripheral nervous system can arise directly from these mutations. It means drugs that target the brain may not fix problems in the rest of the body."

‌



Could this mean an earlier Alzheimer's diagnosis?

The experts note that the "findings suggest a potentially important new direction for Alzheimer's research. And it involves looking beyond memory and other cognitive symptoms when investigating the disease.

"If future studies confirm that changes in motor function are detectable early in certain patients, tests of walking, coordination, or nerve-to-muscle activity might eventually help identify disease-related changes before more obvious neurological symptoms develop."

‌



More research is needed to be sure what this means. If early movement changes can be reliably picked up in some people, simple checks of walking, coordination, or nerve-to-muscle signals could one day help spot Alzheimer’s earlier, before clear brain symptoms show.

Contact Alzheimers Research UK for support

View 3 Images Reach out for support if you are struggling (Image: Getty)

‌



Experts at Alzheimers Research UK explain that because dementia can stem from several different brain diseases, getting a clear, specific diagnosis can make a real difference to how the condition is managed.

Before a dementia-causing disease is identified, a person may first be diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment. At this early stage, they can usually continue making their own decisions, with support from family and friends who understand what’s happening.

Article continues below

You can find more information about different types of dementia and their symptoms, or attend an online public event to learn more about dementia research. If you have questions about dementia, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis or treatment, contact the Alzheimer’s Research UK Infoline team on 0300 111 5111 (Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm) or email infoline@alzheimersresearchuk.org.

News.title: Seven women 'sexually assaulted' in just 30 minutes at University of Huddersfield
News.content:
Seven women 'sexually assaulted' in just 30 minutes at University of Huddersfield

Seven women were allegedly sexually assaulted within just 30 minutes around the grounds of the University of Huddersfield

View 2 Images Seven women were allegedly sexually assaulted at Huddersfield University (Image: Huddersfield Examiner)

Multiple women were allegedly sexually assaulted within just 30 minutes in a shocking series of attacks near a university.

The victims were reportedly targeted in the University of Huddersfield grounds on Tuesday evening.

Police say all seven women managed to get away from the man after he advanced and sexually touched them. Officers rushed to the university after a call from its security office.

They established the alleged assaults had taken place between 6pm and 6.30pm. The force has now confirmed that they have arrested a 29-year-old man on suspicion of sexual assault offences. He remains in police custody for questioning.

They say the University of Huddersfield is supporting those affected by the incident and also working to support cops investigating.

View 2 Images Police rushed to the University of Huddersfield (Image: Huddersfield Daily Examiner)

Detective Inspector Sarah Bradley, of the Kirklees District Safeguarding Unit, has sought to reassure the community.

Kirklees Police has remained in close contact with the university. He remains in police custody for questioning.

She said: "We fully recognise the distress and concern this incident has caused and can confirm a comprehensive investigation remains ongoing into these offences.

"We continue to work closely with our partners at the University to provide reassurance to students and staff and remain fully committed to supporting victims and safeguarding those who live, study and work in Huddersfield."

Anyone with information is urged to contact the force, quoting reference 1367 of 10/11/2026.

News.title: 20st woman with £4,800 takeaway habit unrecognisable after losing half her fat
News.content:
20st woman with £4,800 takeaway habit unrecognisable after losing half her fat

She used to eat a Full English for breakfast, down a litre of Coke, have takeaway most nights then take a large chocolate bar to bed

20st woman with £4,800 takeaway habit unrecognisable after losing half her fat

A woman who ate so many chocolate bars in bed that she ballooned to 20 stone has halved her bodyweight -and says people don't even recognise her in the street. Tracey Mummery started her weight loss journey in May 2025 after struggling with her weight since she was a teen.

‌



‌



Tipping the scales at 20st at her heaviest, 5ft 6ins Tracey says she 'always felt like the bigger friend'. The 41-year-old says she used to gorge herself on full English breakfasts, crisps, baguettes, sweets and a litre of full-fat Coke every day.

‌



Tracey was eating up to £100-worth of takeaways per week, which she would order up to five nights per week - and would even take a large chocolate bar up to bed with her. After struggling with her weight for more than two decades, Tracey decided to start using Mounjaro after ordering the skinny jab from an online pharmacy.

‌



Getting a good night's sleep could save your life, the lies people tell to get antibiotics, and goat's milk kills cancer - all this and more in our science newsletter

View 6 Images Tracey spent thousands on takeaway (Kennedy News and Media)

Tracey has now halved her bodyweight to 10st, slimming down from a dress size 24 to a slinky size 8. And the retail supervisor claims she now looks so different that people don't recognise her in the street and will often give her a 'double take'.

‌



Tracey, from Medway, Kent, said: "I get a lot of comments from people saying that I look amazing, that they can't believe how well I look and that they need to come to the gym with me. I bump into people in the street and they don't recognise me because I look that different, sometimes it's hard to get my head around.

"It's happened a few times where someone has done a double take like 'do I know you or do I not?' It's usually people that I don't see that often - like people I used to go to school with, I've bumped into them and they've said they didn't recognise me for a minute.

‌



View 6 Images Tracey used to eat chocolate in bed (Kennedy News and Media)

"It's a massive compliment that they think I look so different that they don't recognise me. It can be quite overwhelming."

‌



Prior to her weight loss, Tracey says she would spend up to £4,800 per year on fast food deliveries. Tracey said: "I used to have between four and five takeaways per week because I couldn't be bothered to cook dinner.

"I was spending £80-£100 per week on takeaways. When I was thinking about going on Mounjaro the thing that was putting me off was the money but I worked out the amount of money that I was spending on the food shop, or takeaways I could spend that on Mounjaro."

‌



View 6 Images Tracey started to lose weight last year (Kennedy News and Media)

Tracey says she even used to take a large 350g of chocolate up to bed with her. Tracey said: "At night time going up to bed I would have a big bar of chocolate, I could quite happily take one of them out of the cupboard and eat that up in bed.

‌



"I would do that a couple of times per week, my relationship with food was bad, I don't do any of that now, I don't take anything to bed with me anymore."

Tracey has now shed a 10st b ut says she has been left 'infuriated' by comments suggesting that the skinny jab is the 'lazy way' to lose weight - and says she has worked hard for her slinkier frame through a combination of diet and exercise.

‌



View 6 Images Tracey has lost 10 stone (Kennedy News and Media)

Tracey said: "I hear it all th e time that Mounjaro is the lazy way to lose weight and it frustrates me so much. Especially on social media you hear that when you're taking skinny jabs like Mounjaro that it's cheating and it infuriates me so much.

‌



"I didn't rely on Mounjaro completely; it was a tool. I worked really hard - I was calorie counting, tracking my macros, going to the gym, going out on walks. I've worked really, really hard - you don't just jab Mounjaro once a week and then the weight melts away. I'm quite passionate to defending it [Mounjaro]."

Tracey says she never thought she would be able to squeeze into a dress size 8, and now feels confident to show off her body in tight-fitting gym clothes. Tracey said: "I never thought it would be possible for me to be a size 8, I always felt like the bigger one in the friendship group.

‌



View 6 Images Tracey says it has been hard work (Kennedy News and Media)

"Now I'm just able to go into a shop and buy clothes whereas I used to have to order them online. The clothes I wear now are completely different to what I used to wear, I used to be in hoodies and leggings all the time, now I mainly wear gym clothes, my style has completely changed."

‌



Tracey, who stopped using Mounjaro in March, is now urging other women who are thinking about embarking on their weight loss journey to 'go for it'. Tracey said: "If you're thinking about starting your weight loss journey just do it and don't sit on the fence.

View 6 Images Tracey says she regrets waiting so long (Kennedy News and Media)

Article continues below

"That's the one thing that I regret - how long I was sitting on the fence about doing it. Remember every journey is different, not one person's is the same as someone else's. And keep taking before and afters and take photos and videos of your progression - when I look back, I actually can't believe the difference."

News.title: Andy Burnham commits to 2050 net zero target and promises 'leadership' on tackling climate crisis
News.content:
Andy Burnham commits to 2050 net zero target and promises 'leadership' on tackling climate crisis

Addressing the Cop31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, the PM branded the climate crisis a 'national security issue', and one hitting all of us now after a summer of wildfires

View 2 Images The PM said Britain was ready to do its part (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has promised world leaders that Britain is “back and ready to play its full part” in tackling climate change.

‌



‌



Addressing the Cop31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, the PM branded the climate crisis a “national security issue”, and one hitting all of the UK after a summer of wildfires.

‌



This year’s summer was the UK’s hottest on record, with back-to-back heatwaves causing issues with transport, hospitals, and the closure of schools across the country.

‌



Mr Burnham also promised the UK is committed to meeting its 2050 net zero target and pledged to work with other countries to reach it.

Al Gore speaks movingly at climate summit as rogue politicians defy Trump to represent US READ MORE :

View 2 Images Dame Madeleine Alessandri was announced as the first UK Special Representative for Climate Security (Image: civilservicelive.gov)

He said: “The summer from which Britain recently emerged was not normal. I spent my first three weeks as Prime Minister responding to the worst wildfires Britain has ever experienced. I decided then it was important for me to be here to show British leadership in a world where climate issues have taken too much of a back seat.

‌



“The climate crisis is not a distant threat. It is upon us all now, devastating lives and livelihoods everywhere. Meanwhile, two wars across two continents have sent fuel prices and gas bills soaring for families and businesses across the world. The common thread running through all of this: our dependence on fossil fuels.

“The message I carry here at my first COP as UK Prime Minister is this: we are committed to meeting our 2050 net zero target, and committed to working with all of our partners to reach theirs.”

‌



It comes just hours after the PM hailed a £12billion investment in wind farms as "great for billpayers", with construction set to begin on the Norfolk-coast based projects early next year.

During the speech, Mr Burnham also announced Dame Madeleine Alessandri as the first UK Special Representative for Climate Security. Her role will involve strengthening international partnerships and ensuring climate and nature risks are treated as a matter of national security, with a focus on identifying risks before they develop into crises.

‌



The PM told world leaders the crisis can only be solved in “partnership”, and that Britain was again focused on the environment as the Tories abandoned their climate commitments.

He said: “This crisis can only be solved in partnership. I have pledged a new era of British leadership over the next decade. The consensus we once enjoyed on science and climate has gone, and the reality is now the world will breach 1.5 degrees.

Article continues below

"Climate leadership and action have become more urgent. Britain will answer the call. Britain will live up to its commitments. We will help our friends as they live up to theirs. Britain is back and ready to play its full part.”

News.title: UK economy 'defies doomsayers' after GDP grows over summer driven by boom in roll-out of AI
News.content:
UK economy 'defies doomsayers' after GDP grows over summer driven by boom in roll-out of AI

Growth of artificial intelligence helps power stronger-than-forecast growth in the UK economy in the third quarter of this year, with other sectors doing well including car dealers, accountancy and recruitment agencies

View 3 Images Chancellor John Healey says UK economy is showing "standout resilience" and growing at the fastest rate in almost a decade (Image: Stefan Rousseau/Press Association)

The UK economy has defied doomsayers again by growing by 0.7% over the summer, official data has confirmed.

‌



‌



Chancellor John Healey said the results showed the country was showing "standout resilience" and growing at the fastest rate in almost a decade. The latest data for the third quarter - July to September - comes on the back of stronger-than-forecast growth in the first half of 2026. Growth in September alone was 0.2%.

‌



Sanjay Raja, chief UK economist at Deutsche Bank, said the UK economy was in "top gear".

‌



However, experts warned the "fly in the ointment" for millions of borrowers was it made another Bank of England rake hike more likely. The Bank, which upped its base rate to 4% earlier this month, is tasked with cooling inflation but would be wary of unleashing another hike if the economy was weak.

The Office for National Statistics said the 0.7% growth in the UK's gross domestic product was almost entirely due to what is termed the service sector, which makes up the bulk of the economy and includes everything from banks to pubs. But drilling into the data revealed that the UK’s IT industry was the main driver, helped by the rapid roll-out of AI technology.

‌



View 3 Images The largest forecast defying growth figures for the UK are a boost to Chancellor John Healey (Image: Jeff Overs/BBC/Press Association)

Others doing well included car dealers, accountancy and recruitment agencies, the last of which adding to evidence that the UK’s jobs market is holding up better than many economists expected. GDP has now grown by 1.9% over the first nine months of the year, putting the UK on track to be the second-fastest growing economy in the G7 group of countries, just behind the US at 2%.

‌



Professor Joe Nellis , head of economic research at accountancy and advisory firm. MHA, said "UK economy continues to defy doomsayers but the road ahead is bleak."

However, the resilience of the economy will be "severely tested" over the coming months by rising inflation and interest rates. the government was warned. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: “Despite a year where events around the world have pushed up costs here at home, our economy is growing, bringing hope for the future.

‌



"Our job now is to keep focused on what matters to people: bringing down bills, creating good jobs, helping high streets thrive and backing businesses to grow. There is more to do, but we have a clear direction."

View 3 Images Experts say the "fly in the ointment" of stronger economic growth could be another Bank of England rate hike (Image: Getty)

‌



Chancellor John Healey said: “The Middle East conflict has hit growth worldwide, yet Britain is showing standout resilience. Our UK economy is growing at the fastest rate in almost 10 years, outside the pandemic. We are backing UK investment, innovation and fast growth firms. I want to bring back confidence in Britain.”

TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak said: “It’s great that our economy strengthened further over the summer. This faster growth is a vital foundation for creating jobs and rising living standards. But despite this good news, working people across the country are still up against it today as they face spiralling energy bills as a result of Trump’s illegal was in Iran.

‌



“So the Chancellor was right to tax banks’ enormous profits to support families - £100 for most households this January will help cover eye-watering energy costs. After this, more support will still be needed - the next steps should be a social tariff to give low- and middle-income families permanent help with their energy bills.”

Simon Pittaway, senior economist at think tank the Resolution Foundation, said: “The UK’s strong economic performance has continued into the second half of the year, which is all the more impressive given the ongoing disruption caused by conflict in the Middle East. But with inflation and interest rates both forecast to rise towards 5 %, this resilience will be severely tested in the coming months.

‌



“Stepping back, the good news is that the UK looks to be breaking free of its reputation as a stagnation nation. The less positive news is that stronger economic growth is yet to translate into big living standards gains.”

Samuel Fuller, director of Financial Markets Online, said: "If retailers deliver a strong ‘golden quarter’ in the run-up to Christmas, growth for 2026 as a whole should easily surpass the Bank of England’s 1.6% forecast.

Article continues below

“This is the fly in the ointment for anyone thinking of moving home, or the hundreds of thousands due to remortgage in coming months, because it opens the door to higher interest rates."

News.title: People with extension leads at home should make urgent decision
News.content:
People with extension leads at home should make urgent decision

A warning has been issued as more people plug in electric blankets, space heaters, and Christmas decorations

View 3 Images People using extension leads have been issued a warning (Image: Getty )

Homeowners who routinely rely on extension leads around the house are being urged to reconsider their habits straight away. As many households begin to switch on electrical items such as space heaters, electric blankets and festive decorations, UK residents are being cautioned to use extension leads carefully.

‌



‌



Households are being advised to be conscious of how many appliances they plug in this autumn and winter, as failing to do so could render their insurance invalid. A recent survey by the insurance specialists at Quotezone.co.uk found that 32% of Britons were unaware that unsafe electrical practices could impact a claim for damage or fire.

‌



According to the London Fire Brigade, one of the most frequent causes of electrical fires is overloaded sockets. It's thought overloaded sockets and faulty electrical appliances are responsible for roughly 7,000 house fires across the nation each year.

‌



Despite this, the survey revealed 53% of Brits confessed to plugging one extension lead or adaptor into another to generate additional sockets. In certain cases, insurers may decline to pay out for fires caused by overloaded sockets if they consider the homeowner was negligent or failed to take reasonable measures to prevent the fire from occurring.

View 3 Images Brits warned overloading plugs could invalidate home insurance (Image: Getty)

As autumn draws near, many of us find ourselves using more electrical appliances simultaneously, particularly as temperatures drop and nights draw in earlier. Numerous households will be switching on their portable heaters, electric blankets, dehumidifiers, lamps and fairy lights, but running too many devices at once can place additional pressure on plug sockets and heighten the risk of overheating, electrical failures and potentially even fires.

‌



Homeowners ought to be aware that the typical plug socket shouldn't be loaded with more than 3,000 watts. The wattage of a device is generally displayed on its label or plug, though as a rule of thumb, homeowners should steer clear of plugging several high-powered appliances into a single extension lead. This includes items such as kettles, irons, hair dryers, and portable heaters.

‌



Should the socket or plug feel abnormally hot when touched, show discolouration around the socket, emit a melted-plastic odour, or produce crackling and sizzling noises, it's probable the plug socket is overheating, and all appliances should be switched off and unplugged immediately. Helen Rolph, home insurance expert at Quotezone, is urging households with extension leads to take immediate action and reassess how they use them if they're overloaded.

View 3 Images Brits warned over overloaded plug sockets as 53% admit dangerous extension lead habit

‌



"A lot of people aren't aware of how dangerous it can be to overload your plug sockets and the consequences that come along with it," she said. "As the weather starts to take a turn, households will automatically be using more electrical appliances like portable heaters, heated blankets, tumble dryers, and hair dryers just to name a few.

"If you're plugging loads of high-powered electricals into one extension cord, there is a very high chance it could overheat. A fire that breaks out from this isn't automatically covered on your home insurance either.

‌



"Once investigated, if your insurer feels like there was negligence involved, it could invalidate your insurance and you may not be able to make a claim. We want everyone to take care this autumn and winter and be mindful of what items they're plugging into a single electrical lead."
