News.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
News.content:
Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.

As reported in the Times,, external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits.

Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet".

He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.

His report is expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of universal credit or personal independence payment (Pip).

Instead, they would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit.

Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions.

Some claimants would receive less under the plans - although the exact amounts will not be clear until early next year, when the government publishes legislation to implement the changes.

People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions. It is available to those both in and out of work.

Of the four million people claiming Pip in England and Wales, around 430,000 are aged between 16 and 24.

In his interim report,, external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were not in education, employment or training.

Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers.

Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate.

Milburn told the Times about his report: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system.

News.title: Hegseth and advisers reprimanded by guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
News.content:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and a group he was with were reprimanded by a sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery on Wednesday. The incident followed a wreath-laying ceremony marking Veterans Day.

Hegseth had joined the group for a photo and someone laughed, prompting the US Army sentinel guarding the tomb to shout. "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times", the sentinel said.

According to the BBC's US partner, CBS News, the people in the photo before the reprimand also included Hegseth's advisers Patrick Weaver and Tami Radabaugh, Hegseth's chief of staff Ricky Buria and Hegseth's wife Jennifer Hegseth.

"While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum," Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement.

News.title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?
News.content:
Your throat's painful, your head throbs and your blocked nose has kept you awake all night. It's that time of year again - flu season - and you'll try anything to feel normal.

But is that pricey max strength flu remedy really any better than a basic box of painkillers?

"The big brands have been around for a while, they've been tested, and there are adverts on the TV saying they're really good," says Prof Jayne Lawrence, head of the pharmacy division at the University of Manchester.

"But in reality, there's very little difference. Personally, I'd always go for the cheaper ones - and theyâve also been tested."

The trade association representing over-the-counter medicine makers says familiar brands can reassure shoppers and help them find the right product on crowded supermarket shelves.

The medications we've highlighted all contain similar ingredients with marginal differences to their quantities.

News.title: Media industry could be forced to improve safeguards after Walliams allegations
News.content:
The government is prepared to force the entertainment industry to improve safeguarding practices unless rapid change is introduced, BBC Newsnight has learned.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy will tell a meeting of industry leaders next week that if their response to recent allegations is not robust enough, she is prepared to force participation in the industry body to protect whistleblowers, the BBC understands.

Participation in the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority (CIISA) is currently voluntary.

It comes after an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News alleged that entertainer David Walliams had been accused by several women of sexual misconduct and abusing his position, which he denies.

Nandy said earlier this week that she was summoning leaders from the broadcasting, publishing, film and entertainment industries to "draw a line" in the sand.

That announcement came after the publication of allegations against Walliams, as well as the sentencing of disgraced entertainer Russell Brand on charges of rape and sexual assault.

The allegations against Walliams were made as a part of a joint three-year investigation that was published after the entertainer lost a legal bid to stop the claims against him being made public. Walliams denies all the allegations against him.

BBC Newsnight understands that the culture secretary will deliver two messages at next week's round-table meeting.

In the first instance, she will tell industry leaders that they need to meet the moment, take responsibility and tackle issues of safeguarding on their own. But she will add that if their response is not good enough, the government might have to intervene.

Intervention could include forcing participation in the CIISA.

Multiple government ministers gave statements on Wednesday that called for further restrictions on the use of non-disclosure agreements (NDAs).

Women and equalities minister Bridget Phillipson told Sky News that there was "scope to go further" on legislation that restricted the use of such agreementsto ensure that the legal system was not being "abused in order to silence women".

"We cannot have a system where rich and powerful individuals - rich and powerful men - are able to silence women and stop things coming to light," she said.

News.title: Survivor pulled from rubble of deadly building collapse in New York
News.content:
Rescuers are searching for survivors after a three-storey building collapsed in New York City, killing two people.

At least 17 others were injured, including seven children, when the structure crumbled in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn, officials say.

Footage from the ground also shows exposed bedrooms and stairwells in an adjacent building. It is not known what caused the collapse.

News.title: Cold health alerts begin as surge of Arctic air sees temperatures plummet
News.content:
Northerly winds are sweeping across the UK, bringing cold air from the Arctic and some of the most widespread low temperatures of the autumn so far.

Thursday afternoon's highs will remain in single digits for most whilst overnight lows will widely fall below freezing, potentially dropping to -7C.

Strong winds will bring a significant wind chill, especially on northern and eastern coasts, so it will feel colder than the reading on the thermometer would suggest.

Yellow cold health alerts from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) have come into force.

Whilst the cold weather will come with sunshine in most areas, showers will also feature in northern parts of the UK, some of which could be wintry over high ground.

News.title: 'You're triggering me': How to understand your therapy-speak teen
News.content:
Mum-of-four Shannon, from New Jersey, says it took her several years to learn her approach of "I'm your parent and I'm asking you a question and you are going to answer me" was not helpful for her teenagers.

She became frustrated when they would push back - sometimes using phrases about her not respecting their boundaries.

Samuel says carefully choosing when and how you talk to your teenager can help them talk more openly, instead of hiding behind therapy speak.

Rather than asking them in a direct manner, she suggests talking about yourself being in a similar situation.

"You could bring up a subject about yourself at school or something that's related... so it isn't kind of pointing a finger at them," she says.

Shannon says: "I've noticed when I do back off they will then come to me later to say, 'Hey, guess what? I got a 95 on that Spanish test'... You don't have to ask them for three days straight about something."

Carla is glad she's open with her teenagers and feels they can discuss things with her - even if she sometimes struggles with the meaning.

"We are close and I think that's why sometimes they think that they can use these [therapy] words, as if they're talking to a friend."

If you or someone you know is experiencing mental or emotional distress, you can access support from the BBC Action Line.

News.title: Burnham's push for closer EU ties causes ripples in his party and others
News.content:
This lies behind the prime minister's decision to open the door to the argument about rejoining the EU single market - along with the freedom of movement that would bring - and even the EU altogether.

But that longer-term ambition is dividing his cabinet and his party.

Some welcome his approach, including those with formerly Brexit-backing constituencies. Angela Rayner, for example, is understood to have been pushing former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer to be bolder on Brexit since at least autumn 2022.

The housing secretary is said to have been insistent that Labour needs to stick to its manifesto red lines â not to return to the EU single market, customs union, or freedom of movement â but is open minded to changing those at the next election.

Another cabinet minister said: "The best thing you can do in politics is tell the truth. And the truth is that Brexit has been hugely damaging to Britain.

"We are not leading a public conversation here, we are racing to catch up with the public."

But others are watching nervously at a strategy one former minister described as "high risk".

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, for example, has struck a more cautious tone warning about the "costs and consequences" of rejoining the EU as well as staying out.

Jonathan Reynolds, the Business and Trade Secretary, is supportive of getting closer to the EU and discussing the UK's long term relationship.

But he has previously warned against joining the EU's customs union and is also unsure about the prospect of rejoining the EU, highlighting the uncertainty of what terms the UK would face, and what the bloc could look like in years to come with nationalist parties in the ascendancy in several European countries.

A voice from the past has a different set of concerns.

Lord Cameron told Bloomberg's Mishal Husain that starting a conversation about rejoining would be "very long and painful".

The former prime minister warned "flirting with rejoining" could also harm Burnham's attempts to renegotiate the Conservative's Brexit deal.

"If you start endlessly producing this idea that we're actually on a path to rejoining, I think you're in danger of getting a less good partnership deal because of course the EU countries will just think: 'Well, these guys are gonna rejoin anyway, so what's the point in giving them a good partnership deal'."

Attitudes in Labour towards the prime minister's approach don't divide along predictable lines. One Scottish Labour MP, personally opposed to Brexit and with a heavily Remain-voting constituency, said it was a "real problem".

"How can I argue to my constituents that we had a Scottish referendum in 2014 that settled independence for a generation. but then say the 2016 referendum isn't settled? My view is you accept democracy."

For now though, that opposition hasn't broken out into public rebellion, although Labour MP Gareth Snell is one who has warned about reopening the debate.

The MP for Stoke-on-Trent, where the Leave vote was 69.4%, told the BBC's Westminster Hour that doing so would "monopolise an awful lot of time inside parliament, inside government" when there are other things MPs should be doing.

Two Labour MPs among those most unhappy about Burnham's openness to Europe insisted "there are no plans" for any organised criticism of the prime minister.

Despite their concerns, particularly about free movement, they described their current mindset as "wait and see". That temporary truce is likely to fracture if the prime minister's lead in the polls begins to slide.

News.title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers
News.content:
Levels of the two most toxic "forever" chemicals in England's rivers have dropped by nearly a third over the last decade, according to new figures from the Environment Agency (EA).

The decline in the chemicals, PFOS and PFOA, has been put down to stricter restrictions on their use in products after increasing evidence emerged of their damaging impact on human health and the environment.

One expert studying the impact of the chemicals said it was "brilliant" to see how far the UK has come on this issue.

Thousands of other forever chemicals, known officially as PFAS, remain in use but the regulator said its report showed the need for them all to be better monitored and regulated.

PFAS were first developed in the 1930s in the US and became popular with companies making products like frying pans and firefighting foam because of their useful, oil-resistant, water-resistant and electrical properties.

They are called forever chemicals because their natural resistance means they take a very long time to break down naturally.

The earliest types of these chemicals were called PFOS and PFOA. But two decades ago researchers started to find that they were linked to tissue damage in animals and increased rates of certain serious health conditions such as testicular cancer., external

As a result, PFOS was all but banned in the UK in 2010 and PFOA in 2020.

The latest data from the regulator, published on Thursday, shows that the concentrations in English rivers of PFOS and PFOA over the last 10 years have now fallen by 30% and 29% respectively.

Levels in freshwater fish have fallen 49%.

"It's brilliant to see how far we have come in the last 10 years," said Dr David Megson, reader in environmental forensics at Manchester Metropolitan University.

News.title: Man arrested after sexual assaults at University of Huddersfield
News.content:
A 29-year-old man has been arrested after seven women reported being sexually assaulted in and around the University of Huddersfield's grounds.

West Yorkshire Police said it attended the university on Tuesday evening after being called by its security office and established all of the incidents happened between 18:00 and 18:30 GMT.

A spokesperson for the force said the women "had made off from a suspect after he approached and grabbed at them", with the held man remaining in police custody on Wednesday.

Det Insp Sarah Bradley said: "We fully recognise the distress and concern this incident has caused and can confirm a comprehensive investigation remains ongoing.

"We continue to work closely with our partners at the university to provide reassurance to students and staff and remain fully committed to supporting victims and safeguarding those who live, study and work in Huddersfield."

News.title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog
News.content:
A watchdog has launched a crackdown on misleading sunbed adverts, warning tanning firms they must not claim their beds are safe or can treat medical conditions.

The Committee for Advertising Practice (CAP) said it was issuing a UK-wide enforcement notice to "send a clear message to the industry that advertisers must not downplay the risks associated with sunbed use".

Earlier this year, the BBC identified hundreds of social media videos claiming the beds could boost energy and treat skin conditions or mental health problems.

The Sunbed Association, which represents around half of the UK's tanning salons, said it fully supported action against misleading adverts, but said businesses must still be allowed to demonstrate they operate responsibly.

The CAP, which draws up the UK's advertising rules, said some of the claims being made by companies were potentially harmful and could discourage customers from seeking appropriate medical treatment or advice.

"Sunbeds carry serious health risks, including an increased risk of skin cancer," said the CAP's compliance executive James Burnett.

"Ads shouldn't downplay those risks or present sunbed use as a way to improve health."

Cancer charities and doctors are clear about the risks of using sunbeds - and say the machines are linked to higher rates of melanoma and other skin cancers.

Using a bed before the age of 35 increases the risk of melanoma by 59% later in life, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

Young people are by far the biggest sunbed users in the UK - about one in seven 18-to-24-year-olds say they used one in the past year, double the average for all age groups, according to a 2025 YouGov survey.

Rosie Vare, health information manager at Teenage Cancer Trust, said skin cancer was one of the most common forms of the disease in young adults and she welcomed stricter enforcement of the advertising rules.

"We want young people to be properly informed about the risk of sunbed use and we recommend using trusted, regulated sources to find out information such as the NHS, external or cancer charities, external," she added.

News.title: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
News.content:
Poundland looks set to avoid immediate collapse after its US owners told MPs on Wednesday they were in favour of extending a deadline to find a rescue deal.

The discount chain, which has 11,000 employees, has been edging towards administration after being blocked by Gordon Brothers from accessing cash in its bank accounts.

A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation told the BBC they expect more time will be given thanks to the release funding in recent days.

A committee of MPs questioned Gordon Brothers following accusations that the investment firm hoped to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 shops and stock piecemeal.

Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just Â£1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock shops, and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period.

The investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claims.

But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

About Â£50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops.

The BBC understands that Gordon Brothers agreed to release a further Â£9m from Poundland's accounts, on top of Â£10m announced earlier. This will grant the company an additional 10 days to find a new buyer.

There are three bids currently on the table for Poundland, all of which have so far been rejected by the Gordon Brothers, who stand to profit from selling the company and its stock in parts.

News.title: No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister
News.content:
The education secretary told MSPs that she had held a meeting with police and local authorities.

"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," Mairi McAllan said.

"I would take this opportunity to repeat Police Scotland's advice that there is nothing to suggest any threats to the public from the content of the emails."

The cabinet secretary added there was a "considerable amount of work" ongoing by Police Scotland and partners across the UK to "understand the motivations and the individuals behind this".

Most local authorities contacted by BBC Scotland said schools were operating as normal but some confirmed pupils had been evacuated.

More than 300 calls were made to police when a similar message was sent to schools around the country on 19 October.

In many areas, pupils were off due to half-term holidays.

On Wednesday the majority of schools in Dumfries and Galloway received the email and some were evacuated as a precaution.

A spokesperson for the local authority said: "Each school community/setting is unique and as such has its own way of supporting and reassuring learners and staff.

"We also know that local police have attended some school settings in a community capacity to assist and reassure."

In Edinburgh Queensferry High School was evacuated and pupils were sent home.

Highland Council confirmed a number of its schools "made the decision to activate their emergency protocols".

Local authorities in Glasgow, Edinburgh, East Lothian, Aberdeenshire and Orkney also confirmed their schools received the message.

In Northern Ireland, the Education Authority (EA) said the "message has similarities with a bogus threat sent last month" which was treated as a hoax by the (PSNI).

The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the email originated from outside the UK.

Italian reports said 280 school head teachers had received threats in recent days. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called a meeting of top ministers and intelligence chiefs over the issue.

News.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
News.content:
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives that it alleges were involved in a string of plots in the US and Europe.

The DOJ said Iranian agents most recently "orchestrated a terrorist plot at an air force base in the United Kingdom", saying they were involved in the major incident in September near RAF Fairford in the UK, where US armed forces were stationed.

The three men have been accused by the DOJ of being involved in 18 attacks and attempted attacks, including in London, Amsterdam and Paris. Some of the incidents were said to be directed by the men over FaceTime.

The DOJ said they acted in the name of the group Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI).

Iranian Mohsen Mohajeri, Iraqi national Mohammad Ali al-Hassani and dual Iranian-Iraqi citizen Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi were charged in an indictment unsealed on Tuesday, the DOJ said.

The DOJ said that most recently, al-Hassani "orchestrated a terrorist plot" at RAF Fairford - where on 27 September a major incident was declared after suspicious vans were reported near the base.

Seven men have been arrested in the UK over the incident at RAF Fairford.

Iran has strongly denied any involvement.

Al-Hassani and Mohajeri were allegedly both in Iran at the time of the incident, the indictment claims.

Meanwhile, al-Saadi was coordinating with the pair through third parties from a prison in New York, where he is awaiting trial on previous charges after being arrested in August, it adds.

US court records show that al-Saadi is due in court on 19 November, though it is not clear whether this status conference - which is usually a routine scheduled appearance - relates to the new charges or the previous ones. The BBC has asked the Southern District of New York for comment.

News.title: Scottish DJ, 32, confirmed as victim of Krakow shooting
News.content:
Det Ch Insp David McAlinden, senior investigating officer from Police Scotland's Counter Terrorism Policing unit, said the force was "aware of the tragic death of a Scottish man in Krakow".

He added: "Working in conjunction with COPFS (the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service), Police Scotland is supporting the UK counter-terrorism policing network and the Polish authorities.

"The immediate shared priority is to ensure that identification is properly established for the family, so that repatriation can take place as quickly as possible.

"The family has asked for their privacy to be respected. Our thoughts are with them and everyone impacted by this incident."

Mark Jewell, a close friend of Campbell's who regularly DJ'd with him, described him as "a quiet, kind and soft-hearted person, who wouldn't have harmed a fly".

He added: "It's just so tragic that he had to be in the wrong place at the wrong time.

"I had been speaking with him when he was headed over to Poland and I messaged him as soon as I heard about the terrible attack, to ask if he was safe - not for one minute expecting that he would have been caught up in it all.

"I was fully expecting a funny message back from him, saying not to worry. I can't quite get my head round it all."

News.title: Jailed undertaker lodges bid to appeal against sentence
News.content:
Victims of the Legacy funeral scandal say it is an "insult" Hull undertaker Robert Bush has lodged an application to appeal against his 20-year prison sentence.

Bush, 48, admitted keeping 30 bodies after their funerals, presenting families with the ashes of strangers and selling fake funeral plans.

He pleaded guilty to 67 separate offences and was sentenced in July 2026.

Humberside Police said it had been notified by the Criminal Appeal Office at the Royal Courts of Justice and added "any decision regarding the appeal will be a matter for the courts".

In August, Bush wrote to families impacted by his crimes to express regret and said he was "deeply sorry".

Prosecutors said he ran a "shambolic and chaotic" funeral business at premises on Hessle Road in Hull and his "appalling" offending had caused "extreme emotional pain, anguish and upset".

His crimes over a 12-year period involved more than 300 victims.

News.title: Merab Dvalishvili jumped by Khabib Nurmagomedov’s cousin to spark hotel brawl
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Merab Dvalishvili was jumped by Usman Nurmagomedov to spark a brawl in an Abu Dhabi hotel, leaving the former UFC champion bloodied and bruised.

Dvalishvili was filming an interview when PFL lightweight champion Nurmagomedov, the cousin of legendary former UFC fighter Khabib, walk up to the bantamweight from behind before slapping him.

The Georgian looked stunned by the initial attack but as Nurmagomedov’s team came in with follow-up shots, a huge fight between the two fighters and their respective entourages then broke out in the hotel lobby.

Dvalishvili took to social media after the altercation to brand Russia’s Nurmagomedov and his team “snakes”, posting a video of him receiving treatment for his injuries.

He said: “What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind.

“What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way.

“You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***.”

Dvalishvili, 35, is due to wrestle at the Real American Freestyle (RAF) event in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday, taking on Brazilian Marlon Moraes.

open image in gallery Merab Dvalishvili beat Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's brother, in January 2025 ( Getty )

He previously fought and beat 28-year-old Nurmagmedov’s older brother, Umar, for the bantamweight title in an enthralling fight in early 2025, with Dvalishvili branding him “spoiled” in the build-up.

Former two-weight UFC champion Ilia Topuria, a friend of Dvalishvili who also fights out of Georgia, blasted Nurmagomedov and his attackers as he reacted to the footage of the fracas on X.

He wrote: "Usman has reportedly been detained, along with the cowards who were with him.

"What a disgrace. A bunch of absolute cowards. I always thought you were a bunch of mediocre individuals. Now you've removed every last doubt.

"Honour, respect, and humility aren't words you preach. They're values you live by. And you've shown none of them."

Middleweight champion Sean Strickland commented on Dvalishvili’s Instagram post calling for a “lifetime ban” for everyone involved, while Irish lightweight Paul Hughes - who took Nurmagomedov to his limit across two PFL title fights - lambasted his former rival and called his team out for similar behaviour in the past.

“Utterly disgusting,” Hughes wrote. “The same people assaulted my supporters in Dubai for no reason.

“How can this team ever speak about humility and respect. And yet there will be no repercussions.”

open image in gallery Usman Nurmagomedov (right) with cousin Khabib (centre) in his corner ( PFL MMA )

UFC lightweight champion and pound-for-pound kingpin Islam Makhachev, however, issued a rebuttal in defence of Nurmagomedov and suggested that a previous altercation between the two camps, before an RAF event in July, sparked Wednesday’s melee.

"Why were you silent when Merab hit a Dagestani wrestler for nothing and hurt his honor?" wrote Makhachev, who is a close friend and training partner of the Nurmagomedov family.

"Merab started what happened today in his homeland by allowing himself to hit a guest and insulting his mother."

Nurmagomedov is being heavily linked with a move to the UFC after entering free agency following his final PFL fight in the summer.

News.title: UK households urged to prepare for emergencies and ‘attacks’. Here’s what to buy
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The British public has been told to prepare for food shortages and widespread disruption from cyber attacks and emergencies under a new national initiative.

The 'Be Ready' campaign marks the beginning of a three-year drive to boost household emergency preparedness, with Defence Secretary Wes Streeting unveiling updated advice for threats such as flooding and wildfires.

UK households are advised to take simple steps in case everyday services are disrupted, like keeping a three-day supply of cash, bottled water and tinned food at home.

A new government website has also been launched with an emergency kit checklist that can be downloaded.

Mr Streeting told BBC Newsnight: "It's encouraging that people are taking practical steps to be ready.

“Having a few everyday essentials at home, from tinned food to torches, helps households prepare for disruption, whether that's flooding, power cuts or burst pipes. We can all play our part in making Britain more resilient."

open image in gallery British households are being advised to stock up on tinned food ( Getty/iStock )

The Defence Secretary previously called for a "whole society approach" to strengthen national resilience, though he insisted people should remain "alert not alarmed" regarding potential risks.

Here we look at the key items you should stock up on in case disaster strikes.

What is included in the ‘Be Ready’ checklist?

The government says people should put together an emergency kit that includes key provisions you and your household would need during a short-term incident lasting three days, such as a power failure or a disruption to your water supply.

The checklist includes:

Bottled water - enough bottled water for three days. Each person needs about 3 litres for drinking a day in addition to water needed for cooking and washing.

- enough bottled water for three days. Each person needs about 3 litres for drinking a day in addition to water needed for cooking and washing. Non-perishable food that doesn’t need cooking, such as ready-to-eat tinned meat, fruit or vegetables (and a tin opener). As with water, how much you need will vary based on your own circumstances. Don’t forget food for pets.

that doesn’t need cooking, such as ready-to-eat tinned meat, fruit or vegetables (and a tin opener). As with water, how much you need will vary based on your own circumstances. Don’t forget food for pets. Hand sanitiser and wet wipes for hygiene purposes when the water is off.

for hygiene purposes when the water is off. Light and warmth – pack a torch and spare batteries as well as blankets, sleeping bags and warm clothing

– pack a torch and spare batteries as well as blankets, sleeping bags and warm clothing A portable power bank for charging your mobile phone.

for charging your mobile phone. A battery or wind-up radio to get updates during a power cut – a car radio can be used, however in severe weather it might be safer to stay inside.

– a car radio can be used, however in severe weather it might be safer to stay inside. A first aid kit (or some first aid items) including items such as waterproof plasters, bandages, a thermometer, antiseptic, eyewash solution, sterile dressings and gloves, medical tape for dressings, and tweezers.

including items such as waterproof plasters, bandages, a thermometer, antiseptic, eyewash solution, sterile dressings and gloves, medical tape for dressings, and tweezers. Baby supplies such as nappies and baby formula – ready made or ‘ready-to-feed’ formula is best as you may not be able to boil water or sterilise bottles.

such as nappies and baby formula – ready made or ‘ready-to-feed’ formula is best as you may not be able to boil water or sterilise bottles. Money and documents – Keep cash in a mix of notes, coins and cards. Copies of IDs and documents. Also write down any important phone numbers and information such as regular medication and doses.

open image in gallery Government National Checklist ( Gov.UK )

Rather than buying all the items at once, you could just add to your emergency kit when you are able and build it up over time. You should try to store these items together in a single location in your home, ideally in a spot that remains simple to locate if the lights are off.

Maintaining a supply of prescription medication to cover several days is also essential. For those who depend on any medical devices or equipment, ensure that printed physical copies of all operating instructions are kept on hand. Furthermore, any available back-up batteries ought to be kept fully charged at all times.

How are shoppers responding to the ‘Be Ready’ campaign?

Shoppers began responding to the ‘Be Ready’ public awareness campaign from 22 October, with sales of tinned food, wind-up radios and torches all spiking since the updated government guidance was announced.

It comes as figures from Worldpanel by Numerator show supermarket prices are now 2.6 per cent higher than a year ago, an increase from 2.5 per cent in September.

Hand sanitiser sales climbed 83 per cent in the 10 days after the campaign’s launch compared with the same period last year, while bottled water sales rose 67 per cent over the same window, and tinned and jarred goods were up 37 per cent.

open image in gallery Shoppers began responding to the ‘Be Ready’ public awareness campaign from 22 October ( Getty/iStock )

The number of people buying tinned meat each day after the launch rose by 43 per cent, equivalent to an extra 400,000 shoppers a day.

Meanwhile, tinned tuna maker Princes has reported a surge in demand for products such as tinned fish, meat and vegetables as a result of Britons stockpiling essentials.

The Independent can also reveal that average ATM withdrawals hit a record £106.20 on Friday 30 October, as Britons heed the government’s advice to prepare for emergencies.

What threats is the government worried about?

Andy Burnham’s government is focusing on national resilience in the wake of threats from Russia.

Mr Streeting previously announced that Britain must be ready for war in 1,000 days, as the nation’s adversaries could be ready to attack the UK in 2030.

Writing in The Telegraph, he said: “Our adversaries’ willingness to harm us is not new. What has changed is their capacity. By 2030 their force strength and war economy could put them in a position to attack.

“That gives us a little over 1,000 days to complete our mission: to be ready with our allies to fight and win.”

Referencing the potential of Russian aggression, he added: “To prevent the worst, we have to prepare for it”.

open image in gallery Vladimir Putin’s government warned that British facilities in Ukraine will be considered ‘legitimate targets’ if they are used to support long-range strikes against Russia ( Reuters )

Explaining the ‘Be Ready’ campaign, he said: “In the face of those threats, which are not hypothetical but real, and not somewhere else but increasingly here, we have to step up and take seriously our national resilience as well as our national defence.

“It’s really important that we ask households and businesses are they prepared?”.

Vladimir Putin’s government warned that British facilities in Ukraine will be considered “legitimate targets” if they are used to support long-range strikes against Russia.

The Independent also reported that rogue drones are targeting Britain’s military bases almost daily, leaving the UK vulnerable to growing threats from Russia and Iran.

Some 340 security incidents involving drones were reported at or near Ministry of Defence sites in the year to August 2026, data obtained under freedom of information laws show. In 2025, there were a total of 250 incidents recorded – double the 126 recorded the year before.

Why are heatwaves a concern?

The government is also worried following the record-breaking heatwaves the UK experienced this summer, plunging the country into drought and causing numerous wildfires.

Analysts have warned extreme heat and ongoing droughts are putting Britain at risk of its “worst food security crisis in decades”.

open image in gallery The government also plans to advise people on how to deal with the impacts of extreme weather ( Getty )

Meanwhile, Shore Capital analysts previously said the knock-on impact of five back-to-back heatwaves and prolonged dry conditions could destroy farmers’ harvests, leading to food shortages later this year and increasing reliance on foreign imports.

The National Farmers Union (NFU) also warned the situation is “increasingly concerning” and that dairy farmers were already using winter feed because grass had stopped growing.

News.title: Russell Brand allegations to be explored in new Netflix documentary Open Secret
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Netflix is set to look at Russell Brand’s crimes in a new documentary following the comedian’s convictions for rape and sexual assault.

Russell Brand: Open Secret will chart Brand’s career – “from comedian and film star to political activist and YouTuber known for spouting conspiracies theories” – which culminated in him being sentenced to 10 and a half years in prison following a high-profile criminal trial.

The documentary – which is released on Friday (13 November) – is from the producers of Jimmy Savile: A British Horror Story and will feature interviews with insiders who share insight into Brand’s life.

Russell Brand: Open Secret also interviews Rosamund Urwin and Charlote Wace, who broke the story around his allegations in The Times and The Sunday Times in 2023.

open image in gallery 'Russell Brand: Open Secret' will be released on Friday ( Netflix )

It follows backlash recently faced by Netflix after the streamer chose to keep Brand’s 2018 stand-up special on its platform despite the comedian’s guilty verdicts.

Russell Brand: Re: Birth, recorded at London's Hackney Empire, will no longer be actively promoted or recommended to subscribers, but viewers will still be able to access it.

A Netflix source told The Telegraph and other outlets: “We prioritise choice and control for our members: the freedom to watch what, how and when you want, with recommendations and ratings to inform those choices.”

On Thursday 5 November, Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault against four victims between 2004 and 2009. He was sentenced to 10 year sand six months in prison on Monday 9 November.

open image in gallery Russell Brand during his trial ( Getty )

He is expected to serve two-thirds of his prison sentence before being released on licence, and will be on the sex offenders’ register for life.

The judge said Brand’s celebrity status had protected him until a 2023 exposé by Channel 4’s Dispatches, The Times and The Sunday Times “empowered” other women to come forward.

Sending him to the cells, the judge added: “Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and demand justice in the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Mr Brand, act without their consent.”

The Metropolitan Police is also investigating Brand over two more alleged rapes, including against a 16-year-old schoolgirl, and charging files are being considered by the Crown Prosecution Service.

“If you come forward, you will be listened to, supported and treated with care and compassion,” Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy said.

Russell Brand: Open Secret arrives on Netflix on Friday.

News.title: Sky refuses to release David Walliams film following allegations against comedian
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

David Walliams’s new movie has been dropped by Sky following “extremely serious” allegations made against the writer and actor.

The development comes after producers said just yesterday that Walliams’s cameo in the movie had been cut and he would not have any involvement in the film’s release or promotion.

The best-selling author and former Britain’s Got Talent judge, 55, was named as part of an investigation by The Guardian and ITV News on Tuesday, after he tried to obtain an injunction to prevent the reporting of allegations against him.

One woman described her alleged encounter with Walliams, when she was 15, as a “sexual assault”, while multiple women accused him of “grooming” them when they were teenagers.

Walliams denies any wrongdoing.

open image in gallery Walliams is known for his children’s books as well as his career in comedy and television ( Getty )

open image in gallery ‘Fing!’ (right) was the latest of Walliams’s children’s books to be adapted to film ( Reuters )

Several of his children’s books have been adapted into films, including Fing!, which was published in 2019.

A movie based on the book was due to be distributed by Sky across the UK and Ireland in early 2027; however, it has now been dumped.

In a statement shared with the Press Association, a Sky spokesperson said: “The allegations made against David Walliams are extremely serious. We have notified the producers of the film of our intention to exit our position as the UK and Ireland licensee of Fing!.

“We have already removed content which features him from our platforms.”

Directed by Jeffrey Walker and filmed in Australia, some of the film’s stars include Taika Waititi, Blake Harrison and Mia Wasikowska, while Matt Lucas provided the voice of the titular character.

Angel Studios confirmed it will still release the film in the US, but a cameo featuring Walliams will be removed and he will not take part in its promotion.

In a statement to Variety, Angel Studios said: “We take the allegations reported regarding David Walliams seriously.

“Our thoughts are with anyone who has been affected. We have removed his cameo appearance from Fing!, and he will have no involvement in the film’s release or promotion.”

Fing! will also retain its January 14 release date in Australia, but local distributor Transmission Films confirmed to ABC that Walliams will not participate in the publicity campaign.

Local streaming service Stan was set to make the film available on its platform, but told ABC: “In light of the recent and serious allegations against David Walliams, Stan has removed Fing! from its content slate.”

Since Walliams was named in the ITV News and The Guardian investigation, he has been dropped by his literary agent, while the BBC said it was “in the process of removing” programmes including Little Britain.

In a letter understood to have been sent several months ago by Walliams to journalists working on the ITV News and Guardian investigations, he wrote: “Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

“I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.

“And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.”

He added: “I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

Walliams has yet to respond following the publication of his name on Tuesday.

News.title: More heavyweight fights added to Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The main card for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua has been confirmed, and it will seemingly consist solely of heavyweight bouts.

On 11 December, Fury and Joshua will finally square off in the biggest British fight of a generation, headlining at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium and live on Netflix.

Last week brought the news that the chief-support bout will pit Deontay Wilder, one of Fury’s former rivals, against Jai Opetaia, and two more fights have now been added.

open image in gallery Martin Bakole during his draw with Efe Ajagba in May ( Getty )

Martin Bakole will take on Solomon Adebayo, and Da’Mazion Vanhouter will box Michael Essomba.

Bakole (21-2-1, 16 KOs) has roots in the Democratic Republic of Congo but fights out of Scotland, and he has long talked up his success against the division’s best fighters in sparring.

However, his hype took a hit in February 2025, when he fought Joseph Parker on short notice and was knocked out in round two. In his only fight since, three months later, he drew with Efe Ajagba.

Meanwhile, Adebayo is an unbeaten Nigerian prospect who is 15-0 with 14 KOs, and he is due to compete against Ivan Magumba in Nairobi on 28 November – although that fight could be cancelled in light of the news that he will box in Cardiff.

Vanhouter is similarly undefeated at 14-0 (11 KOs) and, at 21 years old, the American is the youngest fighter on the main card. He takes on 34-year-old Belgian boxer Essomba, whose professional record stands at 11-2 (10 KOs).

The most appetising fight on the undercard, however, is surely Wilder vs Opetaia. The latter, a recent cruiserweight champion, will make his divisional debut against Wilder, a former heavyweight champion.

open image in gallery Deontay Wilder (centre) won a 12-round brawl with Derek Chisora in April ( Getty )

Australia’s Opetaia, 31, is unbeaten, while Wilder, 41, was undefeated until his KOs by Fury in 2020 and 2021. Those losses followed the American’s controversial draw with Fury in 2018.

Wilder has since lost twice more, but he will enter his bout with Opetaia on the back of a points win over Derek Chisora, whom he beat in a slugfest in April.

News.title: Two men set to be executed in Texas and Oklahoma today over child beheadings and a deadly affair plot
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The U.S. was preparing to carry out two executions on Thursday, one in Oklahoma and one in Texas.

In Texas, the condemned man is John Allen Rubio, 46, who was set to be put to death at the state prison in Huntsville. He was convicted of beheading three young children he was raising in a 2003 killing that rattled a community along the U.S.-Mexico border. The other man facing execution is James Pavatt, 73, who was set to die by lethal injection at Oklahoma's state penitentiary in McAlester.

His crime was the fatal shooting of the estranged husband of a woman with whom he was having an affair. Prosecutors say he carried out the killing with her, and she is currently the state's only woman on death row. The two executions come as the U.S. is on track to surpass 40 executions for a second consecutive year, a pace driven by Florida.

The death penalty is under renewed attention.

open image in gallery This photo, provided by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice, shows John Allen Rubio ( Texas Department of Criminal Justice )

Last week, California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced he would commute hundreds of death sentences before leaving office, which experts say would be the largest mass clemency in American history.

Rubio and his girlfriend, Angela Camacho, were accused in the killings of 3-year-old Julissa Quesada, 14-month-old John E. Rubio, and 2-month-old Mary Jane Rubio. The children died in the squalid, windowless apartment the couple shared in Brownsville, located on Texas' border with Mexico.

Camacho pleaded guilty and is serving a life sentence. Rubio's first capital murder conviction in the killings was overturned by an appeals court, which ruled that statements by Camacho were wrongly allowed as evidence in his trial.

Rubio again pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity for his second trial, but he was once again convicted and sentenced to death.

open image in gallery This photo provided by the Oklahoma Department of Corrections shows James Pavatt ( AP )

Rubio, according to court records, wasn't the biological father of the two older children but treated them as if they were his own. At various points, Rubio claimed the children were possessed and that he was the “chosen one” intended to save the world. Defense experts diagnosed Rubio as suffering from paranoid schizophrenia, a determination rejected by prosecution experts.

Those testified that his childhood – filled with violence at home, “toxic” parents, drug use, and prostitution – damaged him developmentally. The apartment building where the children were killed was later demolished and the land was turned into a park and a community garden.

Pavatt was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder in the 2001 death of Rob Andrew, a 39-year-old advertising executive. Andrew was fatally shot in the garage of the Oklahoma City home he'd previously shared with his wife as he picked up their two young children before Thanksgiving.

Pavatt, who attended the same church as the Andrew family, had been having an affair with Andrew's wife, Brenda Andrew. They were convicted at separate trials and each was sentenced to death. Weeks before the shooting, Rob Andrew had told police someone was trying to kill him after the brake lines on his car were cut.

open image in gallery Last week, California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced he would commute hundreds of death sentences before leaving office, which experts say would be the largest mass clemency in American history ( AFP/Getty )

Brenda Andrew told police after her husband was killed that masked intruders shot her in the arm and fatally shot him.

Pavatt and Brenda Andrew went to Mexico with her two children after the shooting and were arrested three months later while reentering the U.S.

At a clemency hearing last month, Pavatt said he was “not guilty of shooting anyone,” and that he'd fallen in love with Brenda Andrew and believed “everything she told me.”

“It was not until my trial that I began to see the extent to which I had been manipulated by Brenda,” Pavatt told the board. “I can see why the jury believed that we were both involved in Rob’s murder.”

Prosecutors have said that Pavatt and Andrew plotted to kill Rob Andrew, and that no matter who fired the shots, both were equally guilty.

News.title: Edinburgh City Bypass closed in both directions following serious crash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A major route near Edinburgh is currently closed in both directions following a crash.

Emergency services responded to a collision on the A720 Edinburgh City Bypass between Dreghorn junction and Hermiston Gait at around 8.55pm on Wednesday, 11 November. Police officers closed the route in both directions soon after arriving at the scene.

Transport Scotland confirmed the road remains shut this morning as “investigation works continue,” with drivers warned to avoid the City Bypass. Diversion routes have been set for motorists around the road closure.

A spokesperson for Police Scotland said: "Emergency services remain in attendance following a crash on the A720 Edinburgh City Bypass near Clovenstone, which was reported to police around 8.55pm on Wednesday, 11 November, 2026.

“The road is closed in both directions between Dreghorn junction and Hermiston Gait and is expected to remain closed for a number of hours.

“Motorists are advised to continue to use alternative routes."

In an update on Thursday morning, Edinburgh Travel News confirmed the route remains closed and was causing “lengthy” traffic delays and congestion.

open image in gallery Building traffic on the A720 Edinburgh Bypass following a crash ( Transport Scotland )

Edinburgh Travel News shared on social media: "Lengthy traffic delays across much of west/south west Edinburgh this morning - the City Bypass remains closed both ways between Dreghorn and Hermiston Gait following an incident last night."

In an update at 9am, traffic monitoring service Inrix states: “A720 Edinburgh City Bypass in both directions closed severe delays, queueing traffic due to police incident from M8 J1 (Hermiston Gait, Hermiston) to Dreghorn Link (Dreghorn Junction, Oxgangs).

“Congestion to the M8 J3 (Livingston). Causing long queues on routes towards the city centre including the A80 through Cramond, the Lanark Road and Calder Road past the University.”

What is the A720 diversion route?

Transport Scotland has told motorists to avoid the area and follow these diversion routes:

Westbound Direction: Closure of A720 at Dreghorn Junction westbound off and on slips, leave taking slip to Dreghorn Link, turn right to roundabout at Services/Swanston Muir continue straight across.

Travel on Dreghorn Link to roundabout with Redford Road, turn left and travel on Redford Road to junction with Colinton Road.

Turn left and travel on Colinton Road, Bridge Road and Gillespie Road to junction with Gillespie Crossroads continuing straight across into Wester Hailes Road.

Travel to Clovenstone Roundabout continuing straight across to traffic lights at junction with Murrayburn Road, straight across and travel to Bankhead Roundabout turning left on Calder Road.

Travel to Calder Junction turn right and travel on the on-slip for the M8 and north to Gogar Roundabout.

Eastbound Direction: Closure of A720 eastbound at the off-slip for Hermiston Gait/A71 Calder Road, the eastbound on-slip from Calder Roundabout and the on-slip from Hermiston Gait roundabout to A720, take eastbound slip for A71 to Calders Roundabout (also available from Hermiston Gait).

Turn left onto Calder Road, following westbound diversion, in reverse order.

News.title: England legend Jimmy Anderson set to continue career after signing for Surrey
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Sir James Anderson is set to continue his cricket career and will join Surrey for the 2027 season of the Rothesay County Championship.

Anderson’s career had been in doubt after Lancashire County Cricket Club decided not to offer the 44-year-old a new contract for next year following a change of leadership behind the scenes.

Anderson captained Lancashire this past season as the club slumped to second bottom place in division two of the County Championship despite England’s greatest ever bowler claiming an impressive 50 wickets across 11 matches at an average of 17.68.

His output shows that there has been little diminishment in his skills as time has gone on and Surrey hope to capitalise on his experience and class by offering him a career lifeline.

Anderson made his Test Match debut in 2003, alongside Surrey’s Director of Cricket Alec Stewart, and took 911 international wickets over a 21-year career at the top of the game. Those include 704 Test Match wickets, the most of any Englishman and any fast-bowler in the history of cricket.

Speaking of his switch to Surrey, Anderson said: “It’s an honour to join a club like Surrey and I can’t wait to start a new chapter in my career. Surrey have a great squad and are a team that expects to be fighting for Championship titles and I’m excited to be a part of that.

“I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games of cricket. I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country.”

“I’ve always loved playing at the Kia Oval. For me it’s one of the best grounds in the world. It’s a place that I have some incredibly special memories at and I hope to create some more next season.”

open image in gallery Jimmy Anderson took 50 wickets for Lancashire in the 2026 County Championship Division Two ( Getty )

“Jimmy also brings a wealth of experience to the group that all our bowlers will learn from. Much of our squad have international aspirations, and they will learn a great deal from training, playing and being in the same dressing room with Jimmy.

News.title: Ebola could be raging in DRC for another year, expert warns
News.content:
The Ebola epidemic currently raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo could last at least another year, a leading UK epidemiologist has warned.

Experts have struggled to contain the current outbreak since the first cases of the rare Bundibugyo strain of the disease were reported in May.

There have so far been almost 11,000 cases including 5,000 deaths, making it the second largest outbreak in history, after the devastating West Africa epidemic of 2014-16. Cases have also been reported in Nigeria and Kenya, although transmission has not been widespread.

The outbreak is taking place across a vast area of DRC - North Kivu and Ituri - where conflict and widespread mistrust of authorities, including health workers, have hampered the response.

Neil Ferguson, professor of epidemiology at Imperial College, London, told a press briefing that at the current rate of disease spread that the epidemic could still be ongoing at the end of next year.

“Controlling Ebola outbreaks takes a long time so it is highly likely we’ll still be seeing transmission in a year’s time,” he said.

“We’re ticking over at about 70 confirmed cases a day at the moment and that’s almost certainly quite a significant underestimate of the true number of infections,” said Prof Ferguson, who rose to prominence at the beginning of the Covid pandemic when he advised government on the likely trajectory of the outbreak.

News.title: Many more cattle ranch workers infected with H5N1 than reported, says US farming union
News.content:
Far more US farm workers are infected with bird flu than officially reported, with some suffering “very severe” symptoms, according to the country’s largest farming union.

H5N1 is currently spreading rapidly across US cattle farms in dozens of US states.

Officially, just three people have been diagnosed with the virus in the past month, all following close contact with infected cows.

In total, 73 people in the US have been officially been recorded as infected with H5N1 since 2024, mostly dairy farm workers. Three have died.

But United Farm Unions (UFU), which represents thousands of workers across the US, said it was aware of many more farmers experiencing symptoms consistent with H5N1 who had not been tested.

“We have now connected with a number of workers and have confirmed that more workers are sick with avian flu symptoms who have not been tested,” the UFU wrote on X.

Symptoms range from “very mild to very severe”, the post added, including mild upper respiratory infections and conjunctivitis to severe flu-like symptoms, bone pain, persistent coughing and high fever.

The ongoing outbreak is worrying disease experts.

“H5N1 is not a virus to be casual about- or to let spread unchecked, given every mutation is like the virus buying a lottery ticket to acquire human-to-human transmission,” said Dr Devi Sridhar, a public health researcher at the University of Edinburgh.

Referring to the statement by the UFU, Professor Francois Balloux, director of the UCL Genetics Institute, added: “The most puzzling aspect to me is not even the incompetence and paralysis of the authorities but the resignation and fatalism. It feels like reading some chronicle by a mediaeval peasant.”

Of the roughly 1,000 people infected with H5N1 since the virus was first identified in the late 1990s, almost half have died. However, most historical cases have resulted from contact with wild birds, while the strain circulating in cattle, known as genotype B.12, is thought to cause much milder illness.

Concerns have nevertheless grown after an unidentified farm worker in Washington state died in late October from the cattle-derived H5N1 strain, raising questions about whether the virus may have mutated.

The Trump administration has been heavily criticised for allowing bird flu to run rampant through America’s wild and domestic animals, putting people at risk.

Deep cuts to the federal agencies responsible for managing human and animal health, the US Centers for Disease Control (CDC) and the Department of Agriculture (USDA), have resulted in the scaling down of surveillance and testing programmes amongst both livestock and farm workers.

Every infection, animal or human, raises the chance the virus could mutate and eventually gain the ability to spread between people – something which experts have long warned could trigger the next pandemic.

As flu season begins, experts are concerned a dairy worker infected with ordinary seasonal flu could catch H5N1 at the same time, and the two viruses could mix to create a new, more dangerous strain that could spread between people – a phenomenon known as “reassortment.”

“It is clear that workers are not being informed of the risks of handling sick cattle and infected milk. They are being given no information on flu shots or avian flu testing,” the UFU said.

Estimates suggest that over half of the 150,000-strong dairy workforce in the US are immigrant or undocumented workers, driven in part by high demand for intensive year-round labour and a lack of domestic applicants.

Many are reportedly worried about coming forward for testing over fears they will come into contact with US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the federal agency emboldened under Trump, which has been tasked with deporting one million immigrants every year.

Yakima Valley, the region of Washington State where the three recent H5N1 cases have been reported and where the virus is spreading through dozens of dairy herds, is in the midst of an ICE crackdown.

News.title: Young women must ensure they are vaccinated as measles cases surge, doctors say
News.content:
But the dangers for pregnant women, say experts, are often ignored.

There has been relatively little data on maternal and infant measles deaths related to pregnancy in the West since the late 1960s, after the MMR vaccine was introduced and case numbers fell significantly.

Pregnant women are known, however, to be much more vulnerable to illness from measles than others, as the mother’s body, to stop it from rejecting the pregnancy, shifts its immune response significantly and becomes more susceptible to disease.

Between 2000 and 2025, 36 children and adults died from measles or related infections in England and Wales, according to NHS data, but whether or not any of those people were pregnant has not been made public.

“Given the recurrence of measles outbreaks and the number of cases occurring in adults, there may be value in better understanding the impact of measles infection during pregnancy in the UK,” Kirsty Le Doare, professor of vaccinology and immunology at City St George’s, told The Telegraph.

One study by the US CDC conducted in Namibia looked at 55 unvaccinated women who contracted measles during their pregnancies.

Of them, 53 required hospitalisation for complications arising from the virus, ranging from severe diarrhoea, pneumonia, and encephalitis (swelling of the brain).

Another meta-analysis, published in The Lancet in 2018, analysed data from 19 academic papers from countries including France, Germany, and the UK that had studied pregnancy-related measles between 1941 and 2012.

Of 420 pregnancy-related measles cases, 18 deaths occurred, mostly from pneumonia.

“Measles in pregnancy is serious and can cause stillbirth, premature labour and miscarriage,” the NHS website reads. “There is no medical treatment for measles; MMR vaccination is the best protection against becoming seriously unwell,” it adds.

“We know that if you catch measles during pregnancy, you are very likely to end up in hospital,” Professor Helen Bedford, a professor of children’s health at Great Ormond Street Hospital, told The Telegraph.

“You are much more likely to have pneumonia, and there are higher rates of encephalitis. These are all complications that can happen in adults with measles, but they do seem to occur at much higher rates during pregnancy,” said Prof Bedford.

News.title: Gaza floods are an “immediate humanitarian emergency”, warns Trump’s Board of Peace
News.content:
Donald Trump’s Board of Peace has accused Israel of an “insufficient” response to deadly floods that have hit the Gaza Strip.

In a rare statement, the US-led body, charged with ending war in Gaza and rebuilding the Strip, called on Israel “to act immediately to authorise and facilitate the entry of all necessary winterisation and humanitarian supplies”.

“The situation no longer represents simply a threat posed by the approaching winter, but an immediate humanitarian emergency,” they said on Monday.

The Board has been pushing Israel for at least a month to speed up its “winterisation” policies so that residents in Gaza are better able to withstand the coldest months of the year.

The statement followed a weekend of torrential rain and winds that battered the decimated territory’s displacement camps, causing widespread flooding, landslides and several deaths.

A mother and her three young children were killed when a sand dune collapsed onto their tent in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. The children, aged four, five and eight died on Sunday. Their mother also suffocated under the sand.

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.
