Sports.title: £75m-rated Chelsea star could spark Man United vs Man City transfer tug of war
Sports.content:
£75m-rated Chelsea star could spark Man United vs Man City transfer tug of war

Manchester United and Manchester City are both keeping tabs on Malo Gusto, talkSPORT understands.

The Chelsea defender has seen his role reduced since Xabi Alonso's arrival at Stamford Bridge, leading him to be linked with an exit.

4 Malo Gusto has not been a regular starter for Chelsea this season Credit: Getty

Gusto has not started a Premier League match since September 12 and has increasingly lost his place to Josh Acheampong at right-back, despite captain Reece James being injured.

Two-horse race?

Two of Chelsea's rivals could now be set to pounce, with both City and United understood to be interested in Gusto.

It is not currently clear whether either side will make an official approach in the January transfer window.

Man City were previously linked with a move for Gusto in the summer, who were keen for a reunion between the 23-year-old and former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca.

talkSPORT understands Chelsea value the Frenchman at £75million, however their efforts to sign him could be affected by other matters.

City are still awaiting the outcome of their appeal against the Premier League following their guilty verdict on 114 charges of breaching financial rules.

The Premier League giants were adjudged to have artificially inflated their revenue by £900million via 'sham' contracts over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

While City have since launched an appeal, they are yet to learn the outcome of this, and their pending sanctions hearing will complicate any pursuit of Gusto.

Man United also find themselves at a crossroads amid their interest in the full-back.

The Red Devils look poised for a change in management, with a deal agreed in principle for USA boss Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

4 Gusto made 49 appearances in all competitions for Chelsea in the 2025/26 season Credit: Getty

4 Maresca previously managed Gusto between 2024 and 2026 at Chelsea Credit: Getty

Gusto's Chelsea career so far

Gusto joined Chelsea in 2023 from Lyon for around £26m.

He has been a regular fixture in the team ever since, making 144 appearances and scoring three goals in all competitions.

However, this season he has slipped down the pecking order under new manager Alonso, starting just three of his seven Premier League appearances this term.

Other than this, Gusto started all three of the Blues' Carabao Cup fixtures, before their fourth-round exit to Liverpool on penalties.

His performance in the defeat did little to help his case for more minutes, with concerns being raised over him.

Gusto was the target of plenty of Chelsea fan ire as he was booed off when he was replaced in the 67th minute, and talkSPORT's Adrian Durham and Andy Townsend both weighed in on this.

4 Gusto's theatrics in Chelsea's Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool left talkSPORT's Townsend unimpressed Credit: Getty

Durham said: “There were cheers from the Chelsea fans at Anfield when he was taken off. He was awful.

“One Chelsea fan messaged me saying I don't want to see him in a Chelsea shirt again.

“Players go through this, but it feels like it could be the end of the road. He was actually linked with Man City in the summer, and they're talking about him going Man City in January.

“I don't really understand what City see, but I'm being a very harsh critic of a footballer here.”

Townsend, meanwhile, accused Gusto of going 'a little soft', criticising for him going to ground easily and playing for free-kicks.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel reveals double injury blow on eve of England clash
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has confirmed England will be without both Djed Spence and Ezri Konsa against Croatia.

The Three Lions return to action on Thursday at Wembley, with kick-off at 7:45pm, live on talkSPORT.

4 Tuchel has confirmed Spence and Konsa will miss the match against Croatia Credit: Getty

However, they have been dealt an early blow in defence, with two potential starters in Spence and Konsa ruled out.

Konsa has been managing his fitness after suffering a knee issue during Arsenal’s 2-1 win away to Slavia Prague.

The 29-year-old then played the full 90 minutes in a 1-0 victory over Hull three days later, but has been following an individual training programme since linking up with England.

While Spence has no clear injury, the full-back struggled for fitness following his £30million move to Inter Milan and has only recently began to star regularly, making it likely he is still getting up to speed.

Despite being without the two for the Croatia clash, Tuchel revealed both players could return against Spain on Sunday.

Tuchel: Not risking Konsa and Spence

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Tuchel explained: "It’s my understanding at the moment that they will both be available (for Spain).

"But we will not take the risk tomorrow (vs Croatia), they are out tomorrow.

"The hope and belief is they are in individual training on Friday, team training on Saturday and available on Sunday."

With Konsa's absence for the Croatia clash becoming clear on Tuesday, Tuchel moved quickly to bring in cover.

Uncapped Bournemouth defender James Hill received his first England call-up, having previously been on the 55-man shortlist.

4 Konsa has been a virtual ever-present for Arsenal this term, making 15 appearances in all competitions Credit: Getty

4 Spence has two assists in seven games for Inter Milan this term Credit: Getty

Konsa and Spence's absences aren't the only defensive headache Tuchel has faced in the international break.

Manchester City’s Marc Guehi pulled out of the squad through injury leading to Dan Burn’s late inclusion.

Fortunately though, Jarrad Branthwaite, Jarell Quansah and Ben White are all available and capable of playing at centre-back.

Tuchel will certainly be hoping both Konsa and Spence are ultimately fit for the Croatia clash, particularly with the latter heading into the international break in fine form.

After establishing himself at Inter Milan following a fitness-affected start to life, Spence has earned rave reviews with his recent displays.

The full-back completed his third straight 90 minutes on Sunday in a 2-0 victory over Cesc Fabregas' in form Como side.

4 Spence will have to wait slightly longer for his first England appearance since this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty

As well as keeping a clean sheet, his impact going forward was hailed after he provided his second assist in as many games in the win.

Spence's impact in Italy has drawn widespread praise, with Premier League icon Paolo Di Canio going as far to claim he can play 'blindfolded'

Sports.title: Michael Beale resigns from management role after just 12 games in charge
Sports.content:
Michael Beale resigns from management role after just 12 games in charge

Michael Beale has resigned as head coach of Zulte Waregem after just six months in charge, talkSPORT understands.

The ex-Rangers boss penned a two-year deal with the Belgian side in May - his first managerial role since he was sacked by Sunderland in February 2024.

4 Beale has left his position at Zulte Waregem after a nightmare run of form Credit: Getty

However, Beale's return to the dugout has quickly turned into a nightmare, as he departs with his side on a six-match losing run.

The Englishman's final game in charge saw his side get thumped 4-1 by Sint-Truidense on Saturday, leaving them just four points clear of the Belgian Pro League relegation zone.

Beale leaves his post

Beale's resignation comes after a breakdown in relations with senior figures at the club.

The former EFL boss had previously received a vote of confidence, but talkSPORT understands he has now decided to walk away from the role.

During discussions over a number of weeks, Beale's decision follows a misalignment with leadership over the long-term vision of the club.

It is understood he had concerns around the club’s decision-making, particularly due to a lack of consultation and involvement in recruitment.

Beale walks despite public backing

In his brief spell in Belgium, Beale took charge of 12 games, winning just four times, drawing twice and losing on six occasions.

Pressure had begun to mount on the 46-year-old in late October after his Zulte Waregem side suffered a fourth straight defeat to strugglers La Louviere - who have since sacked Ed Still as manager.

Despite the poor run of form, sporting director Niels Leroy publicly backed Beale, and insisted his job was not under threat.

He said: “Michael Beale is not under pressure right now.

4 Beale's time in Belgium never quite got going, as he lost more games than he won Credit: AFP

4 The Englishman leaves with Zulte Waregem sitting 14th out of 17 in the Belgian Pro League Credit: AFP

“We are confident that we can turn things around and pick up points in the upcoming games.

“But even if we were to lose three more games in a row, that wouldn’t automatically mean we’re going to fire Michael.

“At this club, we always consider the bigger picture. And we have a philosophy here that we don’t part ways with a coach lightly.

“As long as our analysis of a situation gives us sufficient reasons for hope, there is no reason to dismiss a coach.”

Despite this, Beale has made the decision to walk away after finding himself on a different page to club officials.

His appointment at Zulte Waregem marked the first time the 46-year-old had managed outside of the UK.

4 Beale has struggled at both Sunderland and Zulte Waregem after a promising start to management with QPR and Rangers Credit: Getty

He started out at Championship side QPR in June 2022 and oversaw an impressive run of eight wins in 11 games that had the west London side at the top of the table.

However, QPR's form nosedived with four losses in five games after Wolves unsuccessfully attempted to poach Beale from Loftus Road.

But there was nothing QPR could do to stop Beale from moving north to Scottish giants Rangers in November 2022.

Under Beale, Rangers finished the 2022/23 Scottish Premiership in second with 93 points, the largest runners-up total in league history.

Despite a bright start in Glasgow, a run of three losses in seven games in his second season at Ibrox brought the end of his tenure.

Beale was only out of work briefly though as Sunderland chose to roll the dice on him just over two months later, only for his reign to last only 12 games before he was sacked.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola eyed for new manager’s job in dramatic swoop
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola eyed for new manager’s job in dramatic swoop

US Soccer want Pep Guardiola to replace Mauricio Pochettino as the men's national team head coach, talkSPORT understands.

Pochettino looks set to leave for Premier League giants Manchester United having agreed a deal in principle to replace Michael Carrick.

2 Guardiola could be on his way back into management as the United States eye a replacement for Pochettino Credit: AFP

Those overseeing the managerial change in the United States set-up want to hire Guardiola in what would be a sensational appointment.

The Spaniard has been out of management since the summer when he left Manchester City after a decade at the club.

Guardiola won six Premier League titles and the Champions League, and is regarded as one of the best managers in history.

He also lifted three consecutive league trophies with Barcelona and Bayern Munich.

Joining the USMNT would present a fresh challenge as Guardiola has never managed at international level.

However, it won't be as straightforward for the powers that be as he hinted before his City exit that he would take a break from football.

Could Guardiola join USMNT?

"After my contract with City, I'm going to stop. I'm sure," he said in May 2025.

"I don't know if I'm going to retire, but I'm going to take a break. How I want to be remembered, I don't know."

In a separate interview, he reiterated: "So I'm not retiring, but I will take a break, for sure."

"When I finish here, I will take a break. I need to make a stop, that's all," Guardiola added.

2 Guardiola is one of the most successful managers in history and would be a remarkable appointment for the United States Credit: Getty

Despite leaving the club, Guardiola has maintained support for City in recent months.

He sent an emotional message to fans after City were found guilty on all charges of Premier League financial breaches in September.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all," the 55-year-old said.

Guardiola then attended their Champions League league phase clash at home to holders Paris Saint-Germain last month.

However, he watched his former side lose 4-2 in what was their worst home defeat in the competition ever.

Should Guardiola take the USMNT job, he could be on the touchline in time for the Gold Cup next summer.

Sports.title: Harry Kane confirms 2030 World Cup plans and doesn’t rule out future Premier League return
Sports.content:
Harry Kane hasn't got retirement on his mind as he revealed his intention to play at the next World Cup in just under four years time.

The England captain and Ballon d'Or winner joined talkSPORT Drive for an exclusive interview, and he was asked a variety of questions by Andy Goldstein and Darren Bent in a brilliant, wide-ranging chat.

5 Kane was in good spirits ahead of appearing for the 126th time for England against Croatia Credit: talkSPORT

He recently put pen to paper on a new contract with Bayern Munich that lasts until the summer of 2029.

Kane said he doesn't believe this will be the final contract of his football career, although he doesn't have any intention of cutting short his agreement with his current club.

The England legend is very happy in Germany, but once that deal expires, he's not sure what will happen.

One thing he is determined to make happen is the 2030 World Cup.

We saw in the 2026 World Cup that Lionel Messi, Luka Modric and Cristiano Ronaldo all took part despite being in their late 30s or early 40s.

And Kane is targeting involvement in the tournament that is set to be hosted in Spain, Morocco and Portugal, saying: "I hope to still be around by then. I'd be 35 nearly 36, but I think that is pretty young, to be honest.

"There are examples of players playing well into their 30s at the highest level, and as long as I am performing and I deserve my place in the team, then I'll be here.

"If I am scoring 50, 60, 70 goals a season for my club, there is no reason why I won't be here to help the national team.

"My biggest dream is to win a major trophy with England. There are some great things I have achieved throughout my career, but there are many more that I want to win.

"I think it is fairly realistic that I'll still be here for the World Cup in four years, but as we know, we have the home Euros, and that is where the focus lies."

5 Kane was named the best player in the world in October after a stellar 2025/26 season for Bayern Munich Credit: Getty

5 Kane is England's record goalscorer and now a Bayern fans' favourite Credit: Getty

Premier League return for Kane?

After spending his entire career in England, Kane took the bold plunge to abandon Tottenham and join Bayern Munich in a £100m deal.

That happened in 2023, and though the Champions League has evaded him thus far, the move has been a huge success.

He has won the Ballon d'Or and two Bundesliga titles and has scored over 150 goals already.

Kane is loved at the club and by their fans, while his family are settled in Bavaria.

When asked about a potential Premier League return, he said: "I'll be honest, I am really not sure.

"When I think back coming back, it isn't just about the record (top goalscorer in the Premier League), there are things I haven't achieved yet.

5 A few of the questions threw Kane off, but he handled them well Credit: talksport

"But since I've been away, it has really opened my eyes that there is a big old world out there, and I think people are appreciating my game more.

"So, I think it would have to be a perfect situation for me to ever come back, and I can't see where that would be."

Goldstein pressed if that meant it was still possible, he said: "One day, anything is possible."

Right at the end of the interview, Goldstein tried one more question about Kane returning to the Premier League, asking him if he'd re-join Tottenham or another top-flight club.

It left Kane shaking his head before he said: "All the tough questions at the end before I go.

"Who knows, I can't tell you. Time will tell."

5 Kane is a club legend at Tottenham and fans would be desperate to have him back Credit: Getty

Record breaker again

Kane will start England's Nations League game on Thursday night against Croatia, live on talkSPORT.

And ahead of that match, Kane has been speaking about breaking Peter Shilton's record.

This game will be Kane's 126th cap, and in a pre-match press conference, he said: "It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement).

"I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino should TURN DOWN the Man United job unless he gets TWO new signings to fix 'the worst back four in the Premier League', says Gary Neville
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino should TURN DOWN the Man United job unless he gets TWO new signings to fix 'the worst back four in the Premier League', says Gary Neville

Mauricio Pochettino has been warned against taking the Manchester United job, by Gary Neville unless the club's hierarchy promise to back him in the January transfer window and bolster 'the worst back four in the Premier League'.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Pochettino is expected to be named as the new Red Devils head coach, with Michael Carrick - who was pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - set to be sacked later today.

Director of football Jason Wilcox was pictured arriving to the club's training ground on Thursday morning too. He had been in Monaco the day before with the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Upon Pochettino's expected arrival, he will join a club languishing in the relegation zone - with United 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 matches.

United have conceded 19 goals across those 10 games - with only 14th-placed Ipswich Town (20) and bottom side Crystal Palace (24) having conceded more.

Mauricio Pochettino (pictured) has been warned against becoming the new Man United head coach by Gary Neville unless they promise him defensive reinforcements in January

Michael Carrick arrives at Carrington on Thursday morning ahead of his expected sacking

Director of football Jason Wilcox was pictured arriving to the club's training ground on Thursday morning after being in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's fate at the club

And speaking about Pochettino's pending arrival, Neville insists on the Argentine making ultimatums to the board if they want him - starting with improving the defence.

'If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven,' he said on The Overlap.

'He'll do that with a pay-off. So do that in your contract. But secondly, he needs two defenders in January. So he's got to insist that he gets two defenders in January. He's got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer we're not to be able to turn this around. He's got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

'They have to give it to him or else he shouldn't take the job.'

Expanding further, the former United right back didn't hold back in his criticism of the current defensive options at the club.

'I mean look the back four that he finished with on Sunday was [Diogo] Dalot left back, [Noussair] Mazraoui right back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven,' he said.

'That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League. I don't know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. That is I can't believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.'

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

Neville believes Manchester United have 'the worst back four in the Premier League'

Diogo Dalot (left) gave away a penalty during United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games, with United said to be relaxed over the Argentine taking the team. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

Sports.title: Pat Cummins is caught in heated row with his wife, barefoot in public, before his partner posted loved-up photo with Australia cricket captain
Sports.content:
Pat Cummins' wife, Becky, has shared an affectionate family photo hours after images emerged of the couple in an animated exchange on a Sydney street, as Usman Khawaja's allegations reignite the Sandpapergate saga.

News Corp published images of the couple in a heated discussion beside their car on Wednesday afternoon and reported that the exchange lasted about five minutes before they went inside a property.

Cummins was barefoot and alternated between pacing and leaning against the car, while Becky did much of the talking.

Cummins' management declined to comment on the exchange.

In the photo shared on her Instagram Story, Becky rested her head against her husband as he held their daughter, Edith, whose face was hidden from view. She tagged Cummins and captioned the photo: 'My loves'.

Meanwhile, the Australian cricket captain has invited reporters to question him on Friday about Usman Khawaja's claims that the entire Australian team knew about the ball-tampering in Cape Town in 2018 and that sandpaper had also been used in the previous Test in Port Elizabeth.

'Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week at 9.30am.

'I've taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly.'

Pat Cummins and wife Becky were photographed having an animated conversation on a Sydney street on Wednesday before posting this selfie

Cummins has invited reporters to question him about Usman Khawaja's allegations at Cricket Central

Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr, released on Tuesday, alleges knowledge extended beyond Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, the three players Cricket Australia sanctioned over the scandal.

Bancroft was caught using sandpaper on the ball during the third Test in Cape Town in March 2018.

Smith and Warner received 12-month bans and lost the captaincy and vice-captaincy, respectively. Bancroft received a nine-month suspension.

Khawaja's account has placed fresh scrutiny on the bowling group, which included Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon.

'It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us,' he told the Sydney Morning Herald at the weekend ahead of its release.

In a joint statement in 2021, the four bowlers said they had not known a foreign substance had been taken onto the field to alter the ball's condition during the Cape Town Test.

Starc defended his account again on Wednesday when asked about Khawaja's allegations concerning the preceding Test in Port Elizabeth.

'Yeah, that's the first I was aware of any of that taking place in PE... was when [Khawaja said it]... I'll leave that for said authors to explain,' Starc said.

The Australian captain said he had taken time to understand the full extent of Khawaja's claims

Khawaja's autobiography Sabr has reignited questions about Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal

Warner has thrown his support behind his former opening partner.

'It's been eight years since I've spoken on this topic and Uzzie, I throw my full support behind you,' he said.

'I thank you for what you've done. It's 100 per cent accurate what you've said. Everyone knows the truth. It's out there. People wanted to know it.'

Khawaja faced pointed questions about his account during an appearance on ABC's 7.30, including whether he was angry that the bowlers had not admitted knowing about the use of sandpaper.

'I'll say again, I've given my statement about what happened the game before,' he said.

'I was very open and honest to what I saw and what conversations I had.

'Sometimes I'm very specific on things, and sometimes I'm a bit vague on things, and I do it on purpose because I'm trying to tell a story.'

Pressed further about the bowlers, Khawaja declined to elaborate.

'I'm just not going... I'm not going to entertain that,' he said.

'I'm not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment.'

He also acknowledged uncertainty about what the fallout could mean for his friendship with Cummins.

Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft received lengthy bans following the Cape Town scandal

Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has opposed reopening the investigation

Khawaja claims knowledge of ball tampering extended beyond the three players who received bans

Pat Cummins will face questions from reporters on Friday about Usman Khawaja’s claimsover the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.

Join the discussion Should past cricket scandals be reopened or is it time to let players move on?

'I've told my truth, and I'd give him my reasons,' Khawaja said.

'Pat Cummins is a good friend of mine. Mitchell Starc, a lot of these guys, players in the team, Shaun Marsh, Mitch Marsh, are all very good friends of mine. I'm not here to go on a witch hunt.'

Khawaja subsequently cancelled several media appearances, including an interview with Seven News, although he denied cancelling his book tour.

Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has said there would be 'absolutely no benefit' in reopening the investigation.

It has also been reported that CA chairman David Boon backed Cummins and assured him his captaincy was secure.

Before the latest allegations became public, Cummins said the team had already answered questions about the scandal repeatedly.

'It's obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times,' he said ahead of Australia's recent South Africa tour.

'It was dealt with then. All I can say is, as a group, we've moved on.'

Cummins also said Khawaja had given him some notice of the book's contents.

'He didn't go into too much detail... As always it was "no worries, you can tell your story, that's fine".'

Sports.title: Astonishing moment UFC star is brutally 'attacked' by a rival while filming an interview at a five-star hotel, leaving him battered and bruised just days before his next fight
Sports.content:
UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was left bloodied after claiming rival Usman Nurmagomedov attacked him at a five-star hotel while he was filming an interview.

Dvalishvili is set to fight on Saturday in Abu Dhabi, and had described preparations as 'a normal fight week'.

That, though, has now been thrown out the window, with Dvalishvili claiming footage showing him getting jumped portrayed Nurmagomedov and his brother, Umar, alongside their friends, attacking him.

In the early hours of Thursday morning, journalist Ariel Helwani reported on X that 'everyone involved in the hotel brawl is still being detained by the local authorities'.

In the footage, the group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man said a couple of words to him and punched him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

WARNING: Graphic content

Merab was in the middle of filming an interview when Usman and his crew just walked up and openly started assaulting him. pic.twitter.com/eFVWq9S5gW — Parry Punch (@ParryPunchNews) November 11, 2026

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a five-star hotel - blaming rival Usman Nurmagomedov (Instagram/merab.dvalishvili)

The 35-year-old was blind sided while carrying out an interview ahead of his fight this weekend (Instagram/merab.dvalishvili)

Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

Sports.title: David Warner unleashes on former coach who denied Usman Khawaja's Sandpapergate claims: 'Let's get the facts straight'
Sports.content:
David Warner has fired back at former Australia batting coach Graeme Hick after he branded Usman Khawaja’s claims about the Sandpapergate scandal ‘absolutely false’.

Warner also claimed Australian players offered to contribute part of their salaries to keep Michael Di Venuto as batting coach before Hick replaced him in 2016.

'Let’s get the facts straight. Graeme Hick was only appointed because Cricket Australia was unwilling to pay Michael Di Venuto what he deserved,' Warner wrote on X.

'As players, we valued Michael so highly that we even offered to contribute from our own salaries to retain him.

'These discussions were taking place during the New Zealand tour. That alone speaks volumes about how highly we regarded him and how determined we were to keep him involved. Adds to why Graeme has spoken!!'

Warner’s intervention came after Hick rejected Khawaja’s claim that responsibility for the 2018 ball-tampering scandal extended to the Australian team and coaching staff.

'I have seen the various statements around the coaches, and I'm very disappointed with the broad nature of them,' Hick told The Sydney Morning Herald.

'Khawaja puts it simply: 'It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us'. To me, what Khawaja is implying here is absolutely false.'

David Warner (pictured right with Usman Khawaja) has launched another attack as the Sandpapergate dispute continues to divide Australian cricket

Former Australian batting coach Graeme Hick (pictured right with Aussie batsman Travis Head) has strongly rejected Khawaja’s allegations

Warner claims Australian players offered to contribute from their salaries to retain Di Venuto

Hick also explicitly denied knowing about discussions concerning ball-tampering at either Port Elizabeth or Cape Town.

'In regard to any discussions around the ball-tampering in Port Elizabeth or Cape Town, I will say in true honesty that I did not hear or know anything,' he said.

'My first knowledge of all this was, like many, when it appeared on the big screen in Cape Town as I was sat on the outside balcony at the time.'

Hick replaced Di Venuto as Australia’s batting coach in 2016, about two years before the Sandpapergate scandal.

Di Venuto had served in the role since 2013 after a playing career in which he scored 25,200 first-class runs and represented Australia in nine one-day internationals.

His time with the national side coincided with Steve Smith's transformation into one of the world's leading batters.

Australia also trusted Di Venuto to step in as head coach when Darren Lehmann was sidelined with deep vein thrombosis shortly before Di Venuto's departure for Surrey.

Smith made clear how highly Di Venuto was regarded in a farewell message at the time.

Di Venuto enjoyed a prolific domestic playing career before moving into coaching

Steve Smith praised Michael Di Venuto in a glowing farewell message a decade ago

'Thanks Michael Di Venuto for all that you have done for me the last couple of years,' Smith wrote.

'You've been an absolutely amazing Batting coach and a great man. You are going to be missed by myself and all of the Australian batters.

'You are going to be a great head coach and Surrey are very lucky to have you.'

Di Venuto went on to deliver the success Smith predicted, guiding Surrey to the 2018 County Championship, the club's first title in the competition for 16 years.

Smith’s tribute supports Warner’s claim that players valued Di Venuto, although it makes no mention of a salary dispute or an offer to help fund his retention.

Hick served as Australia's batting coach from 2016 to 2020 and was part of the coaching setup when Cameron Bancroft was caught using sandpaper on the ball during the Cape Town Test.

Warner has firmly backed Khawaja's version of events, declaring: 'It's 100 per cent accurate what you've said. Now everyone knows the truth.'

However, their account has been disputed by Hick, former head coach Darren Lehmann and fast bowler Mitchell Starc.

Warner has publicly backed Khawaja’s account of the Sandpapergate scandal

Join the discussion Should more people be held accountable for Sandpapergate, or is blame being unfairly spread?

Former bowling coach David Saker previously said the blame may have been spread more widely in a 2021 interview.

'Obviously, a lot of things went wrong at that time,' he said.

'The finger-pointing is going to go on and on, and on. There was a lot of people to blame. It could have been me to blame, it could have been someone else. It could have been stopped, and it wasn't, which is unfortunate.

'Cameron's a very nice guy. He's just doing it [the media interview] to get something off his chest … he's not going to be the last. You could point your finger at me, you could point your finger at 'Boof' [Lehmann], could you point it at other people – of course you could.

'The disappointing thing is it's never going to go away, regardless of what's said. We all know that we made a monumental mistake. The gravity wasn't as plain until it all came out.'

The competing accounts have reopened the wounds of a scandal that resulted in 12-month bans for Warner and Smith and a nine-month suspension for Bancroft.

In his autobiography Sabr, Khawaja challenges Cricket Australia's finding that only those three players had prior knowledge of the plan.

He has defended his decision to revisit the scandal while declining to publicly identify which individuals knew about it.

Cricket Australia has maintained its support for the original investigation and says it has no compelling reason to reopen it.

Sports.title: Sports broadcaster Julie Stewart-Binks, 39, laid off just weeks after revealing skin cancer diagnosis: 'Livelihood ripped away'
Sports.content:
Sports broadcaster Julie Stewart-Binks, 39, laid off just weeks after revealing skin cancer diagnosis: 'Livelihood ripped away'

Sports reporter Julie Stewart-Binks has been laid off by SNY – just weeks after revealing her cancer diagnosis.

Cruelly, the 39-year-old only found out that her livelihood had been 'ripped away' when her former agent read about it in the New York Times.

Last month, Stewart-Binks explained that she had been off the air after being diagnosed with skin cancer. The veteran broadcaster, who has made stops at ESPN, Barstool Sports and Fox Sports, revealed that she needed to go under the knife to 'remove squamous cell carcinoma' in her nose.

'I thought it was a pimple that wouldn't go away, turns out it was cancer,' she said. Barely a month on, however, Stewart-Binks confirmed that she had lost her job.

'I was laid off on Friday,' she said in a social media video. 'To have gone through a very public skin cancer removal to then be informed by a New York Times article that you didn’t have a job was not on the bingo card for this year.'

She added: 'It turns out, part of the business is wondering how many American holidays you have to work to be invited to the holiday party until you get a message from your former agent that says FYI and it's a link to a New York Times article where it says you don’t have a job anymore.'

Julie Stewart-Binks has been laid off by SNY - just weeks after revealing her cancer diagnosis

She learned her livelihood had been 'ripped away' when her ex-agent read about it in the NYT

Stewart-Binks recently explained that she had been off air after being diagnosed with cancer

Stewart-Binks explained that this is not the first time she has been laid off during her career. '[But] even when you know you’re going to get back up it doesn’t mean your ego isn’t bruised,' she admitted.

'It's just part of the business... [but] in all honesty, it really sucks for a lot of people and in sports broadcasting we spend most of our time talking about this - athletes being cut, waived, released.'

The broadcaster, who spent seven years as a host, reporter and 'opinionist' for SNY, continued: 'Most importantly your job and your workplace are not your identity. Don’t give them the power over who you are... it’s just another day in my life.'

In January 2025, Stewart-Binks filed a lawsuit against Fox Sports and former executive Charlie Dixon, alleging Dixon pushed her against a wall and forcibly kissed her after a work meeting in 2016.

Dixon, who was subsequently fired from the network after being placed on administrative leave for a separate sexual battery complaint, denied any 'sexual or offensive contact' with Stewart-Binks.

In July 2025, she asked to dismiss the suit and issued a statement saying the 'matter has been resolved.'

Sports.title: Man United legend Peter Schmeichel fumes over club's 'very disrespectful' treatment of Michael Carrick as Mauricio Pochettino closes in on Old Trafford job
Sports.content:
Peter Schmeichel has hit out at the 'very disrespectful' way that he believes beleaguered Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is being treated as he awaits his sacking at Old Trafford. The former club captain has endured a torrid start to the season, and while the Man United hierarchy publicly backed him as recently as three weeks ago, Carrick is now set to be handed his marching orders following a crisis summit in Monaco. Man United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to the Principality to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to ratify the decision to move on from Carrick, with current USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed in his wake. But with Carrick still taking team training at Carrington while plans for his ejection from the club made global headlines, Schmeichel admitted he felt deep sympathy for the former midfielder's awkward position. 'I think the way this is playing out is very disrespectful to him,' Schmeichel said on The Overlap Daily. 'If I’m honest, I don’t think he’s doing anything wrong. Michael Carrick remains in limbo at Manchester United after a shocking start to the season Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have been in Monaco discussing his dismissal this week

Your browser does not support iframes.

'I know the team that he’s in charge of is where they are in the table, but I don’t put all of that on him. There are so many things that have been going on at Manchester United literally since Alex (Ferguson) and (former chief executive) David Gill left the club. And it’s never been corrected. 'It’s not been the correct people, not the right people in charge, and slowly it’s just gone worse.' Man United sit within the relegation zone as this international break plays out, with Carrick's men winless in the Premier League since late August. Last-minute comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in domestic action however may have briefly boosted morale at Old Trafford. But to Schmeichel, the issue lies at the feet of those who recruit at the club, rather than Carrick himself. 'If you think about this transfer window now, it’s abundantly clear to everyone - everyone who knows just a little bit about football - that Manchester United needed defenders,' he continued. 'They got through a whole transfer window without signing a single defender. 'There was a little bit of talk about Lewis Hall joining the club or going for Lewis Hall. That didn’t happen. And so, they bought three midfield players. And we know, because we’ve been in the game for so many years, that you can’t win games - if you concede 30 goals in 10 games, then there is a problem, and that was not addressed. 'Now, was Michael Carrick in on those decisions? Well, it took them forever, forever, to give him the job. So, I suspect he wasn’t in any of those discussions about who to sign up until the point he got named as manager. Former Man United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel believes the club's treatment of Carrick has been demeaning The under-fire manager turned up to take training for a second day in a row as speculation swirled over his future

Your browser does not support iframes.

'So yes, I do feel a lot of sympathy for Michael. I think what is happening is wrong. I think we should stick with Michael. I think we should just try and steady the ship a little bit and then get into January and then sign the players that he feels he needs to bring the team forward and then be realistic about what this season is all about. Obviously, it’s about climbing as high as Manchester United can in the table.' By contrast, Schmeichel's co-pundit Tim Sherwood said he did not feel sorry for Carrick, because he will have understood the brutal situation he was stepping into at Man United. The former Middlesbrough head coach served as interim manager for the second-half of the previous season following the sacking of Ruben Amorim, and was named on a permanent basis over the summer. But while Schmeichel admitted that the life cycle of a Premier League coach was undeniably short, his issue is with the manner of treatment Carrick has received in the process of the changing of the guard in the dugout. 'If they’re looking for somebody else, then relieve the man of his duties,' the former goalkeeper argued. 'Don’t let him come into training yesterday. He took training yesterday. How disrespectful is that? 'How do you think this fella – I mean, he’s a human being. He’s a very, very good human being. He’s one of the nicest people you’ll ever meet in your life, and obviously you two know him well. So, treat the guy with respect. Tell him, "Sorry, mate. We don’t think that you are the future here. Here’s a cheque. Move on." But they’re not doing that. They’re dragging it out.' Schmeichel was incensed too by Carrick's status within the club, wondering aloud whether, since they had taken 'weeks and weeks' to come to their messy, public decision, the club's hierarchy might not really understand what it is to truly represent the club. 'Do you think these people know? Do you think they care?' Schmeichel continued. 'These people are not Manchester United people. 'They don’t understand what it’s like to be one of the Manchester United people. They don’t know that. This is obviously part of the broader issue here, part of the reason the club is where they are now. I’m not saying I feel sorry for Michael, but I’m a little bit angry at how this great football club is treating one of its greatest players. Simple as that.' Talks have been planned with Pochettino overnight on Wednesday, with the club's hierarchy thought to be preparing to dismiss Carrick face-to-face on Thursday. Mauricio Pochettino remains locked in talks to take over at Old Trafford as the club's preferred candidate for the role

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday. It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester. The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and it seems inconceivable that Pochettino would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later. It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave. It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill. The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m. Meanwhile in Manchester, Carrick took training for the second day in a row at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday, arriving at 7.45am and departing shortly after 1.30pm. Carrick has overseen the club's worst start to the season in 40 years, but the man himself remained adamant that he would not be falling on his sword after battling back to claim a draw against Villa. In an awkward interview with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick remained steadfast in the face of questions as to whether he would quit his role amid the turbulence. 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games,' he said. 'But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'
