Racing Bulls has also been explicitly asked by Austria to stand on its own feet both in terms of identity and performance, so that's why a dyed-in-the-wool F1 veteran like team principal Alan Permane would have been keen to maximise performance and stick with Lawson.



"The main factors are, as always, pace and speed. That's the very first thing we look for," Permane said when grilled on the topic on Friday in Sao Paulo. "But we're not just a team that exists solely to compete. We are here to bring young talent through, so we have to keep an eye on that. And that doesn't necessarily mean that we just keep churning young talent through the car. We need to maybe have some experience as well to measure that talent."

The clearest hint that a difference in opinion between the various stakeholders is what has really been holding up the decision came from Lawson himself. "I feel like Alan's been extremely supportive to me and I appreciate that a lot," he said. "I've enjoyed working closely with him and with the team this year. Obviously, it's a big organisation so..."



Permane recently inked a fresh deal until 2031 as Racing Bulls team principal and co-CEO, so it's obvious that his opinion carries plenty of weight. And it would stand to reason that Permane has wanted some assurances about his share in the decision-making before committing.

"Alan is doing a tremendous job, and the progress the team has made is a direct reflection of his experience, commitment and competitive mindset," said Permane's boss Oliver Mintzlaff, CEO Corporate Projects and Investments Red Bull. "He brings clarity, composure, and a deep understanding of what it takes to perform in Formula 1, while creating an environment where people can consistently deliver at their best."

Meanwhile, fans of Lawson and the team have been flooding the squad's social media channels urging it to re-sign the Kiwi. He said: "I appreciate all the support. I've seen it over the last few weeks. It's honestly really nice to see.

A treacherous Brazil weekend was one of Liam Lawson's finest. Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"Obviously, I would love it if it was more from a team. But at the moment I'm just trying to enjoy driving the car because with everything else going on I don't really know what else I'm meant to do. I don't really know what else I'm meant to say to you guys. So, at the moment I'm just going to keep driving and see what happens."

When it mattered the most, Brazil was perhaps Lawson's finest weekend yet. In treacherous conditions, Lawson took fifth on the grid, starting from third after grid penalties for George Russell and Charles Leclerc.

In the rain, he picked off McLaren's Lando Norris for second at the start, only to fall back to his natural position once drivers got their intermediate tyres back in the right operating window. Lawson battled to claim eighth on the road, being promoted to seventh after Leclerc was penalised for barging his way past in the closing laps.



Permane was obviously appreciative of how tough the past few weeks and months have been on one of F1 2026's standout performers, but said the team is nearly there.



"I realise it's frustrating for our drivers," he added. "I realise it's frustrating for everyone else, but we want to get it right, and we will get it right. I'm sure when we announce it in the coming weeks, everyone will be happy..."

Sports.title: Piastri and Webber terminate management agreement
Sports.content:
Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber have mutually agreed to terminate their management agreement, the pair have announced.

Webber and his wife Ann – who ran Mark’s career herself back in the day – became Piastri’s managers in 2019, the year the youngster narrowly beat Victor Martins to the Formula Renault Eurocup title and a spot on Renault’s F1 academy.

Piastri’s rise was meteoric from then on, as he clinched the Formula 3 title the following year – again marginally, with Theo Pourchaire and Logan Sargeant just a few points adrift – and won Formula 2 in 2021, also as a rookie, and with little competition that time.

Under Webber, Piastri made the career-defining move to leave the Alpine fold and sign a McLaren race deal for the 2023 Formula 1 season, which paved the way for his 2025 title bid. Across 88 career starts so far, the Australian has taken six pole positions and nine victories.

“We are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of Oscar's career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early on,” Webber said.

“Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close. This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure, and for us to embark on our new ventures. We wish Oscar all the very best for a long and successful career.”

Oscar Piastri, McLaren Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

Piastri added: “I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward.”

Webber had taken a step back at the start of the 2026 season and no longer supported Piastri trackside, with a couple of new figures assisting the McLaren driver – Pedro Matos, his race engineer at Prema in Formula 2, and mental coach Emma Murray.

“There wasn't anything specific, just we made a decision for things to look a bit different,” Piastri said back in February. “Mark is still very much involved and I've been in contact with him a lot over the last few weeks. He just won't be trackside as much anymore. So that's really the extent of it.

“There was nothing specific that triggered it.”

Appearing on the High Performance Podcast in May, the 25-year-old added: “The relationship's good. Very thorough, is Mark. When I first got into F1, Mark was coming up with questions and ideas that literally hadn't even entered my brain. I would hear him say it and go like, 'How the hell did he think of that?' Or like, 'How am I ever going to think of that?'

Oscar Piastri, McLaren with Mark Webber Photo by: Getty Images

“And I think just with experience, we're always learning every day, but now starting my fourth year, I have either the answers to a lot of those kinds of questions that I wouldn't have had in the first couple of years, or I know the questions to keep asking, which just comes with experience.

“There's naturally less and less for Mark to do on the racing side of things the more experienced I become. But especially in the first couple of years, there are some lessons you have to learn the hard way, and there's no other way of doing it, but I'm sure there could have been plenty of other slightly annoying, tougher lessons to learn that I was probably spared because of Mark's experience and Mark's guidance.

“There's probably always going to be situations or things that have gone smoothly or almost problems that weren't problems that I'm never going to know about because Mark managed them for me. That's probably how it's changed in the last few years.”

Sports.title: Leclerc penalised for Lawson clash; Antonelli and Oliver Bearman also punished after F1 Brazilian GP
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc was handed a five-second penalty after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix for his clash with Liam Lawson, dropping the Ferrari driver down to eighth place in the final results.

The Monegasque was battling the Racing Bulls driver for seventh place on lap 69 of the Sao Paulo race when the pair made contact into Juncao, Turn 12, but both were able to continue and finish the race.

The clash did enable Leclerc to take seventh place from Lawson but the incident was placed under investigation for a post-race hearing.

After speaking to both drivers and assessing the video and data, the FIA stewards determined Leclerc was to blame and duly gave him a five-second penalty, dropping the Ferrari driver behind his rival and into eighth place in the final results.

The FIA stewards accepted that the contact was minor and in wet conditions, which was enough mitigation to keep the penalty to 5s and not a potential 10s punishment.

The FIA stewards report read: “While the contact was minor and Car 30 was able to maintain the lead thereafter, the driver of Car 30 claimed that the contact damaged the rear left rim of his car and also enabled Car 16 to get closer to him on track and then eventually overtake him 5 corners later. Furthermore, under the Driving Standard Guidelines, Car 30 had the right to the corner and it was for Car 16 to take the necessary steps to avoid a collision.

Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

“The driver of Car 16 claimed that it was a minor contact with no obvious sporting consequence.

“While we acknowledge that the contact was minor, having examined the fight on track between the two cars, we conclude that Car 16 was able to get closer to and thereafter overtake Car 30 because of the contact. The contact clearly disrupted Car 30 and allowed Car 16 to pull up alongside when it was further away before the contact. This was an obvious sporting consequence.

“In mitigation, the wet conditions coupled with the nature of the contact (i.e. minor) was taken into account in imposing a 5 second time penalty as opposed to a 10 second time penalty.”

Antonelli and Bearman also penalised for unsafe releases from pitstops

New F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli was also given a five-second penalty after the Brazilian GP for an unsafe pitstop release.

The Italian was released from his final pitstop of the race into the path of the oncoming Franco Colapinto and despite attempting to take avoiding action it was judged unsafe and a five-second penalty was duly handed out.

But because Antonelli finished over 20s ahead of Oscar Piastri, who was directly behind him on the road, it does not change his final finishing position of fifth place – as Mercedes secured this year’s F1 constructors’ championship.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

In a separate incident also involving Leclerc, Oliver Bearman was given a post-race five-second penalty for an unsafe release from a pitstop. The Haas F1 driver was released into the path of the Ferrari driver, which forced Leclerc to check-up in the pitlane.

The penalty has no consequence to Bearman either given he finished in 17th and one lap up on Sergio Perez in 18th place.

Sports.title: Antonelli explains "weird" spin and car instability which cost F1 Brazilian GP win
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli vowed to put aside his Brazilian Grand Prix anger to celebrate Mercedes winning the Formula 1 constructors' title, as he rued the balance issues and the spin that took him out of victory contention.

The new world champion had picked up the lead from polesitter Lando Norris at the start, and was building a pretty healthy lead over the Briton in the opening laps of the race. He held the lead either side of the first round of pitstops, as the circuit was dry enough for slicks, although Norris' undercut had taken a considerable chunk of time out of Antonelli's advantage.

At the start of lap 20, Antonelli then lost the car and this precipitated a spin at the opening corner. He was able to recover, but Norris had long since bolted past for the lead - and it left the Italian in the clutches of Isack Hadjar.

Antonelli had reported before his spin that he was worried he'd picked up a suspension issue, and that the car was pulling to one side under acceleration - and his difficulty with balance cost further positions to Hadjar and Max Verstappen. However, no clear cause had emerged during the race.

"I'm very disappointed for the race. I'm very angry to be fair, but I'm going to put all this aside for now because the team clinched the title," Antonelli said.

"We clinched the title for the team, and they all deserve it and I'm very proud to be part of this group and this team who has done and still does so much for me and I'm very happy for them. But talking about the race specifically, yeah, very disappointing.

Lando Norris, McLaren, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"We were on for the win up to that point. Also in the lead, once I was able to get some temperature I was getting to the rhythm. But yeah, the spin came which still is something I need to look at because I don't know why I lost the rear so quickly as well.

"Like no warning, nothing. But already to be fair when I put the soft, I felt something weird with the car. So, we need to check what happened but on the other hand yeah, shame because we lost the race there."

When speaking to Sky Sports, Antonelli expanded on the issue and noted that it was only occurring in the left-hand corners, particularly in higher-speed sections - which, around Interlagos, would account for much of the first and third sectors.

The tyre flat spots sustained in the spin made his life much harder; when he'd taken a second set of soft tyres, his improvement in lap time was demonstrable and this afforded an opportunity to challenge Hadjar late on.

"We need to check something with the geometry of the car, of the rear, because I had this issue only in left corners. So especially at the high speed was when I was feeling it the most," he told Sky.

"And the rear felt very unstable, even in coming into the finish line in the left kink, the rear was very loose, which was weird.

"We need to check something in the car to see if anything happened. But it was a very odd feeling. And then when I spun, the tyres were gone; all four wheels flat spotted. Only when then I put on the second set, we got back to pace. It was a shame."

Sports.title: On This Day: Bourdais wins in final bow for Champ Car’s Lola in Mexico City | Brief
Sports.content:
20 years ago today Sebastien Bourdais won the 14th and final race of the 2006 Champ Car series. It was the final race for the Lola B2/00 chassis before it was replaced by a new designed built by Panoz.

The race was held at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, prior to its remodelling for F1’s return in 2015. Most of the corners were wider and quicker.

In previous years the cars ran through the Foro Sol stadium, much as F1 does today. However for 2006 the original, 180-degree Peraltada was restored, but with a tight chicane before it.

Sports.title: On This Day: F1’s first female racer, Maria Teresa de Filiipis, born 100 years ago | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Maria Theresa de Filippis, the first woman to start a round of the Formula 1 world championship, was born 100 years ago to this day.

She started 19th on the grid for the Belgian Grand Prix in 1958 (above) in a privately-entered Maserati 250F. She took the chequered flag in 10th place, but unlike today, only the top five finishers scored points.

De Filippis started two other races that year, but retired from both with engine trouble, and made two unsuccessful attempts to qualify for the Monaco Grand Prix. She died 10 years ago.

Sports.title: Lawson made sure Red Bull saw he helped Verstappen in Brazil after Mexico incident | Formula 1
Sports.content:
“When you’re fighting for your seat, it’s not very smart behaviour,” remarked Max Verstappen after Liam Lawson refused to get out of his way during practice in Mexico last week.

A week later during the grand prix at Interlagos, Lawson was far more obliging. He dived out of Verstappen’s way when the Red Bull driver appeared in his mirrors. Lawson then made sure his Racing Bulls team – and perhaps more importantly its senior sibling Red Bull – did not overlook how helpful he’d been.

It’s not uncommon to see drivers make way for their team mates when ordered to on the radio. In the same race Isack Hadjar slowed significantly to let Verstappen in the other Red Bull past.

Lawson, in theory at least, drives for a rival team and has no need to be helpful at all. But while a midfield team driver such as Lawson would likely see no benefit from wasting time and tyre life fighting one of the front-running cars, nor would they be expected to cost themselves time by slowing down. “Don’t lose time with him” is typical advice from race engineers.

Yet that is precisely what Lawson did. Racing Bulls made sure he was aware how quickly Verstappen was gaining on him. Then Lawson dived out of the way on the Reta Oposta back straight, slowing so sharply he dropped down two gears and lost over one-and-a-half seconds.

Job done, he pointed out to race engineer Alexandre Iliopoulos he had not cost Verstappen any time:

Lap: 9/71 LAW: 1’28.088 Iliopoulos Copy. The car behind is now Max. Iliopoulos Some cars around are struggling with tyres. Iliopoulos Car behind is Max, two seconds. Iliopoulos Feedback on balance when you can Lawson Well, it’s just graining, so I have no fronts, and the traction is really, really bad. Do you want me to try clear it? Lap: 10/71 LAW: 1’27.900 Iliopoulos Yes. Yes, we think that’s the best option. Iliopoulos Engine braking eight if you want. Engine nine position three. Lap: 11/71 LAW: 1’29.516 Iliopoulos Push toggle last corner if you want. Iliopoulos Lawson pulls over, slows down and lets Verstappen pass him

Car behind, Piastri, one second, and Hulkenberg is six behind you. Lawson Yep, I let him go. Iliopoulos Copy.

Lawson is still waiting to learn if he will remain at Red Bull’s junior team next year. He clearly wanted to demonstrate he is ready to help Racing Bulls’ sister team.

He was much more prepared to fight his corner in Miami earlier this year, when he challenged Racing Bulls’ order that he let Verstappen past.

But Lawson’s eagerness to show his worth to Red Bull also highlights how unusual their arrangement with their junior team is. One driver pulling over and slowing down so blatantly to let a driver from a rival team overtake him – and then drawing attention to it – would be astonishing if it involved any other pair of teams on the grid.

Sports.title: F1 scraps back-up plan to race at Imola if Middle East GPs are cancelled – reports | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has committed to holding the final two rounds of the 2026 world championship in the Middle East or not at all.

The series had made contingency arrangements to relocate the final round it Imola in Italy if it decided the risks posed by the war in Iran meant it should not proceed with its races in the Middle East. Multiple reports now claim F1 has told Imola it will not be required to hold a race.

The world championship will resume at Las Vegas in the USA next week. Following that it is due to race at the Losail International Circuit in Qatar and Yas Marina in the United Arab Emirates on the following weekends.

The series cancelled its grands prix in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this year due to the war between Iran and the USA. It later held an event using the ‘Bahrain Grand Prix’ title at Malaysia’s Sepang International Circuit.

The political situation in the Middle East remains uncertain. US president Donald Trump this week suggested he would not escalate its military campaign in the region, but has made similar comments since beginning his war in February, only to subsequently launch further strikes. The US retains a significant military presences in the region and moved more troops there last month.

However Moto GP, which like F1 is owned by Liberty Media, raced in Losail on Sunday. It postponed its Qatar round in April due to the war.

Four bikes were missing from the field as Yamaha did not participate. Most of the series’ riders expressed concerns over visiting the country and asked the championship to provide extra guarantees for their security.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff defended Moto GP’s decision to race in Qatar. He criticised riders who expressed concerns about racing there, saying they “know nothing” about the situation.

Many television broadcasters also opted not to send their staff to the region.

The 2027 F1 season is due to begin in the Middle East with races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia next March. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali told investors last week “the disruption we experienced in the Middle East this year does not change our long-term regional strategy and ongoing partnership with our promoters.”

“This year, we currently remain scheduled to complete our calendar season and at this stage, continue to plan to finish the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi,” he added. “We will continue to monitor the situation. As always, the safety and security of everyone in the sport will remain our first and foremost priority.”

Many other series have cancelled events in the region due to the war in the Middle East. The World Endurance Championship called off its planned rounds in Qatar and Bahrain, replacing them with races in Italy and Spain. The 2027 Dakar Rally, previously held in Saudi Arabia, will take place in Africa. The 2026-27 Asian Le Mans series, which previously raced at Dubai Autodrome and Yas Marina, will take place in Europe under the name ‘Winter Le Mans Series’.

Sports.title: No F1 engine manufacturers to get extra upgrades after FIA’s third ADUO evaluation | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA will not to offer any engine manufacturers the chance to perform extra power unit upgrades following its latest Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) evaluation.

Under new rules introduced as part of Formula 1’s 2026 power unit regulations the sport’s governing body controls how often manufacturers can upgrade their internal combustion engines.

The evaluations take place periodically throughout the season. The FIA has completed its third such evaluation and, as was the case during the second, determined no further engine homologation opportunities should be offered.

The third evaluation period concluded after the United States Grand Prix last month. The second followed the Hungarian Grand Prix.

The first evaluation period, which ran from the start of the season to the Canadian Grand Prix, remains the only time any additional upgrade opportunities were awarded. On that occasion Red Bull-Ford were found to have the top-performing power unit.

Audi, Ferrari and Honda’s units were found to be more than 4% less powerful. They were permitted two extra homologation opportunities this year and two more next year. Mercedes were found to be within 2% and 4% of the leading power unit and therefore received one extra upgrade this year and next.

Separately, in May the FIA changed the ADUO rules to allow any manufacturer which was 10% off the leading design to spend more money. The revision was expected to assist Honda following their poor start to the season.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Some have likened F1’s ADUO to the World Endurance Championship’s heavily-criticised Balance of Performance regulations. The FIA’s single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis defended the regulations but indicated they may be revised in coming seasons.

“Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” he said.

“The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1. However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose.

“To that end, we have been working closely with the power unit manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons.”

Sports.title: Roy Jones Jr. Backs Vasily Lomachenko but Warns About Foster
Sports.content:
Roy Jones Jr. believes Vasiliy Lomachenko can still be competitive at 38, provided he drops down to 130 pounds and adjusts his approach following a layoff of over two years. Even with those changes, Jones views unified champion O’Shaquie Foster as a dangerous test for Lomachenko right now.

“I think that break gave him a chance to re-evaluate the whole situation and see that he should be fighting 130, which is true. And now he can go out the way he wants to go out,” Jones said on Hall of Game. Citing the Devin Haney bout as evidence, Jones explained that lightweight was simply too big for Lomachenko. He also noted that the extended hiatus likely gave the two-time Olympic gold medalist a much-needed mental reset after a grueling career.

Before Lomachenko even considers a title shot against Foster, he is expected to return against Charly Suarez, a tough super featherweight contender who gave Emanuel Navarrete major problems in their clash.

Taking on a high-motor opponent like Suarez right out of a two-year absence carries obvious risk, leaving Lomachenko little room to shake off ring rust. Still, Jones believes Lomachenko remains more skilled than 75% of the active boxers in the sport. Doubting a two-time Olympic gold medalist overlooks the fact that elite fundamentals and ring IQ do not simply vanish after two years away.

The real test against a relentless pressure fighter like Suarez, or a master technician like Foster, will be how frequently Lomachenko can still dart to his opponent’s blind side and fire before they have time to turn. While he might pull that off in short bursts, surviving twelve rounds means finding ways to score from a stationary position. That becomes critical against an opponent who uses a stiff jab to dictate range and force him to reset.

“To me, O’Shaquie is peaking right now. So that’s the wrong time to really mess with him,” Jones added. Foster proved that point against Emanuel Navarrete by controlling distance, clinching effectively on the inside, and maintaining enough power to score a knockdown in the twelfth round. Lomachenko would need to bait Foster into overextending before creating his signature angles, though Foster possesses the discipline to force Lomachenko to initiate the action.

Ultimately, Jones thinks Lomachenko’s deep amateur pedigree gives him the tools to trouble Foster if he evolves his game. The main thing to watch at super featherweight is whether Lomachenko can bait reactions with his jab and feints. If he can pull a younger opponent out of stance first, his footwork will only need to do half the work.

Sports.title: Dan Rafael Not Buying February 6 Ryan Garcia vs. Floyd Mayweather Talk
Sports.content:
Dan Rafael isn’t buying Ryan Garcia’s claim that he’ll face Floyd Mayweather on February 6. While Garcia threw that date out during an appearance on N3on’s stream, Rafael notes that Garcia’s team is already deep into negotiations for a February matchup against Teofimo Lopez.

“I don’t believe it,” Rafael said regarding the February 6 date. “They’re far, far down the road, his team with Teofimo’s team, about making the match for February.”

That doesn’t mean Rafael rules out a Garcia vs. Mayweather bout entirely for down the road. The financial upside is massive, and it would pit Garcia against a 49-year-old who hasn’t had an official professional bout since stopping Conor McGregor in 2017. Mayweather has stayed busy with exhibitions in the years since, though stepping into the ring with a reigning welterweight champion is a completely different test.

The idea of Mayweather fighting for Garcia’s title isn’t completely out of left field, especially since the WBC appears open to sanctioning it. Rafael pointed out that the organization could grant an exception given Mayweather’s long history in WBC championship fights, which explains how he could land a title shot after nearly ten years out of official competition. Even so, it remains tough to see why Garcia would lock in February 6 against Mayweather when his camp is so close to finalizing things with Lopez.

As for Lopez’s side of the equation, Rafael expects him to vacate his WBA title if forced to choose between a mandatory defense against Jack Catterall or the Garcia fight. Rafael shared that take prior to the WBA’s ruling while acknowledging Lopez could always have a change of heart. Still, the math is easy to understand. Facing Garcia brings in far more money, even if dropping the belt means losing the marketing angle of a unification bout.

Dropping Mayweather’s name certainly succeeded in generating buzz around February 6. However, the real story is the serious progress Garcia’s camp has already made toward locking in a different opponent for that exact same month.

Sports.title: WBA Ruling Leaves Teofimo Lopez With Zero Leverage for Garcia
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez painted himself into a corner at welterweight, and the WBA’s November 11 decision to uphold Jack Catterall’s mandatory status just stripped away his biggest bargaining chip. Lopez now has 10 days to either strike a deal with Catterall or surrender the belt he won from Rolly Romero in August. Either path leaves him in a weakened spot.

The biggest hit comes at the negotiating table. Lopez wants WBC champion Ryan Garcia in early 2027, with February 6 floated as a target date. Walking into those talks as a fellow champion gave Lopez standing to push for a fair purse split in a two-belt unification. Without the WBA title, Lopez becomes a belt-less challenger who lacks the massive social media reach and box-office pull that Garcia commands. Garcia’s side would immediately treat him as the B-side and squeeze his percentage.

Dropping the belt also carries a steep hit to his reputation. Vacating a title less than three months after winning it—right after losing an appeal to bypass a mandatory—looks like a textbook duck. Catterall has already called on Lopez to either fight or vacate, and fans will view a decision to drop the strap as Lopez running from another slick southpaw after Shakur Stevenson swept him 119–109 at 140 pounds. Worse yet, Lopez could vacate his title only to watch Garcia walk away toward a rumored February 6 matchup with Floyd Mayweather.

Teofimo Lopez plans to appeal the WBA’s ruling that he must defend his title against Jack Catterall, sources told @SInow. Lopez’s team says they filed a request for permission to fight in a title unification with Ryan Garcia on 11/5. A copy of that request was reviewed by SI. — Chris Mannix (@SIChrisMannix) November 12, 2026

Staying to defend the belt brings its own headaches. Catterall has refused to step aside, and his awkward, counter-punching southpaw style is built to make aggressive fighters overreach. Even if Lopez edges out an ugly decision over 12 rounds, a flat performance hurts his market value before a Garcia fight. If Catterall pulls off the upset, the eight-figure Garcia payday vanishes completely.

Lopez’s team claims it filed a special permit request on November 5 to keep the unification alive, though the WBA stated it had no formal application on file when it ruled. Unless the sanctioning body reverses course over that paperwork dispute, Lopez is stuck choosing between a stylistic spoiler in the ring or a major financial haircut outside of it.

Sports.title: WBA Orders Floyd Schofield to Face José Valenzuela
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield has until December 11 to finalize a bout with José Valenzuela after the WBA ordered the lightweight titleholder to make his first mandatory defense. Valenzuela’s southpaw counterpunching presents a tricky stylistic puzzle for Schofield, who captured the belt on October 10 and thrives when he can close the gap in a hurry.

The sanctioning body opened a 30-day negotiation window on November 11. If both sides fail to agree on terms by the close of business on December 11, or if either camp declines to negotiate, the WBA Championships Committee can send the fight to a purse bid. No date or venue was included in the initial ruling.

Schofield’s hand and foot speed give him a clear path to seizing early control. The real challenge lies in his exits. Valenzuela is comfortable yielding space as an opponent rushes in, waiting for Schofield to plant his feet before firing his straight left. Should Schofield linger in the pocket after finishing a combination, Valenzuela will have clean looks to answer before the champion can reset.

To disrupt Valenzuela’s timing, Schofield will need to vary his level of commitment on the way in. Snapping a quick jab to the chest can score points while forcing Valenzuela to reveal his defensive reads. Feints can trigger that left hand early and give Schofield room to step inside behind it.Making those subtle adjustments would allow him to control the tempo without overextending on every entry.

On the other side, Valenzuela has to decide how much real estate he is willing to surrender. If he becomes too patient while hunting for the counter, Schofield can score with single lead shots and angle out before the return fire arrives. Valenzuela’s strongest moments will come when he baits Schofield into leading, tags him at the tail end of an exchange, and immediately presses forward to deny the champion room to reset. Catching Schofield with that left hand early would make the young titleholder second-guess every subsequent entry.

In issuing the order, the WBA referenced Rule C.11, which mandates that a champion defend against the designated official challenger, alongside Rule C.12, which restricts voluntary opponents within 60 days of a mandatory deadline. Both teams now have a month to hammer out a deal before the committee steps in to force a bid.

This first mandatory test will measure how effectively Schofield can weaponize his speed against a fighter content to wait for him to overcommit. While the champion can bank rounds by striking first, he may be forced to dial back his aggression and make Valenzuela initiate if the challenger consistently gets the final word in their exchanges.

Sports.title: Arnold Barboza Jr vs. Oscar Duarte Set for Jan. 23 in Anaheim
Sports.content:
Arnold Barboza Jr. and Oscar Duarte are set to meet on January 23 in Anaheim, California, in a junior welterweight bout built around a classic clash of styles. Golden Boy Promotions announced the date and location during the WBC convention, according to reporter Darshan Desai.

The Anaheim card is also expected to showcase top junior middleweight talent. WBC number one contender Brandon Adams is slated to appear in either an interim title bout or a final eliminator, alongside fellow contender Charles Conwell. Specific venues and opponents for the undercard fighters have not yet been revealed.

For Barboza, the biggest danger against a relentless pressure fighter like Duarte lies in his defensive exits. Barboza has the tools to score consistently with his jab and crisp combinations, yet retreating in a straight line will allow Duarte to march right behind him and force him against the ropes.

Lateral movement is the key adjustment here. Every time Barboza pivots off the center line after landing a punch, Duarte is forced to reset his feet and start his attack from scratch. How well Barboza maintains that spatial discipline will dictate whether this fight happens at his preferred distance or in a phone booth.

Duarte’s path to victory depends on cutting off the ring with patience rather than reckless aggression. Charging in from the outside gives Barboza plenty of time to read the attack and fire counters before Duarte is even set to punch. Instead, Duarte needs to inch forward behind a tight guard until he is close enough to target the midsection.

Barboza is slick enough to slip wide hooks upstairs, but his torso remains an accessible target when he leans back. Investing in heavy body work early will pay major dividends by slowing Barboza’s legs and making it much harder for him to escape the ropes in the second half of the fight.

Meanwhile, Barboza cannot afford to rely purely on defense to win rounds. While his jab and straight right hand can punish Duarte for overreaching, making an aggressive opponent miss is rarely enough on the scorecards if the aggressor is landing the harder, more eye-catching shots during brief exchanges on the inside. Barboza must throw enough volume to bank rounds decisively.

This makes the opening stanzas crucial for setting the physical terms of the night. If Barboza establishes his jab and glides back to open canvas after every exchange, Duarte will burn tremendous energy just trying to close the gap. Conversely, if Duarte traps Barboza on the perimeter within the first three rounds, Barboza will be dragged into heavy trenches he would much rather avoid.

Further down the bill, the stakes for Brandon Adams hinge entirely on the sanctioning body’s final ruling. Depending on how the WBC structures the matchup, Adams will walk into Anaheim fighting either for an interim championship belt or for the mandatory challenger spot that guarantees a future shot at the full world title.

Sports.title: Can Josh Kelly’s Speed Solve Jaron Ennis in Atlanta Unification?
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly pulled off his title win over Bakhram Murtazaliev by picking his spots with surgical precision. He’s going to need every ounce of that timing when he steps in with Jaron “Boots” Ennis on February 27, 2027, for a three-belt junior middleweight unification at State Farm Arena in Atlanta.

Matchroom just made it official: Ennis (36-0, 32 KOs) is putting his WBA and WBO belts on the line against IBF champion Kelly (19-1-1, 9 KOs) in the promoter’s first-ever show in Atlanta. Fans in the U.S. can catch the action on TNT, truTV, and DAZN, while DAZN will stream it everywhere else around the globe.

Ennis grabbed his two 154-pound straps by stopping Xander Zayas in seven rounds at Barclays Center last June, picking up right where he left off after unifying at welterweight against Eimantas Stanionis the year before. Meanwhile, Kelly upset Murtazaliev in Newcastle back in January to win the IBF belt and successfully defended it against Caoimhin Agyarko in July.

Against Murtazaliev, Kelly showed he knows how to frustrate a dangerous puncher into long stretches of inactivity, baiting leads and resetting the pace after landing his own counter. The problem is that Ennis brings a completely different kind of speed in the split second right after an exchange. Boots closes the gap in a flash, switches stances mid-combination, and unloads before you even have a chance to reset your feet.

Kelly’s best shot is to make Ennis pay early every time the Philly star marches forward. A crisp counter on the way in can buy Kelly just enough breathing room to angle out and force Ennis to start over from the outside. If Kelly backs straight up after throwing, Ennis will happily walk him to the ropes and start tearing up the body. Once Kelly gets pinned there, climbing back out to his preferred range gets awfully tough.

“I’ve waited a very long time to prove myself at the highest level, finally I have that moment!” Kelly said.

Even if Kelly stays off the ropes all night, he still has a scorecard problem to solve. Ennis can steal a quiet round with a three-second burst that gives the judges plenty of clean, eye-catching shots to remember. Kelly definitely has the hand speed to catch Ennis coming in, so how often he dares to pull the trigger between those flurries will decide just how competitive this fight gets.

Whoever leaves Atlanta with their hand raised will hold three of the four major belts at 154 pounds. WBC champion Sebastian Fundora still holds the fourth piece of the puzzle, though Matchroom’s announcement didn’t include any deal for him to fight the winner. Ennis and Kelly will get their first look at each other this Friday at a kickoff press conference in Los Angeles.

Sports.title: The Three Kings: Shakur, Devin, And Ryan Keep Fumbling The Crown
Sports.content:
Currently, world champions Shakur Stevenson, Devin Haney, and Ryan Garcia are the premier boxing names, but each time one of the stars gets in position to assume the role of the king, they end up fumbling the crown.

Back in 2023, Gervonta “Tank” Davis, Teofimo Lopez, Devin Haney, and Ryan Garcia were tagged with the moniker “The Four Kings.” All four boxers have achieved success, but the landscape has experienced a slight shift.

As of now, Shakur Stevenson, Devin Haney, and Ryan Garcia are the Top Dogs. From lightweight all the way up to welterweight, many hungry boxers have placed these top names on their radars.

In past decades, fight fans witnessed the Mike Tyson Era, the Roy Jones Jr. Era, the Floyd “Money” Mayweather Era, and the Canelo Era. With the current crop of talent, we’re still waiting for one of them to step up and claim this time period.

After outpointing Vasiliy Lomachenko, Devin Haney moved up to super-lightweight, defeated Regis Prograis, and won the WBC title. In his next fight, Haney was dropped three times by Ryan Garcia and lost via majority decision.

A month later, the New York State Athletic Commission overturned the win to a no-contest because Garcia tested positive for ostarine. Haney would go on to move up to welterweight, outpoint Brian Norman Jr., and win the WBO world title.

Instead of immediately following up on the big November 2025 victory, Haney wasted most of 2026 having a Twitter battle with Shakur Stevenson. It would have made more sense for Devin to rematch Ryan or fight Rolly Romero.

Shakur Stevenson looked spectacular in January 2026 when he thoroughly outclassed Teofimo Lopez and won the WBO super-lightweight title. The boxing pundits praised Shakur’s performance, and they were ready to crown him.

Unfortunately, Shakur fumbled the crown by being inactive for the remainder of 2026. Shakur Stevenson wasted a considerable amount of time going back and forth with Devin Haney over two pounds.

At one point in October, it seemed like Stevenson and Haney agreed to fight at 145, and then suddenly, the negotiations stalled. Shakur could have claimed the crown by defeating Haney at 147 and becoming a five-division world champion.

After losing to Rolly Romero, Ryan Garcia bounced back by scoring a unanimous decision victory over Mario Barrios. With the win, Garcia became the new WBC world welterweight champion.

Seven months later, in September 2026, Garcia looked extremely impressive as he stopped Conor Benn in the second round. The victory put Garcia in position to grab that elusive crown.

According to media reports, it appears as if Garcia is going to fumble the crown by placing himself in a lose-lose situation. If Garcia loses to Floyd Mayweather, he’s going to get trolled.

If he defeats Mayweather, nobody is going to give him credit for beating a 50-year-old man. Garcia has more eye-catching options such as Teofimo Lopez, a rematch with Devin Haney, or avenging the loss he suffered against Rolly Romero.

Once upon a time, star boxers used to thrive on claiming ownership of a particular time period. Those days appear to be gone because nowadays, it seems like none of the elite boxers want to step up and take ownership of this current era.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Faces Jadier Herrera’s Power March 13
Sports.content:
William Zepeda will defend his WBC lightweight championship against interim titleholder Jadier Herrera in Mexico on March 13, 2027, according to ESPN’s Salvador Rodríguez. Herrera easily carries the rawest punch Zepeda has encountered in the pro ranks.

Still, Ricardo Núñez sent the Cuban southpaw to the canvas in the opening frame of their clash, exposing technical cracks before Herrera managed to close the show in the eighth round.

Boasting 16 knockouts across 18 bouts, the 24-year-old proved that a single blow can bail him out of trouble. Yet the nature of that knockdown against Núñez highlights a glaring liability. Núñez baited Herrera late in the first round by faking low with the left, drawing Herrera’s eyes down before looping a clean right hand upstairs. That willingness to bite on basic level-change feints could prove fatal against Zepeda, whose entire offense is built around digging to the beltline before detonating hooks around a dropping guard.

Surviving the Storm Before the Stoppage

While Herrera recovered from only the second knockdown of his career by relying on jabs and forward pressure to halt Núñez in round eight, surviving Zepeda demands a far tighter defensive shell. Relying on dramatic second-half rescues rarely works against an engine that throws 80 to 100 punches per frame. Herrera cannot afford to spend minutes waiting for the perfect counter while Zepeda piles up triple-digit punch totals.

Zepeda shines deepest into his sequences. He crowds the pocket, alternates targets between ribs and chin, and continues firing even when his rival shells up. Herrera’s clearest route to slowing that machine is timing his counters directly between the incoming shots. Catching the champion cleanly during the level-change from head to body could make Zepeda hesitate before launching extended combinations.

With both men operating from the southpaw stance, Zepeda anticipates an aggressive challenger. The champion noted in remarks to the WBC that Herrera comes forward rather than circling away. Holding real estate in the center of the ring gives Herrera punch-for-punch trades, but it leaves him vulnerable to the exact high-low sequences that made him vulnerable against Núñez.

A single sharp counter might steal a frame for Herrera if it rattles Zepeda and yields room to follow up. Yet if Zepeda simply absorbs the shot and resumes digging to the liver, Herrera risks landing the prettiest single punch while dropping the round on raw work rate. Núñez troubled him with basic feints; Zepeda will amplify that pressure exponentially from the opening bell.

Rodríguez added that the WBC plans to mandate two lightweight eliminators featuring its top available contenders, though specific pairings remain unconfirmed. Herrera has his title shot locked down, and the opening rounds will reveal whether his vaunted power can keep Zepeda off him or if his defensive lapses will cut the night short.

Ghana News.title: South Africa rethinks online gambling through strict digital enforcement and stronger consumer protection
Ghana News.content:
The era of hands-off gambling regulation in South Africa is over. With the market generating R75 billion in gross gambling revenue on R1.5 trillion in total turnover, the stakes are too high for the status quo. In 2026, the national strategy is clear: regulate through digital platforms, not just around them. That means sharper legal definitions, enforceable digital controls, and consumer protection tools that reflect a market moving at the speed of technology.

Growing Need for Clear Information

You know how it feels when every second ad on your phone is pushing some casino offer? That's basically the South African market right now, saturated with offshore operators reaching consumers through social media, SMS, and influencers. In that kind of noise, telling a legal sportsbook from an illegal casino gets genuinely difficult for the average person. That's precisely why accessible, straightforward information has become essential.

Players need practical guidance on local laws, platform security, and which operators actually comply with South African regulations. Resources like Casino.com in South Africa serve this purpose directly, functioning as comparison and review platforms that help users assess their options before committing real money. In an environment where the most attractive offer is often the least legitimate, informed decision-making is the first line of defence.

Digital Platforms and Consumer Empowerment

The way South Africans gamble has changed. Mobile apps and web platforms have replaced physical betting shops as the primary point of access, and regulators have been forced to rethink their entire approach. Punishing offenders after the fact is no longer enough. The priority now is equipping consumers with the knowledge and tools to protect themselves from the start.

The NGB's Verified Gambling Operators Portal, which went live in April 2026, is the centrepiece of this effort. It allows anyone to instantly check whether a bookmaker holds a legitimate provincial licence, removing the ambiguity that unlicensed operators have relied on for years.

The contrast between licensed and unlicensed platforms could not be starker. Offshore and unregulated sites operate without any obligation to South African provincial standards. They may refuse to honour payouts, skip mandatory FICA identity and age checks, and store user data without adequate security measures. On top of that, the law treats any winnings from these platforms as potentially unlawful, meaning they can be forfeited entirely.

The message to players is simple and non-negotiable: check operators through the verified portal before signing up, complete FICA promptly on any legal platform, and take advantage of every available responsible gambling safeguard.

The Push for Regulatory Clarity

The local market spent years operating in a grey area regarding the legality of interactive gambling. That’s no longer the case—the boundaries are becoming much sharper now. Online sports betting is fully legal when offered by operators holding a valid provincial bookmaker’s licence, with major brands operating securely under frameworks governed by authorities such as the Western Cape Gambling and Racing Board and the Gauteng Gambling Board.

It’s a different picture for interactive casino-style games. Online slots, roulette, and blackjack remain strictly prohibited under Section 11 of the National Gambling Act of 2004. The National Gambling Board moved decisively in 2026 to close remaining loopholes, directing provincial authorities to stop authorising remote servers for products disguised as “betting on contingencies.”

Meanwhile, the Remote Gambling Bill, which could eventually establish a national licensing framework for all remote gaming, continues progressing slowly toward a possible 2027 implementation. Right now, the priority is clarifying exactly what’s currently permitted.

Crackdown on Illegal Platforms

South Africa’s regulators have shifted from warnings to concrete digital enforcement. In mid-2026, the National Gambling Board issued an Expression of Interest for technology providers capable of monitoring, tracking, blocking and reporting illegal online gambling websites. Industry estimates put the unlicensed and offshore share of the online market at roughly 62 percent, involving around 16 million users and more than R50 billion in annual gross gambling revenue that generates no local tax.

The NGB has also engaged Google, Meta and the communications regulator, requested assistance with IP-address blocking, issued cease-and-desist notices to operators based in Curaçao, Malta, Gibraltar and the Philippines, and supported joint raids by a new Illegal Gambling Task Team. These steps signal that the era of easy access for unlicensed digital platforms is ending.

Proposed National Tax and Policy Momentum

Pressure on the fiscal and legislative fronts is increasing alongside enforcement. National Treasury has suggested a 20 percent national tax on gross gambling revenue from the online sector, layered on top of current provincial levies. Consultation ended in early 2026, and the proposal remains under consideration. Parallel efforts by the National Gambling Policy Council and a specialised Gambling Technical Committee are advancing a wider Bill to address online gambling issues.

Together, the steps aim to reclaim lost revenue, reduce social harm and establish a more coherent national framework, making it clear that only licensed and tax-compliant platforms will be accepted over the long run.

Ghana News.title: No new taxes in 2027 Budget – Ampem Nyarko
Ghana News.content:
Thomas Nyarko Ampem

Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Ampem Nyarko has hinted that no new taxes will be introduced in the 2027 Budget.

Mr. Nyarko gave the indication ahead of the presentation of the New Economy Budget on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

According to him, the government does not intend to impose any new taxes on Ghanaians in the 2027 fiscal year.

Ahead of the budget presentation, the Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry, for instance, warned that it would oppose any fresh tax impositions on businesses.

The Chamber wants the government to instead expand the tax net and strengthen compliance to help achieve its revenue targets.

Currently, the effective VAT rate is 20%, the highest personal income tax rate is 35%, while the general corporate income tax rate is 25%.

The Budget presentation on Thursday is expected to provide greater clarity on the government's revenue targets and how it intends to achieve them without introducing new taxes or increasing existing tax rates.

Ghana News.title: Six MDs in eight years weakened TOR – Managing Director
Ghana News.content:
Managing Director of TOR, Edmond Kombat.

Frequent changes at the top of the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) during the eight years of the previous administration undermined management stability and made it difficult to address the facility’s deep-rooted operational problems, the refinery’s Managing Director, Edmond Kombat, has said.

He said the refinery went through six managing directors and an interim management committee under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, leaving successive management teams with limited time to implement decisions and deliver lasting improvements.

Mr Kombat said the repeated changes, at a time when TOR was not refining crude oil, contributed to the uncertainty that affected the state-owned facility.

In an interview on Wednesday, November 11, he argued that turning around a refinery with complex technical and financial challenges required consistent leadership and a sustained management approach.

“In eight years, they had six managing directors, including an interim management committee. And an IMC of three personnel. So let’s say roughly seven MDs. You see that the turnover was very short,” he said on Channel One TV.

“They were not refining, and I think they had an instability in leadership.”

Mr Kombat also identified the failure to produce independently audited financial statements over several years as a major weakness in the refinery’s governance and management.

He said the absence of audited accounts made it difficult to establish a clear picture of the company’s financial position and compounded the challenges facing successive management teams.

“I think they didn’t really have a lot of time to make decisions. And then an audited account just piled up. It was a management account, not an independently audited account,” he said.

He disclosed that the current management had worked with the Ghana Audit Service to clear the backlog, auditing the refinery’s accounts for the seven-year period.

The management had also convened an annual general meeting to consider the accounts covering 2017 to 2025, he added.

Beyond the management and accounting challenges, Mr Kombat said doubts about TOR’s commercial viability within the previous administration had also raised questions about the future of the refinery.

He said some officials at the Ministry of Energy had reportedly considered converting the facility into a tank farm or handing it over for alternative use rather than maintaining its refining operations.

“There are indications that some of the people in the government at the Energy Ministry didn’t really believe that TOR was viable. So there was this argument about either making it a tank farm or probably giving it out,” he said.

Mr Kombat, however, maintained that TOR remained a valuable national asset whose capacity should not be overlooked in discussions about its future.

He cited its storage capacity of one million metric tonnes, which he said was about three times that of the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company (BOST), as well as its ability to process 45,000 barrels of crude oil per stream day.

“If you have a refinery like this, the refinery of TOR, the storage is one million metric tons; it’s like three times that of BOST, and you have a refinery that is 45,000 capacity,” he said.

He said the task before the current management was to consolidate the refinery’s recovery and ensure that subsequent leadership teams maintained the gains rather than allowing another cycle of instability to derail its progress.

Ghana News.title: Facing our past and shaping our future together – British High Commissioner to Ghana Dr. Christian Rogg writes
Ghana News.content:
Britain and Ghana cannot change the past, but we can face it honestly, listen carefully and strengthen a modern partnership founded on dignity and mutual respect.

A few weeks ago, I sat in Ghana’s National Theatre and watched The Darkest Chapter, a moving play by Latif Abubakar. It traces a path from the horrors of the transatlantic slave trade through decolonisation and independence to modern Ghana. One line has

stayed with me: “before diplomacy, before policy, before resolutions, there were human beings”.

That is where any conversation about the slave trade must begin. With the millions of people torn from their homes, families and communities. With those whose labour and suffering enriched others. And with the descendants and societies that continue to live with that history today.

The transatlantic slave trade was a brutal and barbaric violation. People were denied their humanity, separated from their families, treated as property and worked to their deaths. The UK Prime Minister has expressed his “sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions of people” and recognised the way this history “still shapes our world today.”

Ghana has helped ensure that the world does not look away. Its leadership in shining a spotlight on the slave trade has brought renewed attention to questions that are difficult, deeply felt and important. Ghana’s perspectives have helped shape the wider

Commonwealth conversation.

At the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) last week, Commonwealth leaders agreed that the time had come for a meaningful, truthful and respectful conversation to forge a common future based on equity. They welcomed

the UK Government’s agreement to engage in a structured, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties, addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms. The Prime Minister also met with President Mahama

during CHOGM to set out these plans and welcomed the President’s support.

This is an important step, and the United Kingdom enters the dialogue seriously and respectfully. Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of the process, and the Prime Minister has said that he is open

to them. A dialogue of this importance must allow those most affected to help shape it. Its outcome should not be predetermined, but neither should the depth or difficulty of the conversation be underestimated. The first responsibility is to listen.

One of the privileges of serving as British High Commissioner is gaining a view of the many layers of the UK’s and Ghana’s shared history. At the British Museum this summer, I saw how one object, the Asante Ewer, can tell a story spanning medieval

England, trans-Saharan trade, Asante ceremonial life and the violence and pillage of the Anglo-Asante wars. Such objects do not offer simple stories.

They ask us to confront complexity and understand what they mean to different communities.

Other moments remind us how relationships can change. Last year at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park, I stood with the Duke of Edinburgh before the image of Queen Elizabeth II dancing with President Kwame Nkrumah in Accra in 1961. Ghana

had won its independence only four years earlier and was inspiring movements across Africa. That photograph captured our countries’ relationship being reshaped at a decisive moment.

Today, the United Kingdom and Ghana meet as sovereign partners. Our relationship is rooted not only in history, but in people, education, culture, business, security and a shared interest in prosperity. That modern partnership gives us a strong foundation for difficult conversations. We should be confident enough to discuss both progress and pain, allow space for honest disagreement, and recognise that listening is part of an equal partnership.

As Ghana approaches its 70th anniversary of independence, there will be many opportunities to reflect on the journey from colonial rule to the Black Star of Africa, and on Ghana’s continuing influence in the world. The United Kingdom should take part in

those conversations with humility, openness and respect.

We gather to remember. We also need to listen. The dialogue agreed at CHOGM will not be simple, and there will be strongly held views. But our bilateral relationship is mature enough to face difficult history honestly, to hear each other with respect and to work together towards a common future based on dignity and equity.

Ghana News.title: Industry, manufacturing must drive 2027 Budget — Awuah
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Association of Bankers, John Awuah, says lending to the private sector has increased by more than 30 per cent over the past year, but has challenged the government to use the 2027 Budget to stimulate demand for credit by supporting viable businesses and productive sectors.

He said the banking industry was seeing increased lending activity, with interest rates also easing, although the availability of bankable projects remained a major concern.

Mr Awuah said the challenge facing the economy was not necessarily a shortage of funds in the banking system, but whether enough viable businesses and projects existed to attract financing and generate wider economic activity.

Speaking on the PM Express programme on Joy News on Wednesday, November 11, ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, he cited Bank of Ghana data showing that credit to the private sector had expanded by more than 30 per cent between the previous year and this year.

“I am quite surprised to hear that there is no money in the system,” he said, pointing to the growth in lending as evidence that banks were actively supporting businesses.

He said lending rates had also declined from levels above 20 per cent to about 15 per cent, with some borrowers receiving offers at rates as low as 9.5 per cent.

Those developments, he said, indicated that banks were increasingly prepared to extend credit, although access to financing would also depend on the quality and viability of projects presented to them.

Budget must stimulate productive activity

Mr Awuah said the 2027 Budget should help direct lending towards sectors capable of expanding production, creating jobs and increasing household incomes.

He identified industry and manufacturing as areas that required greater attention, arguing that investment in those sectors could have benefits beyond the businesses receiving loans.

He explained that the expansion of factories and manufacturing operations would create employment, put more income into the hands of workers and stimulate demand for goods and services.

Workers with regular incomes, he said, would have greater capacity to spend at markets such as Kantamanto and other trading centres, helping to improve business activity across the economy.

“If the Budget is directed towards industry and manufacturing, and we get a lot more people on the factory floors, these are all people who will be consuming, who will be going to Kantamanto and the like to purchase,” he said.

He suggested that such an approach could help address concerns among traders about weak customer spending by improving employment and purchasing power.

The bankable projects challenge

However, Mr Awuah said increased lending and lower interest rates would not automatically translate into stronger business investment if there were insufficient projects capable of meeting banks' financing requirements.

He said the government needed to address the conditions that would encourage businesses to develop viable projects and attract investment.

“Do we have sufficient bankable projects for the banks to lend to? And that is the question, the multi-million-dollar question, that we want the Minister to answer for us tomorrow,” he said.

His comments come as businesses and financial sector stakeholders look to the 2027 Budget for measures to strengthen the link between banking-sector liquidity, private-sector investment and economic growth.

While the expansion in private-sector credit suggests increased lending activity, the ability of businesses to turn available finance into productive investment will remain important.

For Mr Awuah, the task before government is to create the conditions for more investment in industry and manufacturing, so that bank lending translates into jobs, higher incomes and stronger demand across the economy.

Ghana News.title: AKSA bribery claims: Parliament finds no evidence against MPs, staff
Ghana News.content:
Parliament has found no evidence that any Member of Parliament or officer of the Parliamentary Service received money allegedly paid to influence the approval of the 2015 AKSA emergency power agreement.

The finding follows an internal administrative review commissioned by the Speaker of Parliament, Alban S.K. Bagbin, into allegations that about $46,000 was paid to individuals associated with the House in connection with the agreement.

However, the Speaker has made it clear that the outcome does not establish that no bribes were paid or absolve anyone who may have received such payments.

Addressing Parliament on Wednesday, Mr Bagbin said the report, together with supporting documents, would be forwarded to the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) and other relevant investigative agencies for further examination.

The referral is expected to provide investigators with information gathered from Parliament’s records and interviews conducted during the administrative exercise.

The controversy is linked to the conviction in the United States of Asante Kwaku Berko, a former Goldman Sachs employee, for his role in facilitating bribe payments to Ghanaian officials.

Berko is awaiting sentencing in the case, which relates to the development and financing of a power generation project in Ghana by Turkish energy company AKSA.

Mr Bagbin said the review was intended to establish the circumstances surrounding Parliament’s consideration and approval of the agreement, identify those who took part in the process and determine what relevant information the institution could provide to assist investigations.

The exercise involved an examination of parliamentary records, including the Votes and Proceedings, official reports, committee documents, the report of the Committee on Mines and Energy and the resolution by which the House approved the agreement.

Some former and serving officers of the Parliamentary Service, as well as a former chairperson of the Committee on Mines and Energy, were also interviewed.

According to the Speaker, neither the documentary evidence nor the interviews established that an MP or a Parliamentary Service officer received the alleged payments.

He cautioned, however, against treating the findings as a final determination of the bribery allegations.

The review, he explained, was administrative in nature and did not have the authority to compel witnesses to appear, take evidence under oath or demand the production of documents.

It also did not have access to bank records, financial transactions or communications outside the custody of Parliament.

Mr Bagbin said the exercise was therefore not a criminal investigation and could not establish the guilt or innocence of any person implicated in the matter.

He maintained that the responsibility for investigating financial transactions and other evidence beyond Parliament’s reach rested with the appropriate law enforcement agencies.

The Speaker said the transmission of the report to the OSP and other relevant bodies was intended to enable them to pursue any further inquiries considered necessary.

Ghana News.title: Police seize 3,752 slabs of suspected Indian hemp at Ada
Ghana News.content:
The Tema Regional Police Command has intercepted a canoe carrying 3,752 slabs of suspected Indian hemp during an intelligence-led operation on the Volta Lake at Ada in the Greater Accra Region.

The suspects transporting the consignment escaped after being intercepted by Marine Police personnel on November 4, 2026, abandoning the canoe and its contents.

The recovered items included 53 sacks containing the suspected narcotic substances, two outboard motors, 30 yellow gallons of petrol and premix fuel, a cutlass and other articles.

According to a police statement issued on Wednesday, November 11, the operation followed intelligence that a consignment of suspected narcotic drugs was being transported from Jemeniweres through the Volta Lake towards Ada.

Marine Police officers initially proceeded to Mepe in the Volta Region, but discovered on arrival that the suspects had fled in their canoes.

The team subsequently moved to Big Ada to pursue them.

At about 11.10 p.m., the officers intercepted the suspects at Agorta Island, Ada. However, the individuals managed to escape into the river, leaving their canoe behind.

The police retrieved the vessel and transported it, together with its contents, to the Marine Police Base at Ada.

A subsequent search of the 53 sacks at the Regional Criminal Investigations Department (CID) in Tema on November 5 revealed 3,752 compressed and cello-taped slabs of dried leaves suspected to be Indian hemp.

The suspected narcotics have been secured as exhibits pending examination.

No arrests yet

The police said no arrests had been made in connection with the seizure, but investigations were continuing to identify and apprehend those involved.

The Tema Regional Police Command has urged members of the public to provide credible information to support efforts to combat drug trafficking.

The seizure forms part of the command's efforts to disrupt the transportation of suspected narcotic substances through waterways in the region.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
