World.title: United Nigeria Airlines, NCS Kick-off Initiative to Fight Cancer
World.content:
*United Nigeria MD recalls how he survived cancer, lost 2 sisters to disease

Chinedu Eze

United Nigeria Airlines (UNA) and the Nigerian Cancer Society (NCS) have launched the ‘United Against Cancer’ initiative to help create awareness for the early detection and treatment of cancer.

Speaking at the press briefing in the airline’s Lagos office yesterday, United Nigeria Airlines’ Managing Director, Mazi Osita Okonkwo, said the airline’s position is that the fight against cancer must begin with early detection.

Sharing his own experience, he said he is a cancer survivor and also lost two sisters to the disease and does not shy away from talking about it because telling the story gives hope to people who may be facing the disease or who may think a diagnosis is a death sentence.

For the initiative, he said the first level of the campaign will focus on early-stage prevention, a large-scale awareness drive and the sharing of information. The second level addresses cancers that are not caught early and need treatment.

“We have heard the news, and we have seen people who have been affected by this deadly disease. It is on that basis that United Nigeria has decided to work with the Nigerian Cancer Society in a special way to mount a campaign against cancer in Nigeria. We have looked at the programmes and activities of the Society, and we are very happy with them. We believe they need to be supported, not only by United Nigeria Airlines through the United Nigeria Airlines Foundation but also by the passengers who fly with us and book tickets on our platform.

“Our passengers would have the oppourtunity to contribute to the fight against cancer in a very simple but unique, innovative way. You book a ticket and have the option to make a voluntary contribution on our platform. You can give as little as N1,000, N2,000, N5,000, N100,000, and so on. That is the first stage of the campaign. All the money and donations raised will go directly to the Society, into an account designated by the Society for this purpose.

“The second level is that some cancers will not be caught at that early stage, and those patients will need treatment. Successful treatments have been recorded across the board. This is also a personal matter for some of us. I mentioned that we have our own personal stories. I am a cancer survivor myself. I also lost two sisters to cancer; both were victims of this deadly disease. We are not shy about talking about it, because when you tell the story, it gives hope to someone who may be facing this problem or who may think it is a death sentence. It is not,” Mazi Okonkwo said.

Mazi Okonkwo said United Nigeria Airlines has committed to making its platform and flights available to the Society, not only to raise money but also to raise awareness about the disease. UNA’s cabin crew will lead the campaign on board, making announcements and engaging passengers directly. Passengers will find information in the seat pockets in front of them, and co-branded materials will appear at check-in counters.

Speaking at the event, NCS President Prof. Abidemi Omonisi, a pathologist, described the partnership as an important intervention in addressing the funding challenges facing cancer care in Nigeria.

He commended the airline for taking the initiative and noted that the programme was conceived and driven by UNA as part of its corporate social responsibility.

Prof. Omonisi stressed the financial burden that cancer places on families. He described it as a catastrophic illness capable of impoverishing even wealthy households.

“Advanced therapies like immunotherapy can cost up to N50 million and rural patients often face transport costs and temporary housing in major cities, which can force them to abandon treatment partway through. He said the funds raised through the airline’s platform will directly support nationwide early screening, diagnostic assistance and treatment for indigent patients in urban centres and underserved rural communities,” he said.

Omonisi also noted that the greatest gains lie in early detection, stating that patients diagnosed at early stages have better chances of successful treatment, and organised national screening, adding that the most critical way to save lives in developing nations is through early detection.

He, however, cautioned against one-off screening exercises that identify positive cases without providing continuous patient support, leaving people abandoned.

Omonisi, therefor, called for sustained health education and community outreach to dispel myths, such as mistaking early breast cancer symptoms for minor boils or attributing tumours to spiritual attacks.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu Directs Ondo APC Leaders to Work With Aiyedatiwa, Says Gov is State Campaign Coordinator
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has directed all leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ondo State to come under Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa as he is the Coordinator of the party’s campaigns in the state, and work together for a victorious presidential election in January.

The President also charged Aiyedatiwa to open his doors to all party leaders and give them opportunities to play active roles in the campaigns.

He stressed the need for unity and genuine reconciliation among members ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections.

The directives were conveyed by the Senate Majority Leader and Deputy Director-General (South) of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, at the party’s presidential campaign rally held at the Akure Township Stadium, on Wednesday

Bamidele said Tinubu gave him two major messages for the people and political leaders of Ondo State, with the first focusing on the need for party cohesion and recognition of the governor’s leadership of the campaign.

“The appeal of Mr President is that all our leaders should recognise that there is only one state coordinator for this campaign.

“The state coordinator for this campaign is the governor of the state, and everybody must work with him,” he said.

He, however, said the governor must also accommodate all leaders and stakeholders, adding that the President wanted every influential member of the party to be involved in the campaign.

“The President also asked me to emphasise to the state coordinator, Governor Aiyedatiwa, that he must open his door to all the leaders of the party to work with him,” Bamidele said.

He urged the party leadership to sustain the reconciliation achieved after the last governorship election, saying the forthcoming poll was a presidential and National Assembly election, not a governorship contest.

“The President also said I should remind all of you that this election is about him. It is his own election. The election we are holding in Ondo State in January is not a governorship election,” he said.

Bamidele called for the inclusion of all party leaders in the campaign structure, specifically mentioning former Governor Olusegun Mimiko and other political stakeholders who had returned to the APC fold.

He said the party must provide opportunities for leaders from different political tendencies and senatorial districts to contribute meaningfully to the campaign.

The Senate leader said Aiyedatiwa had promised to deliver at least one million votes for Tinubu in the state, noting that the target would require cooperation among party leaders.

He added that the President’s second message was a call on all stakeholders to maintain peace, unity and understanding, warning against divisions and feelings of exclusion among party members.

According to him, Tinubu urged political leaders and residents not to misconstrue his individual acknowledgements or appreciation of stakeholders, explaining that such gestures were intended to promote the collective interest of Ondo State.

The message came amid renewed efforts by the party to consolidate its structures ahead of the 2027 elections.

Earlier, Aiyedatiwa had assured Tinubu that Ondo State would deliver a minimum of one million votes for his re-election, saying the President’s economic reforms had begun to translate into development at the grassroots.

The governor listed the recruitment of more than 6,000 workers, road and bridge construction, rehabilitation of health facilities and support for young entrepreneurs as some of the achievements of his administration.

He also commended Tinubu for appointing three ministers from Ondo State, describing the appointments as recognition of the state’s contribution to national development.

Former governor Olusegun Mimiko also pledged to work with other APC leaders to deliver votes for Tinubu and the party’s National Assembly candidates.

Mimiko said the President had facilitated political consensus among influential political leaders, which he described as necessary for addressing major national issues, including insecurity and economic reforms.

Also speaking, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, who represented APC governors, called on Ondo residents to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), saying many collected cards were still awaiting collection at INEC offices.

In his goodwill message, Former Edo State Governor and Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole commended President Bola Tinubu for appointing prominent indigenes of Ondo State into strategic positions in his administration.

He described the state as blessed with men and women of remarkable intellect.

He particularly acknowledged the Minister of State for Finance, Prof. Taiwo Oyedele; Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Wisdom, and the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo.

He described their appointments as evidence of the confidence Tinubu had in the state’s human resources.

He said, “When the President needed not just a Minister of Finance, but one that will truly deploy experience and intellect, not only to reform the tax system but to manage the account for those transactions, he looked towards Ondo and knows that this state is blessed with men and women of remarkable intellect.”

The senator also commended the President for reforms aimed at reviving the manufacturing sector, saying increased local production would help create jobs and improve economic opportunities for Nigerians.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who represented President Tinubu at the rally, charged the state to deliver 1.2 million votes for the President, citing what he described as broad support for Tinubu among political leaders in Ondo State.

The rally was attended by APC governors, ministers, members of the National Assembly, national party leaders and other political stakeholders.

World.title: Yusuf Presents N1.107 Trn 2027 Budget
World.content:
Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

Kano State Governor, Alhaji Abba Yusuf, has presented a proposed budget of N1.107 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the Kano State House of Assembly, with a strong focus on capital development, completion of ongoing projects and accelerated rural development.

Tagged, “Budget of Consolidating Gains and Accelerated Rural Development,” the proposal stands at N1,107,024,004,244.48 and represents the fourth and final budget of the administration’s first tenure.

Presenting the estimates, Governor Yusuf explained that the budget was designed to consolidate achievements recorded since 2023, complete priority projects and strengthen essential public services before the expiration of the administration’s first tenure on May 29, 2027.

The proposed budget allocates N693.47 billion to capital expenditure, representing 63 per cent, while N413.55 billion is earmarked for recurrent expenditure, representing 37 per cent.

The governor said the capital-heavy structure demonstrates his administration’s commitment to infrastructure expansion, human capital development and investments capable of stimulating economic growth.

He further disclosed that the state projects N692.64 billion in recurrent revenue for 2027, comprising N142.84 billion from Internally Generated Revenue and N549.80 billion from the Federation Account.

Governor Yusuf also noted that more than 90 per cent of the programmes, projects and policies contained in the administration’s development blueprint had been achieved.

He assured that the government would strengthen budget monitoring, transparency and accountability to ensure effective implementation and value for money.

The governor subsequently presented the 2027 Appropriation Bill to the State House of Assembly for legislative scrutiny and passage into law.

World.title: Cybersecurity Experts Converge for ISSAN Annual Confab
World.content:
The Information Security Society of Africa – Nigeria (ISSAN) is set to host its 2026 Annual Cybersecurity Conference on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, bringing together leading industry executives, policymakers, regulators, cybersecurity professionals and technology experts from Nigeria, across Africa and the international community.

The conference, themed “Cybersecurity: Balancing Risk, Resilience and Responsibility in the AI Era,” will provide a platform for critical conversations on the evolving cybersecurity landscape, particularly the opportunities, vulnerabilities and responsibilities emerging from the rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence. Hybrid and Registration: https://bit.ly/4ignVK0.

According to a statement, as organisations increasingly integrate AI into their operations, the conference will examine how businesses, financial institutions, government agencies and critical infrastructure operators can strengthen their cyber defence capabilities, manage emerging risks and build sustainable digital resilience.

The event will feature an impressive line-up of speakers and industry leaders, including Dr. Aminu Maida, Executive Vice Chairman/CEO, Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC); Dr. Blaise Ijebor, Director, Risk Management Department and Chief Risk Officer, Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN); Dr.Rakiya Yusuf, Director, Payments System Supervision Department, CBN; Premier Oiwoh, Managing Director/CEO, Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS); Prof. Obadare Peter Adewale, CEO, Digital Encode; Mrs. Doyin Odunfa, Founder/CEO, Digital Jewels Africa; Dr. Bharat Soni, Chief Information Security Officer, GTB; and other distinguished cybersecurity and technology experts from Nigeria and across Africa.

The conference programme, the statement note, will feature keynote presentations, expert-led panel discussions, technical sessions and interactive breakout discussions addressing critical issues such as AI-enabled cyber threats, threat intelligence, incident response, cybersecurity governance, regulatory compliance, third-party risks and the protection of critical national infrastructure.

Speaking on the significance of the conference, President of ISSAN and Host and Convener of the event, Dr. David Isiavwe, said the increasing sophistication of cyber threats, alongside the accelerated adoption of AI, makes collaboration, professional capacity development and collective responsibility essential to securing Nigeria’s digital ecosystem.

The conference is expected to attract senior executives, Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs), Chief Information Officers (CIOs), Chief Risk Officers, IT and cybersecurity professionals, regulators, financial institutions, telecommunications operators, fintech companies, technology providers, government agencies, academics and other stakeholders.

ISSAN invites organisations, financial institutions, technology companies, cybersecurity solution providers, development partners and other stakeholders to participate in the conference.

According to ISSAN, opportunities are available for corporate partnerships, sponsorships, strategic collaborations, brand visibility and stakeholder engagement.

“Organisations interested in showcasing their solutions, contributing to industry conversations or supporting the advancement of cybersecurity in Nigeria are encouraged to partner with ISSAN,” it said.

World.title: Coca-Cola Value Chain Delivers $1bn Economic Impact, Supports 160,000 Jobs
World.content:
Raheem Akingbolu

For more than seven decades, Coca-Cola has been part of Nigeria’s commercial and social landscape, refreshing millions of consumers while building an extensive economic ecosystem that connects manufacturers, suppliers, farmers, distributors, transporters and retailers across the country.

The scale of this contribution is now becoming clearer. A comprehensive Socio-Economic Impact Assessment (SEIA) has revealed that the Coca-Cola System in Nigeria generated approximately $1 billion in value-added economic activity and supported more than 160,200 jobs across the country in 2024 alone, highlighting the far-reaching economic impact of its operations beyond the production and sale of beverages.

Conducted by Steward Redqueen, a global consultancy with experience undertaking similar assessments for the Coca-Cola System in more than 60 markets, the study examined the economic footprint of The Coca-Cola Company and its authorised bottling partner, Nigerian Bottling Company (NBC), alongside the extensive network of businesses that support their operations.

Using the internationally recognised input-output economic model developed by Nobel laureate Wassily Leontief, the assessment went beyond the companies’ direct contributions to capture the wider economic activity generated across their value chains. It examined how spending on local goods and services stimulates business activities, supports employment and creates additional economic opportunities across interconnected sectors.

The employment figures offer a particularly compelling insight into this multiplier effect. Of the more than 160,200 jobs supported in 2024, approximately 2,989 were direct jobs within the Coca-Cola System, while about 157,200 were sustained indirectly across sectors including agriculture, manufacturing, transportation, distribution, retail and services.

In other words, for every direct job created within the System, approximately 53 additional jobs were supported elsewhere in the economy. This illustrates how the activities of a major manufacturing and distribution business can generate employment opportunities far beyond its immediate workforce.

Local procurement is another significant driver of this impact. According to the assessment, the Coca-Cola System spent approximately $601 million on goods and services sourced from Nigerian suppliers in 2024. This expenditure supports a broad network of local businesses, including agricultural producers, packaging manufacturers, industrial suppliers and service providers. The System’s reliance on locally sourced, produced, manufactured and distributed ingredients and packaging further strengthens these economic linkages.

Beyond its immediate commercial operations, the Coca-Cola System continues to invest in initiatives addressing environmental sustainability and community development.

In February 2025, the System inaugurated a Packaging Collection Hub in Apapa, Lagos, with the capacity to process up to 13,000 metric tonnes of PET bottles annually. The facility is also expected to support approximately 1,000 informal waste collectors, strengthening the country’s recycling ecosystem while creating livelihood opportunities.

Water stewardship is another important area of investment. Through its Africa Water Stewardship Initiative, announced in September 2024, the Coca-Cola System is supporting a nearly $25 million investment across more than 20 African countries by 2030. The initiative, involving The Coca-Cola Company’s Africa Operating Unit, Coca-Cola Beverages Africa and Equatorial Coca-Cola Bottling Company, seeks to improve water access and strengthen community resilience.

In Nigeria, The Coca-Cola Foundation has also committed $1.25 million towards expanding access to safe water and strengthening water systems in Lagos and Abuja. The initiative is designed to improve critical infrastructure, build local capacity and promote more sustainable access to water for communities.

These interventions come against the backdrop of the System’s ambition to accelerate investment in Nigeria to $1 billion over the next five years, subject to a predictable and enabling operating environment. The proposed investment signals continued confidence in the country’s economic potential and the opportunities presented by its large consumer market and extensive business ecosystem.

Taken together, the findings of the SEIA present a compelling picture of the Coca-Cola System’s economic footprint in Nigeria. Beyond its familiar consumer brands, the business supports a network of enterprises, livelihoods and economic activities that contribute to national development.

At a time when Nigeria is seeking to stimulate investment, expand employment and strengthen local productive capacity, the assessment offers an important perspective on the wider economic value of manufacturing-led businesses and the multiplier effects they can generate across the economy.

World.title: NIESV Seeks Bigger Role for Women in Nigeria’s Real Estate Industry
World.content:
Sunday Okobi

The National Women’s Wing of the Nigerian Institution of Estate Surveyors and Valuers (NIESV) has called for greater recognition and participation of women in the real estate industry, saying qualified female professionals can compete favourably with their male counterparts.

The National Coordinator of the Women’s Wing, Alhaja Ibironke Ogun, made the call in Ikeja, Lagos State, while briefing journalists ahead of a four-day retreat and investiture scheduled for Abeokuta, Ogun State, from November 26 to 29.

Ogun, who described the programme as the first of its kind for the women’s wing, said the initiative was designed to strengthen professional capacity, improve visibility and create more opportunities for women in the real estate sector.

She said the programme, with the theme: ‘Women in Real Estate Practice: Challenges, Opportunities and Prospects’, would bring together about 250 female estate surveyors and valuers from state branches across the country.

According to her, the profession has evolved significantly in terms of female participation, noting that when she entered the profession, women were a small minority.

“I recall when I was about to go into this field. In a class of about 150, we were just five women,” Ogun said.

She, however, noted that the situation had improved, with women now occupying more professional and leadership positions across the industry.

Ogun, who was surrounded by the executive members of the Lagos State chapter of NIESV, including Olutosin Bamigbola, Agbalaye Toyin, and Ganiyat Balogun, said the women’s wing of NIESV would focus on ensuring that qualified female estate surveyors were given equal opportunities to manage projects, secure professional appointments and occupy strategic positions in government and private organisations.

“One of the things we will be doing is to ensure that the right peg is put in the right hole,” she said.

The incoming chairperson of the Lagos State chapter of the Institute added that the women’s wing would also seek greater visibility for female-led firms, stressing that women estate surveyors and valuers possessed the same professional competence as their male counterparts.

Beyond gender inclusion, Ogun identified quackery and fraudulent property transactions as major challenges confronting the real estate sector.

She urged members of the public to verify the professional status of estate practitioners before engaging them, warning that patronising unqualified operators could expose property owners and investors to financial losses.

According to her, registered estate surveyors and valuers are required to undergo professional training and examinations and operate within established regulatory and professional frameworks.

She said professional practitioners also operate under approved scales of fees, unlike unqualified operators who may charge arbitrary fees to attract unsuspecting clients.

Ogun explained that estate surveyors and valuers play critical roles beyond property sales, including valuation, property management, feasibility and viability studies, development advisory services and project coordination.

The incoming chairperson said professionals could advise investors on the appropriate use of land and bring together other specialists such as architects, land surveyors and engineers to ensure that property developments deliver value.

“An estate surveyor is trained to do feasibility and viability studies of projects. We advise on whether a project is viable and feasible and whether it will give value for whatever investment has been put into it,” she said.

On technology, Ogun said the women’s wing would explore the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies to improve professional practice.

She said although AI would not replace professional judgement, it would serve as an assisted tool for improving efficiency, analysis and service delivery.

Ogun added: “AI and other technologies are not going to be 100 per cent of what we do, but they will be assisted tools that will enhance our job.”

She also disclosed plans to strengthen the profession’s pipeline by introducing more young people, particularly secondary school students, to estate surveying and valuation.

According to her, the NIESV branches across the country would be encouraged to organise career talks in schools to educate students about the profession and its opportunities.

She said the initiative was part of efforts to “catch them young” and ensure that more young people understand the distinction between estate surveying and other professions within the built environment.

Ogun said the four-day retreat would also feature professional lectures, networking and cultural activities, including visits to tourist attractions in Ogun State.

The investiture, scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026, will feature a lecture by the Managing Director of Orange Island, Mrs. Yinka, while other professional women in the built environment are expected to participate.

She said the programme would provide an opportunity for female professionals from across Nigeria to exchange ideas, build capacity and develop strategies for greater participation in the real estate industry.

Ogun urged property owners and investors to patronise registered estate surveyors and valuers, irrespective of gender, to protect their investments and ensure professional accountability.

World.title: 2027: Our Strength Lies in Our Grassroots Support, Says Oborevwori
World.content:
Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, has said that the All Progressives Congress (APC) strength lies in its grassroots support and growing acceptance among the people, insisting that the party does not need to buy votes to win the 2027 elections.

Oborevwori made the declaration yesterday at the APC Local Government-by-Local Government campaign rally in Akwukwu-Igbo, headquarters of Oshimili North Local Government Area, where he expressed confidence that the area would sustain its strong electoral support for the party in the 2027 general election.

“How can we buy votes when we have the votes? Do you buy what you already have? It is those who do not have the people that will resort to such practices,” the governor declared, urging party supporters to translate their enthusiasm into massive votes.

He recalled that Oshimili North recorded the highest number of votes in Delta State in the last election, expressing optimism that the local government would consolidate its position in 2027.

The governor described the rally as an opportunity to celebrate his administration’s achievements and appreciate the people’s support, assuring them that more development projects would be delivered.

“Sometimes, when I look at the projects we have done here, it is amazing, and I am happy. I want to assure you that we are going to do more,” he said.

Oborevwori attributed the improved capacity of the state government to execute development projects to the economic and fiscal reforms of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, noting that increased revenue had enabled his administration to undertake more projects and approve a 13th-month salary for state workers.

“The money is coming from somewhere. The reform is working,” he said, urging Deltans to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to sustain the reforms and ongoing development initiatives.

At the rally in Asaba, headquarters of Oshimili South LGA, the governor disclosed that his administration had completed 54 roads in the local government area alongside interventions in stormwater management.

He maintained that he preferred to let the administration’s achievements speak rather than engage in political boasting.

“I don’t like talking about what I have done,” he said, challenging residents to assess his administration by its visible projects and impact on their communities.

On his part, the state Deputy Governor, Sir Monday Onyeme, urged the people of Oshimili South to identify with the APC and support its candidates, stressing the need for unity and collective commitment to the party’s success.

Emphasising his personal connection with the people of Asaba, Onyeme urged residents not to turn their backs on one of their own, and called for an overwhelming victory for all APC candidates under the party’s ‘five over five’ campaign slogan.

Also, the Director-General of the Delta State APC Campaign Council, Senator James Manager, described President Tinubu, Governor Oborevwori, former Governor Ifeanyi Okowa, and the APC candidate for Aniocha/Oshimili federal constituency, Rt. Hon. Ndudi Elumelu, as experienced politicians whose records of public service demonstrated their leadership capacity

Manager urged voters to assess the candidates on the basis of their records, achievements and programmes, rather than political sentiments. He also commended Oborevwori for the infrastructure development taking place across Delta State.

Presenting flags to the party’s candidates of the Oshimili North and Oshimili South constituencies for the Delta State House of Assembly, Hon. Innocent Esewezie and Hon. Bridget Anyafulu respectively, Chief Solomon Arenyeka charged party leaders and supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: Adeyeye: Nigerians are Suffering, But Tinubu Saved Nigeria from Economic Collapse, Bankruptcy
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

The Chairman of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Senator Dayo Adeyeye, has acknowledged the economic hardship currently confronting Nigerians, but insisted that President Bola Tinubu’s administration prevented Nigeria from sliding into economic collapse and possible national bankruptcy through its far-reaching reforms.

Adeyeye, who is also the National Chairman of the South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA), said the painful decisions taken by the administration, particularly the removal of fuel subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market, were necessary interventions to rescue the nation’s economy from a dangerous path.

Speaking with journalists in Ado-Ekiti, the Ekiti State capital, yesterday, the former senator said he understood the difficulties being experienced by citizens, but argued that the alternative would have been a deeper economic crisis that could have affected the survival of the country.

“I know Nigerians are suffering, but the truth is that President Tinubu saved the Nigerian economy from collapse and prevented national bankruptcy. The difficult decisions were necessary because the country was already facing serious fiscal challenges before this administration came in,” Adeyeye said.

He explained that Nigeria’s economy before May 2023 was weighed down by an unsustainable subsidy regime, declining government revenues, foreign exchange distortions and prolonged fuel scarcity, which he said created severe pressure on the nation’s finances.

According to him, although petrol prices increased after subsidy removal, Nigerians now have improved access to petroleum products compared with the era of persistent fuel queues and scarcity, while the foreign exchange reforms have brought greater transparency into the system.

Adeyeye also argued that the reforms had strengthened the financial position of state governments through improved allocations, enabling many administrations to meet obligations such as payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities.

The NPA chairman further highlighted the Federal Government’s student loan scheme and increased funding for universities as measures aimed at reducing the burden on families and improving access to education.

Drawing from his experience as a former Pro-Chancellor of Ekiti State University, Adeyeye said improved funding and better welfare for university workers had contributed to greater stability in the education sector after years of recurring industrial disputes.

On the 2027 presidential election, Adeyeye dismissed the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as a serious threat to President Tinubu’s re-election ambition, arguing that the opposition party lacked the political structure and grassroots spread required to defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

He said a party without governors, significant National Assembly presence or strong control of state assemblies could not be compared with the APC’s nationwide political network.

Adeyeye also questioned the strength of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s political base, saying a presidential candidate must first establish strong support in his home state before seeking national acceptance.

He expressed confidence that President Tinubu would secure victory in 2027, declaring his readiness to campaign across the country for the President’s re-election.

“I am absolutely confident and ready to campaign anywhere for Tinubu. I believe he deserves massive support and I am convinced he will win in 2027,” he said.

World.title: Unemployment: SA woman’s TikTok exposes harsh reality after graduation [Video]
World.content:
A graduate’s TikTok contrasting her graduation day with her job as a Milo promoter has resonated with thousands. Image: Pexels

Graduate unemployment rarely gets a face, but one South African woman’s TikTok has given it one.

In a short video, Amahle Shezi shows the gap between her graduation day and her life today, working as a Milo promoter in a supermarket.

Thousands of graduates have since shared their own stories in response.



Shezi, who posts as @mashezi, shared the video on 8 November as part of a TikTok trend.

It has since drawn more than 2 000 comments.

Life after varsity in two scenes

The clip has just two parts. In the first, Shezi stands at what looks like a graduation venue, with the words: “I haven’t seen you since we graduated.”

In the second, she is behind a promotional stand in a supermarket, offering shoppers cups of Milo.

The video doesn’t spell out the message, and it doesn’t need to.

‘It gets better’

The comments quickly became a space for honesty and encouragement.



One law graduate said they had spent two years unemployed and a year packing groceries before landing a lecturing job, urging others to keep going.

Another said they had skipped their graduation ceremony altogether because they could see what was coming.

Many others shared the jobs they had taken to get by while searching for work in their fields.

What the numbers say about graduate unemployment

The video went viral just as new jobs figures landed. On Tuesday, 10 November, Statistics South Africa reported that the official unemployment rate rose to 33.7% in the third quarter of 2026.

Youth unemployment stood at 47.3%.

A degree still helps. In the second quarter, graduates had an unemployment rate of 12.4%, compared with 39.2% for people without matric, according to the National Youth Development Agency (NYDA).

But graduate unemployment itself increased during that quarter.

Every job counts

For many young South Africans, roles such as promotions, retail and call centre work are a way to earn an income and build experience while they look for work in their field.

If you are still searching, government programmes and youth platforms can help you find opportunities and gain experience.

WHAT JOB DID YOU DO WHILE LOOKING FOR WORK AFTER YOUR STUDIES?

Let us know in the comments below …

World.title: Mama Joy received MORE public funding than Tatjana – report
World.content:
Mama Joy reportedly received more funding from government than Tatjana Smith did, a report has claimed. Images via IG

Sports fan Mama Joy – real name Joy Chauke – received more funds from the Department of Sports, Arts and Culture and other public funds than Olympic gold-medallist swimmer Tatjana Smith, a report by Renaldo Gouws has claimed.

The star athlete announced her decision to switch her sporting nationality from South Africa to the Netherlands after voicing grievances to the aquatic governing body, Swimming South Africa (SSA).

The Minister has since issued a statement, wishing Tatjana well. He also, despite public blame, stated that the 29-year-old’s departure should “not be turned into a political weapon” against his office.



MAMA JOY TRENDS AMID TATJANA SMITH NEWS

In a YouTube video, Renaldo Gouws claimed that Mama Joy had received more public funding from the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture than decorated swimmer, Tatjana Smith.

The FF Plus member – whose X spat with Mama Joy trended on the social media app in 2023 – claimed that the superfan had been the beneficiary of the department’s budget to travel to multiple international sporting competitions, at their expense.

Chauk received around R700 000 to attend the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France. She also attended the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar and the 2023 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Australia and New Zealand, which she claims was paid for by President Cyril Ramaphosa.



Gouws said of the link between the two females: “One is supported by the government through millions of rands, and the other is struggling to get funding, and their parents have to put in their own money for this athlete.

“What infuriates me is that there is a lot of arrogance from Mama Joy, who demands to be sent across the world to show how proud she is of South Africa, yet has never won a medal.

“She’s been to various events, and it’s cost the taxpayers millions



“When Tatjana wins a gold medal, she gets R700 00…she gets less money than what a superfan gets to sit in the stadium on their a** in the stadium and cheer for athletes

“This is astounding”

GAYTON IN THE FIRING LINE

DA’s Liam Jacobs also weighed in on Tatjana Smith’s decision with his own video, which criticised Minister Gayton McKenzie over the management of the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture.



He also touched on a report that SSA pay tens of thousands, from their own money, to travel to the upcoming World Aquatics Swimming Championships in Beijing.

“This department was able to find R31 million to send a massive delegation to the [2026 FIFA] World Cup, a 151-person delegation. They were able to spend R3 million on 294 match tickets, and R10 million on exhibition spaces.

“This is not an allegation of corruption – this is to say, what are the priorities?”



“One side of the ledger speaks about hospitality, entertainment, exhibitions and World Cup trips. And the other side of the ledger speaks out about athletes that have to fund themselves to get to international tournaments to represent our beautiful country.

“That is not a money problem, but a priorities problem”.

OLYMPIC SWIMMER SPENT R10 MILLION ON HER CAREER

Tatjana Smith has opened up about how her parents and support networks had to fork out around R10 million over the years to fund her 16-year professional swimming career.



“The reason for my success has purely been because of the people in my support group” she told Carte Blanche in a recent investigation.

In it, Tatjana also revealed that she only started receiving meaningful commercial sponsorship after achieving major international success. She added that she did not receive the consistent financial backing from SSA which she believed elite athletes needed, describing her relationship with them as “absent”.

WHAT HAS GAYTON SAID?

In a statement issued by the Department of Sports, Arts and Culture wished Tatjana Smith well on her future career with the Netherlands.



In it, the minister also stated that the gold medallist’s “personal choice” did not warrant an “attack” on him.

It read: “It is regrettable that some people have used a deeply personal decision by one of South Africa’s most loved athletes to attack the Minister. Tatjana’s choice belongs to her, and it should not be turned into a political weapon”.

The department claimed that it had both honoured Tatjana at the South African Sport Awards and gifted her prize money. It went on to elaborate on its roles and responsibilities, which were distinct from those of sporting federations like SSA.



“The Department does not run federations, and it cannot take on all of their costs. That includes the significant cost of competing internationally. The people who lead federations are responsible for running their affairs sustainably and for attracting the partners and sponsors who can pay for these costs”.

It continued: “The Department is aware of the problems at Swimming South Africa, including concerns athletes have raised. These problems are being dealt with through a reform”

World.title: Bad news for Orlando Pirates as key winger faces lengthy injury layoff
World.content:
Orlando Pirates could be without influential winger Ghampani Lungu for the Carling Knockout Cup semi-final after the Zambian international suffered an ankle injury.

The 28-year-old is facing a potential spell on the sidelines that could keep him out for the remainder of November.

The Football Association of Zambia (FAZ) has confirmed that Lungu could be sidelined for 14 to 21 days due to an ankle sprain. As a result, he has been withdrawn from the Chipolopolo squad for their back-to-back Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Burundi.



“We also have Ghampani Lungu, who has a right ankle sprain that could take about 14-21 days,” the association said this week.

Lungu has been an excellent signing for Orlando Pirates this season, contributing four goals and one assist in the 12 matches he has played.

His potential absence would be a significant blow for the Buccaneers, who are preparing to travel to the Cape to face Stellenbosch in the Carling Knockout Cup semi-final.

With the estimated recovery period, Lungu faces a race against time to be fit for the encounter. However, his chances of featuring appear slim.

Pirates also have other concerns heading into the semi-final, with four of their players called up to the Bafana Bafana squad.

There is always a risk of injuries during international duty, and any setbacks could further weaken the Buccaneers’ squad as they look to reach their second successive cup final this season.

World.title: How much fuel do you need for a trip through Kruger National Park?
World.content:
How much fuel do you need inside Kruger and can you fill up inside the park? Image: wikimedia commons

A self-drive safari in the Kruger National Park can involve several hours behind the wheel, particularly for visitors planning to explore different parts of the reserve.

While there are petrol stations inside the park, visitors should still plan their fuel stops carefully. Distances between camps and gates can be considerable, and game drives often involve travelling slowly, stopping frequently and taking detours along smaller roads.

So, there is no single amount of fuel that every visitor needs for a Kruger trip. The total depends on the vehicle, its fuel consumption, the routes you drive, and how many days you spend exploring the park.



Where can you fill up with fuel in Kruger?

Visitors do not have to leave the park to refuel. According to South African National Parks (SANParks), you can refuel with petrol and diesel at all major Kruger National Park rest camps.

These include:

Berg-en-Dal

Crocodile Bridge

Letaba

Lower Sabie

Mopani

Olifants

Orpen

Pretoriuskop

Punda Maria

Satara

Shingwedzi

Skukuza

The availability of fuel at the main camps makes it possible to plan a self-drive trip without carrying extra fuel in containers.



However, visitors staying at smaller bushveld or satellite camps should remember that these facilities do not necessarily have their own petrol stations. It is important to check the location of the nearest main camp before setting off.

How much fuel should you budget for?

The best way to estimate your fuel requirements is to work out the distance you expect to drive and use your vehicle’s average fuel consumption.

For example, a vehicle that uses 8 litres per 100km would need approximately 8 litres to cover 100km. A vehicle using 10 litres per 100km would need about 10 litres for the same distance.



Distance driven At 8L/100km At 10L/100km 50km 4 litres 5 litres 100km 8 litres 10 litres 150km 12 litres 15 litres 200km 16 litres 20 litres 250km 20 litres 25 litres

These figures are estimates based on the stated fuel consumption. Actual use may be higher in the park, where vehicles spend time idling, accelerating slowly, stopping for sightings and travelling over gravel roads.

Visitors should therefore allow a reasonable buffer rather than calculating fuel requirements to the last litre.

Why you may use more fuel than expected

A drive through Kruger National Park is very different from travelling at a steady speed on a highway.



The park recommends an average speed of around 30km/h on its tourist roads to allow for safe driving and better game viewing. The speed limit is 50km/h on tar roads and 40km/h on gravel roads.

Visitors may also spend considerable time waiting for animals to cross the road or stopping to watch wildlife. Longer routes, detours and repeated drives around a particular sighting can add to the distance travelled.

The type of vehicle also matters. Larger SUVs and 4x4s may use more fuel than smaller passenger cars, while air-conditioning, vehicle load and road conditions can affect consumption.



Some tips

It’s definitely worth filling up before entering the park, particularly if you are arriving with a low tank.

Once inside, avoid waiting until the fuel warning light comes on before looking for a petrol station. Top up when you reach a main camp if your tank is getting low, especially before travelling to a more remote part of the reserve.

Visitors should also plan their daily routes around their overnight camp. Trying to cover too much ground in one day can mean unnecessary driving and fuel use.



SANParks recommends taking a slower approach to game viewing rather than attempting to cover excessive distances.

Most visitors also should not need to carry additional fuel, given that petrol and diesel are available at the major rest camps.

But if you are considering transporting fuel in a separate container, check the park’s current rules and the relevant safety requirements with SANParks before travelling. Do not leave fuel containers exposed to heat or stored in an unsafe position inside a vehicle.

World.title: Caster Semenya rules out SA athletics role: ‘I will not work with snakes’
World.content:
Two-time Olympic champion Caster Semenya has ruled out taking up a leadership role in South African athletics, delivering a blunt message to the country’s sporting authorities.

The 35-year-old has dismissed the possibility of standing for election to the Athletics South Africa (ASA) board or becoming an ambassador for the South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee (SASCOC).

SASCOC is pursuing a potential South African bid to host the 2036 or 2040 Olympic Games.



‘No interest’

However, Semenya says she has no interest in becoming involved in the country’s sporting administration, citing what she describes as repeated betrayal by people within the system.

“I have been betrayed so many times by the very same people. I don’t see myself sitting at a table with an enemy,” she said on the sidelines of the Spar Grand Prix road running awards in Johannesburg.

“I am going to be honest; I am speaking just for myself. I have no interest in any position or any organisation at this moment.”



Semenya delivers blunt message to athletics authorities

Semenya’s relationship with athletics governing bodies has been shaped by a lengthy dispute over regulations governing athletes with differences of sex development (DSD).

The South African is a three-time world 800m champion and won Olympic gold at the 2012 London Games and the 2016 Rio Olympics.

Her career was also marked by a prolonged legal battle against World Athletics over rules requiring certain female athletes with naturally elevated testosterone levels to lower those levels medically to compete in specified women’s events.



Semenya refused to take medication to reduce her testosterone levels and challenged the regulations.

READ | IOC reinstating gender tests ‘a disrespect for women’ – Caster Semenya

Although she lost an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport in 2019, the European Court of Human Rights ruled in her favour in 2023 in a case concerning Switzerland’s handling of her legal challenge.



She has now made it clear that she does not see herself returning to athletics administration.

“They use you as bait, so I don’t want to be in a space where I need to answer to someone,” she said.

Focus on coaching and developing athletes

Rather than taking up a national or international leadership position, Semenya wants to concentrate on her own athletics projects.



These include her Masai Athletics Club and the Caster Semenya Foundation, which works to encourage children and communities from disadvantaged backgrounds to participate in sport.

“I want to fix my own ship, which is Masai Athletics Club, the Caster Semenya Foundation, which is my priority, and my athletes,” she said.

She added that leadership within national and international sporting organisations was something she intended to put on hold.



“At the moment I will pause it because I don’t see myself working with snakes.”

No ambassadorial role for 2036 or 2040 Olympics

Semenya’s comments also close the door, for now, on the possibility of her becoming an ambassador for South Africa’s potential Olympic hosting bid.

SASCOC is exploring the prospect of bringing the Games to South Africa in either 2036 or 2040.



Having represented the country at the highest level and won two Olympic gold medals, Semenya would be a high-profile figure for any national sporting campaign.

However, her latest comments make it clear that she has no intention of taking on such a role at this stage.

For now, the former middle-distance star says her priorities lie with her club, foundation and the athletes she is helping to develop.

World.title: Six changes: Bafana Bafana’s expected starting line-up vs Kenya
World.content:
Bafana Bafana head coach Pitso Mosimane is expected to make at least five changes from the team that took on Eritrea in the previous Afcon 2027 clash.

Kamogelo Sebelebele is injured and unavailable at right-back, as is Thapelo Maseko on the right-wing. Mosimane has also welcomed back three clutch players from injury in Mbekezeli Mbokazi, Teboho Mokoena and Aubrey Modiba.

BAFANA BAFANA STARTING LINE-UP TO EXPECT AGAINST KENYA

Goalkeeper: Ronwen Williams, Right-back: Thabang Matuludi, Right-central-defender: Olwethu Makhanya, Left-central-defender: Mbekezeli Mbokazi, Left-back: Aubrey Modiba, Central midfielder: Sphephelo Sithole, Central midfielder: Teboho Mokoena, Attacking midfielder: Relebohile Mofokeng, Right-winger: Tshepang Moremi, Left-winger: Oswin Appollis, Striker: Iqraam Rayners.



AFCON 2027: SOUTH AFRICA VS KENYA

Bafana Bafana have enjoyed a perfect start to the Afcon 2027 campaign. Mosimane’s side are on six points from two matches to lead Group D with a +6 goal difference.

The qualifying journey kicked off with a 2-1 home win over Guinea in Johannesburg. It was followed by the 5-0 demolition of Eritrea in Cairo. Those results also lifted South Africa to 48th in the FIFA world rankings and 10th in Africa.

With Kenya already guaranteed a place at the 2027 finals as co-hosts alongside Tanzania and Uganda, only the Group D winners will secure the remaining qualification spot. Two victories over Kenya, starting in Soweto on Friday before the return fixture at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi on Tuesday, November 17, would put South Africa in a commanding position to progress.

The clash between South Africa and Kenya also brings a familiar face into the opposing dugout. Bafana Bafana’s all-time leading goalscorer, Benni McCarthy, returns to South Africa as Kenya’s head coach, facing his homeland for the first time in his new role.

The Harambee Stars are bottom of Group D with just one point from their opening two matches. They suffered a 1-0 defeat to Guinea before settling for a 1-1 draw against Eritrea.

McCarthy has also had to deal with problems away from the pitch. The former Bafana striker publicly disclosed that members of his technical team have gone roughly three months without receiving their salaries.



Friday’s encounter will be the first competitive meeting between the two nations. However, they have faced each other four times in international friendlies. South Africa remain unbeaten in those matches, recording three wins and one draw, while scoring six goals and conceding two.

Bafana claimed a 1-0 victory in 1996. Then played a 1-1 draw in 2002 before Kenya won on penalties. South Africa secured a 2-0 win in 2011. In 2012 in Nairobi it was a 2-1 triumph.

World.title: Equatorial Guinea vs Zimbabwe: Kick-off time, venue and where to watch the AFCON qualifier
World.content:
Zimbabwe’s Warriors face a crucial test against Equatorial Guinea on Thursday as both nations look to strengthen their chances of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

The Group E encounter is the third match of the qualifying campaign, with the two sides level on three points after their opening two fixtures.

The match will be played at a neutral venue in Cameroon after Equatorial Guinea was unable to secure approval to host the encounter at home.



When and where is Equatorial Guinea vs Zimbabwe?

The match takes place on Thursday, 12 November 2026, at Stade Ahmadou Ahidjo in Yaoundé, Cameroon.

SuperSport’s broadcast schedule lists the match for 5:50pm CAT, while ZIFA’s fixture information lists the kick-off as 6pm CAT.

Where to watch Equatorial Guinea vs Zimbabwe

Zimbabwean and South African football fans can follow the encounter on SuperSport.



The confirmed broadcast channels are:

SuperSport Kickoff SA

SuperSport Kickoff Africa

GOtv Kickoff

SuperSport’s schedule lists the broadcast at 5:50pm CAT.

What is at stake for Zimbabwe?

Zimbabwe head into the match looking to bounce back from their 2-1 defeat to DR Congo in September.



The Warriors began their qualifying campaign with an impressive 3-2 comeback victory over Sierra Leone, with Marshall Munetsi scoring twice and Tawanda Chirewa also finding the net.

Equatorial Guinea, meanwhile, lost 2-0 to DR Congo before responding with a 1-0 victory over Sierra Leone.

DR Congo currently lead Group E with six points, while Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea have three points apiece. Sierra Leone are yet to register a point.



The top two teams in each qualifying group will secure places at the 2027 AFCON tournament, which will be co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

Victory would give either Zimbabwe or Equatorial Guinea an important advantage in the battle for qualification.

The two nations will meet again on Monday, 16 November, when Zimbabwe host the return fixture at the National Sports Stadium in Harare.

World.title: South Africans in Istanbul: Chance meeting on a street leaves Mzansi proud [video]
World.content:
A TikTok user filmed a chance meeting with fellow South Africans on a rainy street in Istanbul, Turkey. Image: Pexels for illustrative purposes

South Africans in Istanbul don’t stay strangers for long, if a viral TikTok video is anything to go by.

A chance meeting between fellow Saffas on a rainy street in Turkey has left social media users back home beaming with pride, and a few debating the etiquette of it all.

The clip was shared by TikTok user @galagain, who filmed the moment selfie-style near a tram line on a busy tourist walkway.



The on-screen caption sums it up: “This is what happens when you meet fellow South Africans.”

How the meeting unfolded

The encounter was warm, cheerful and completely unplanned.

The group mixed in a few isiZulu greetings and fell straight into easy conversation, like old friends rather than people who had just met thousands of kilometres from home.

One of the travellers, from Durban, was in Istanbul for work and had a few free days to explore.

The person filming said they work on a ship and were off duty, also making the most of some time ashore.

As it turned out, both were trying to find the same place: Istanbul’s famous Grand Bazaar.



They laughed as they compared notes on finding their way with Google Maps.

Saffas abroad react

Plenty of South Africans in the comments said the clip captured something every Saffa abroad recognises: the instant bond when you hear a familiar accent on a foreign street.

Not everyone was satisfied, though.

Some viewers playfully complained that there was no handshake and no hug, with one asking what had happened to Ubuntu.

Another said the background traffic sounded just like the taxis heading to Mamelodi and Mabopane.

Why Saffas abroad find each other

South Africans travel and work all over the world, from cruise ships to corporate offices.

Videos of Saffas bumping into each other in cities such as Dubai, London and New York have become a familiar and much-loved genre on social media.

World.title: Protesters clash with police in Spain after huge housing cost rallies
World.content:
MADRID - Police fired tear gas as sporadic clashes broke out in Madrid and Barcelona after huge protests across Spain over housing affordability and purchasing power just weeks before an early general election.

Hundreds of thousands of protesters turned out during Spain's first nationwide 24-hour strike since 2012, with authorities estimating around 120,000 demonstrators marched through the capital and more than 50,000 rallied in Barcelona.

Clashes broke out after the protests in Spain's two largest cities, as groups of hooded and masked demonstrators hurled projectiles at police and sparked fires, according to AFP journalists.

Video footage showed large rubbish skips as well as bicycles and pot plants engulfed in flames on roads in Barcelona with heavy contingents of police vans racing through the streets.

World.title: MAGA influencers reel after midterm rout of Trump's Republicans
World.content:
WASHINGTON - For years, influencers with the "Make America Great Again" movement thrived alongside President Donald Trump.

But after Democrats hammered candidates from Trump's Republican Party in last week's midterm elections, the content creators find themselves facing questions over their ideological and financial futures.

"I've been running on empty for too long," said conservative commentator Laura Loomer, a conspiracy theorist and confidante of Trump who announced last week she was taking a break from her podcast.

Samuel Woolley, a communication professor at the University of Pittsburgh, said post-midterm soul-searching would result in an inevitable "changing of the guard" among influencers espousing Trump's nationalist views.

"I would expect that many influencers who worked with MAGA are going through an introspective period in the same way that many conservatives are," Woolley told AFP.

Danielle Lee Tomson, a researcher at the University of Washington, said many prominent pro-Trump influencers were losing their appeal.

"A lot of these creators, like Laura Loomer or Mike Cernovich or even Jack Posobiec, they are now aging, they're older millennials," Tomson said, naming a few top influencers.

"They don't have the same kind of novelty as they once did," she added.

"Quite frankly, a lot of their message got boring."

- Underdogs -

Right-wing commentators like Posobiec, Tim Pool and Benny Johnson built their online audiences on a fiercely anti-establishment message.

But over time, their closeness with the Trump administration lent them an institutional air, having taken part in news conferences alongside the president and flying on his jet.

The midterms also put a spotlight on the waning momentum of top MAGA-aligned movements, such as youth organisation Turning Point USA, whose founder Charlie Kirk was shot dead last year.

Candidates backed by Turning Point were overwhelmingly defeated in last Tuesday's Democratic "blue tsunami."

Some pro-Trump influencers have opted to "reclaim that they're underdogs" after the midterms rout, Tomson said, and lash out at the Republican Party rather than Trump.

Specifically, they have accused the party of alienating young, white, working-class, male MAGA supporters by pushing for war with Iran.

Others have cheered Stephen Miller's appointment to White House chief of staff.

The combative Trump ultra-loyalist spearheaded the administration's staunch anti-immigration policies and is seen as a return to the MAGA movement's ideological roots.

Commentator Johnson called Miller's ascension "a complete game-changer" and a "great move."

- Who writes the check? -

Questions over money are also at the heart of the influencers' futures.

Some have thrived not only by monetising content, but also by receiving payments -- often through opaque channels -- from political funding organisations and lobby groups, Woolley said.

As social media personalities rely increasingly on an image of authenticity, some are now touting their independence as a way to stand out.

"Loyalty has shifted from the agenda to whoever is writing the check," said Alex Bruesewitz, a media advisor often credited with helping Trump return to the White House.

Following the midterms, the consultant criticised Loomer for failing to disclose that she had been paid for making certain posts on X.

And in 2024, influencers such as Pool and Johnson were linked to a case in which the Justice Department accused Russia of paying right-wing content creators to spread pro-Moscow messages.

Woolley said social media companies are the "wild card" in the influencer ecosystem.

Tech giants like Meta and Google "have shown themselves completely willing to shift their behaviours and policies based upon who is in the White House," he said.

So if sites like YouTube or TikTok took a more active stance on disinformation and hate speech, "it will change these influencers' lives and change their behaviours," he said.

World.title: Sunken treasure: Historic US ocean liner reborn as artifical reef
World.content:
MIAMI - A majestic and all-but-indestructible 20th-century ocean liner that once ferried royal leaders, movie stars and even the "Mona Lisa" to the United States was being deliberately sunk to become the world's largest artificial reef.

Experts were conducting a controlled flood-sink of the 302-metre vessel, a veteran of more than 800 transatlantic crossings in the 1950s and 60s, that is set to send it to its final resting place on the Gulf of Mexico's sandy floor, some 40 kilometres southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach, Florida.

"Two of the valves have been opened. The deployment process has started," said an official on the livestream operated by the city.

Florida's Okaloosa County, gambling that such a huge new reef would be a local tourism boom and attract dive and fishing enthusiasts, bought the long-decommissioned SS United States from a conservancy group for $1 million in 2024.

The vessel -- longer than the Titanic and the transatlantic speed record holder -- will become the centrepiece of Okaloosa's undersea garden of sunken ships, including World War II vessels, tugboats, and even a casino boat.

Captain Tim Mullane of Alabama-based maritime company Coleen Marine which led the repurposing, has described it as "a great honour to put this fine vessel to rest... where it's going to serve a second life" promoting marine fauna, diving and fishing.

A year-long process of cleaning the vessel, removing all toxins like fuel, paint and wiring, towing, environmental remediation, safety assurances, and eventual sinking cost roughly $13.5 million.

The SS United States, the result of a celebrated feat of mid-century American engineering, made its maiden voyage in 1952.

In its heyday, the luxury liner carried countless celebrities, including president John F Kennedy, Former King Edward VIII, Grace Kelly, Elizabeth Taylor and Salvador Dali. Future president Bill Clinton travelled on board on his way to study at Oxford.

Perhaps its most famous passenger was Leonardo de Vinci's "Mona Lisa," the 16th-century painting that visited America in 1963.

Within two decades of being built, the liner was out of service, falling victim to the growing popularity of air travel. It remained docked in Philadelphia for 29 years.

While the ship will rest at a depth of 180 feet, its top decks will be just about 55 feet below the water's surface, reachable for beginner divers.

Until now, the largest artificial reef was an aircraft carrier sunk 20 years ago off the coast of Pensacola, also in Florida.

Repurposing the SS United States keeps its heritage alive, said Okaloosa County tourism director Jennifer Adams Kemp.

"She's our country's flagship," she told CNN shortly before the sinking. "Why wouldn't we want to preserve that?"

World.title: Mbappe ruled out of France's Nations League game against Italy
World.content:
MILAN - France's captain Kylian Mbappe will miss his country's Nations League match against Italy with a hamstring problem, coach Zinedine Zidane said Wednesday.

Les Bleus take on Roberto Mancini's Italy in Milan on Thursday as they bid to strengthen their grip on top spot in Group A1, before facing Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday.

"He will miss tomorrow, he felt a little pain and we won't take any risk," said Zidane.

"It's a shame to lose players but it's part of the game. I hope that it's nothing too serious and that he'll be available for Sunday... It's just a minor issue."

The Real Madrid forward is back in the France squad for this camp after missing their last three matches through injury.

He has already netted 17 goals in all competitions for his club this season.

Mbappe scored the winning goal in Zidane's first match as coach, against Turkey in September in the Nations League, but had to leave the pitch shortly afterwards due to pain in his left knee.

After three wins and a draw in four group games, victory over Italy would see France qualify for the quarter-finals.

World.title: 40 mines, high unemployment: Northern Cape community votes for change
World.content:
POSTMASBURG - A small community in the Northern Cape has voted the ANC out of power in the Tsantsabane Local Municipality.

Rise Tsantsabane Communities (RTC) secured 43.8% of the vote in the recent local government elections, winning 13 council seats.

The ANC was reduced to just three seats.

According to Northern Cape Premier Dr Zamani Saul, this is not the first time RTC has beaten the ANC by a significant margin.

The ANC later regained control, securing more than 60% of the vote.

However, growing frustration over poor service delivery, with residents having to build their own bridges and roads, has once again shifted support towards RTC.

The party’s president, Michael Mabilo, says they are pleased with the election outcome.

“We are excited because now we have the opportunity to change the lives of our people,” says Mabilo.

He says the party will not pursue personal or political agendas but will focus on improving the lives of residents.

Mabilo believes the ANC became complacent, taking residents’ continued support for granted while failing to address service delivery challenges.

“It is an organisation that was never close to the people until the people decided to put their foot down and go the alternative way,” he says.

World.title: Tenth suspect arrested in SA over alleged plans to join Russia-Ukraine conflict
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Hawks have arrested a 38-year-old foreign national en route to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war.

This follows the arrest of nine other foreign nationals who were also allegedly on their way to join the conflict.

The man, who was arrested on Wednesday, will appear before the Kempton Park Magistrate’s Court on Thursday.

He will face charges relating to the contravention of the Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act 15 of 1998.

World.title: Matlala's silence at Madlanga Commission raises questions, expert says
World.content:
PRETORIA - Over the past three days, Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matlala has faced tough questions at the Madlanga Commission.

But throughout his testimony, the alleged crime boss has refused to answer some questions, repeatedly invoking his right against self-incrimination.

A crime expert says there needs to be a balance between protecting Matlala’s legal rights and ensuring the Commission gets answers.

“The right is important and it must be respected, especially because he’s facing criminal charges. But it’s a shield, not a menu where he picks the questions that he likes," said Professor Dee Khosa.

"It really becomes a problem when he points fingers at others, but it goes quiet when his own role, the role that he has played in the entire scenario.

"Because then the Commission only gets half of the story."

World.title: Iced cider and biscuit cake: Prince William gives glimpse behind palace gates
World.content:
LONDON - Britain's future king Prince William gave a glimpse of life behind the palace gates, including his son's budding talent as a wildlife artist and his own love of chocolate biscuit cake and cider with ice.

William paid tribute to the "quiet pride" and strength of rural communities in the November edition of Country Life magazine, which he guest edited.

"Nobody, in my experience, talks about 'rural communities' in the abstract. They talk about their village. Their farm. Their high street. Their children. It is personal, it's special, because it is theirs," he wrote in a first-person piece.

William and his wife Catherine, also known as Kate, split their time between properties on his father King Charles III's Windsor Castle estate and Norfolk in eastern England.

The couple, formally known as the Prince and Princess of Wales, have three children Prince George, 13, Princess Charlotte, 11 and Prince Louis, eight.

William is a major landowner, having inherited the Duchy of Cornwall, a private estate spanning 128,000 acres (51,000 hectares) across parts of England and Wales, from the king.

Asked to name a few of his favourite things linked to country life, William listed a bird identification mobile phone app, his dogs Orla and Otto, and a Land Rover Defender "a 2016 model in British racing green".

Equally important, he said, was a flat cap that "shows you belong, that you have a deeper connection with the countryside", and a pair of swimming trunks for impromptu dips "if I come across a beautiful stretch of river on a walk".

William, a fan of the traditional British pub, revealed his favourite tipple was cider, an alcoholic beverage made from fermented apple juice.

"I love very cold cider with ice," he said.

The issue also published a recipe for chocolate biscuit cake from the royal kitchens.

The cake, which he enjoys so much it was served at his wedding, was a regular feature of afternoon teas with his grandmother, the late Queen Elizabeth II.

Describing himself as definitely having a sweet tooth, he added he was "quite militant" about the recipe which had to be just the right balance of chocolate to biscuit.

And the magazine published a detailed drawing of a kingfisher perched on a branch by William's eldest son George, said to have been completed when he was aged 12.

World.title: How Sarah Wairimu lied to police about Tob Cohen's whereabouts
World.content:
Sarah Wairimu, charged with the murder of her late husband, Tob Cohen. [Nancy Gitonga, Standard]

Fresh details have emerged of how Sarah Wairimu allegedly misled police investigators about the whereabouts of her missing husband, Dutch businessman Tob Cohen, days after his disappearance, giving officers conflicting accounts of his purported travels abroad and failing to report him missing.

The revelations were made before the Kibera High Court by former Kilimani Divisional Criminal Investigations Officer (DCIO) Fatuma Ali Hadi, who told the court that Wairimu initially claimed Cohen had travelled to Thailand for medical treatment.

World.title: Buxton estate tensions escalate after county officials attacked
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

A dispute over the multibillion-shilling Buxton Point housing project in Mombasa turned violent after county officials were allegedly attacked while enforcing a government order suspending construction over outstanding contractual obligations.

The confrontation came a day after County Executive Committee Member (CECM) for Lands, Housing, and Urban Development Mohamed Hussein ordered GulfCap Real Estate to halt all construction activities pending the resolution of disputes involving the county government and hundreds of former Buxton Estate residents.

The officials were reportedly pelted with stones as they attempted to serve the developer with an enforcement notice, with allegations that individuals linked to businessman Suleiman Shahbal were involved in the confrontation.

Hussein condemned the incident, saying attempts to intimidate government officers would not derail efforts to enforce the law and protect public interests.

"Let them bring goons, machetes, and stones if they want. I am not intimidated. I will execute my duties, and nobody will threaten me. The law must be followed, regardless of who you are or how much money you have," he said.

"We are here for the people of Mombasa, and we will ensure their rights are protected. Nobody is above the law," he added.

The November 10 enforcement notice, issued by County Director of Physical Planning Qassim Ali, directed GulfCap Real Estate to stop further development activities and obtain valid construction permits.

The notice, issued under Section 72(1) of the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, cited construction under a varied development plan without county approval and an ongoing dispute involving the developer, former tenants, and the county government.

The notice was reportedly received by the project's manager, Billy Okendo.

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county government and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units and commercial spaces developed in the first and second phases.

An addendum to the agreement signed on January 15, 2020, outlines the county's entitlement, with the allocation expected to be transferred upon completion of the second phase.

In a letter dated April 30, 2025, the county demanded 10 per cent of the proposed 1,800 housing units, translating to 180 apartments. The demand was renewed in February 2026, with the county seeking details on how the allocation would be implemented.

However, in correspondence dated September 22, 2026, the Department of Lands, Urban Planning and Housing expressed concern over what it described as the developer's failure to provide substantive responses to previous demands.

The county also questioned whether GulfCap had provided performance security equivalent to 10 per cent of the total construction cost for each phase, as required under the agreement.

It further demanded proof of payment of the Project Development Fee, which is payable in instalments as the project progresses.

The county said it had also raised technical and planning concerns during a meeting with the developer on April 15, 2026, including the need to address outstanding issues and resubmit the masterplan application.

But the dispute goes beyond the county's financial and contractual entitlement, with more than 500 former residents accusing the developer of failing to honour promises made when they were displaced in 2019.

John Tsuma, Secretary-General of the Buxton Tenants Welfare Association, said former residents had waited for more than seven years to return to their homes despite assurances that they would be prioritised once construction was completed.

"We are very disappointed by what happened. We had a meeting with the CECM, and he made it clear that all construction activities should stop until the outstanding issues are resolved. We did not go there to fight anybody. We wanted the directive implemented," Tsuma said.

He accused the developer of benefiting from the project while former residents continued to struggle to secure the houses they were promised.

"The developer has benefited from A to Z. He was given land by the county government, and the houses were sold off-plan. Yet, when it comes to fulfilling the promises made to former residents, we are still being taken around in circles," he said.

Tsuma said residents were not demanding free houses but wanted the affordable tenant-purchase arrangement they were promised before leaving the estate.

"We are not asking for free houses. We want the tenant-purchase arrangement that was promised to us so that we can pay for the houses and return to our homes," he said.

He also questioned why the developer had allegedly failed to surrender the county government's 184 housing units under the joint venture arrangement.

Mohamed Mzee Rubea, chairman of the evicted Buxton residents, said the money paid to the families during their displacement was a relocation allowance and not compensation for their homes.

He said the former tenants were given Sh240,000, with assurances that they would rent alternative accommodation for 12 months and return once the houses were completed.

"What we received was relocation money, not compensation for our houses. We were told to take the money and rent houses for 12 months and that we would be the first people to return once construction was completed. But here we are, more than seven years later, still waiting," Rubea said.

He said the original agreement involved 522 former tenants who were promised priority access to houses under the redevelopment.

Rubea added that each household was also promised Sh60,000 as a deposit towards acquiring a house under the tenant-purchase scheme.

"We were promised Sh60,000 as a deposit for those who would take up the houses. The developer later said the money would only be given to those who actually acquired the units. We are still waiting, and many of us have not received anything," he said.
