World.title: Budapest housing prices stall as Hungary’s property market loses momentum
World.content:
Hungary property prices are rising at their slowest annual pace in more than two years, while Budapest’s residential market has remained virtually unchanged for three months. New figures also reveal substantial price differences between the capital’s districts, following a brief surge in buyer interest at the end of October.

Hungary’s residential property market appears to be entering a quieter period after years of rising prices. According to the latest figures published by property listings platform ingatlan.com on Wednesday, 11 November, annual house price growth slowed to 6.9% in October, down from 8.2% in September.

The slowdown was particularly pronounced in Budapest, where prices increased by just 1.8% compared with October 2025 – the weakest annual growth recorded in the capital since December 2023.

On a monthly basis, Hungary property prices rose by only 0.2%, while Budapest recorded virtually no change.

The latest figures suggest that the previous wave of rapid price increases has lost momentum, although a nationwide decline in property values has yet to emerge.

Budapest property prices have barely moved for three months

The stagnation in Budapest is especially noteworthy because the Hungarian capital remains by far one of the country’s most expensive housing markets.

According to the latest ingatlan.com figures reported by MTI, the median asking price for existing residential properties in Budapest stood at HUF 1.4 million (€3,862) per square metre in early November.

That was practically identical to the figure recorded a year earlier.

For buyers considering a typical 60-square-metre property, this translates into an indicative asking price of HUF 84 million (approximately €232,000).

However, the capital’s overall median conceals significant differences between neighbourhoods.

The price gap between Budapest’s districts remains enormous

Budapest’s central 5th district remains the most expensive area for existing properties, with median asking prices approaching HUF 2 million (€5,517) per square metre.

At the other end of the market, the 20th and 21st districts have median asking prices of approximately HUF 1.03 million (€2,841) per square metre.

This means that, based on district-level median prices, a 60-square-metre property would have an indicative asking price of almost HUF 120 million (€331,000) in the 5th district, compared with approximately HUF 61.8 million (€170,000) in the more affordable outer districts.

The difference approaches HUF 58 million (€160,000), illustrating why location remains one of the most important factors influencing property affordability in Budapest.

Newly built properties command an additional premium.

The median asking price for new homes in the capital reached HUF 1.72 million (€4,744) per square metre in early November, representing an annual increase of 4.5%.

The 2nd district recorded the highest median new-build price, at HUF 3.1 million (€8,551) per square metre.

These figures also demonstrate that the slowdown is not uniform across property categories. While the broader capital market has stagnated, newly built homes continue to show higher annual asking prices.

A final rush before Hungary’s mortgage programme changed

Another important development occurred at the end of October, when Hungary’s government-backed Otthon Start mortgage programme was being phased out and replaced by Wekerle Plusz.

If you missed it: What is Wekerle Plusz? Here’s the new housing programme the government offers instead of Orbán’s Home Start

According to ingatlan.com’s October demand analysis, the final days of the previous scheme triggered a temporary surge in buyer interest.

Between 26 and 30 October, telephone enquiries about properties advertised on the platform were 38% higher than on an average September day.

The increase was even more pronounced for Budapest properties meeting the former programme’s eligibility criteria, where enquiries were estimated to be 55% above the level expected without the policy change.

However, the surge proved short-lived. By 31 October, buyer interest had already fallen below the level normally recorded on a Saturday.

Across October as a whole, approximately 250,000 telephone enquiries were registered for properties for sale. Despite the temporary increase compared with September, average daily demand remained 15% below its level a year earlier.

The figures indicate that the late-October rush was closely linked to the mortgage deadline rather than necessarily signalling a broader recovery in demand.

What does the slowdown mean for buyers in Hungary?

The latest figures offer a mixed picture for prospective homebuyers.

On one hand, Budapest prices are no longer increasing at the pace seen during earlier periods of rapid growth. The capital’s three-month stagnation may also reduce some of the pressure on buyers to make immediate decisions.

On the other hand, relatively stable prices do not automatically mean affordable housing.

Even in Budapest’s less expensive districts, the purchase of a typical flat requires substantial savings or mortgage financing.

The government’s new Wekerle Plusz programme introduces different borrowing conditions for newly built and existing homes, potentially influencing which properties attract buyers.

Whether this leads to sustained changes in housing demand and prices remains uncertain.

For now, the evidence points towards a market that is cooling rather than collapsing.

Is Hungary’s housing market entering a new phase?

The latest property figures raise a broader question about the future of Hungary’s residential market.

Want to explore Hungary’s property market beyond Budapest?

The extended analysis on Substack compares housing costs in Hungary’s largest cities, examines the growing supply of properties for sale and explores how the new mortgage scheme could affect buyers.

Read our full Hungary property market analysis on Substack.

The slowdown in Budapest is occurring alongside significant differences in housing costs across the country, changes in mortgage support and shifting patterns of buyer demand.

These developments could become increasingly important for Hungarian households, foreign residents considering a property purchase and investors assessing the market.

While prices remain high, October’s figures suggest that the period of rapid and widespread increases may be giving way to more stable market conditions.

The coming months will show whether Budapest’s stagnation becomes a lasting trend – and whether the rest of Hungary’s housing market follows the same path.

World.title: Indonesia’s super priority tourism destinantions spotlighted in Budapest to boost Hungarian travel ties
World.content:
The Europe Committee of the Association of the Indonesian Tours and Travel Agencies (ASITA), supported by the Embassy of the Republic of Indonesia in Budapest, successfully hosted an official Tourism Promotion and Business Networking Event at the Kimpton BEM Budapest on 9 November 2026.

For the event, a specialized 6-member Indonesian tourism delegation—led by Mr. Rocky W Praputranto—traveled to Hungary to connect directly with Hungarian tour operators, travel agencies (represented in part by Ms. Zsuzsa Tukacs from MUISZ Hungary), tourism industry professionals, and travel influencers.

The event officially opened with key remarks from H.E. Ms. Penny Dewi Herasati, Ambassador of the Republic of Indonesia to Hungary, highlighting tourism as a crucial vehicle for cultural connection between the two nations.

“Tourism is the ultimate catalyst for people-to-people connection,” stated Ambassador Herasati during her opening address. “When a Hungarian traveller visits Indonesia, they do not just see a beautiful landscape—they connect with our local communities, experience our rich cultural heritage, and share in our universal values of hospitality. These personal, human connections are the bedrock of the deep, long-standing relationship between Hungary and Indonesia.”

Ambassador Herasati also emphasized Indonesia’s strategic shift beyond traditional travel hubs, championing the country’s Super Priority Tourism Destinations:

Lake Toba (North Sumatra): The world’s largest volcanic lake, offering breathtaking highland landscapes, a cool climate, and the rich cultural heritage of the Batak people;

Likupang (North Sulawesi): An emerging premier marine paradise dedicated to sustainable ecotourism, pristine white-sand beaches, and luxury coastal resorts;

Borobudur (Central Java): The world’s largest Buddhist temple and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, serving as the crown jewel of Indonesia’s spiritual and cultural tourism;

Mandalika (West Nusa Tenggara): A world-class integrated resort zone on Lombok Island, established as a premier global sports tourism hub hosting the MotoGP world championship; and

Labuan Bajo (East Nusa Tenggara): The exclusive gateway to the UNESCO-listed Komodo National Park, world-renowned for luxury Phinisi cruise adventures and rich marine biodiversity.

Following the Ambassador’s address, the ASITA delegation delivered a comprehensive presentation detailing these destinations and their latest travel packages, highlighting experiences ranging from ancient heritage and unique wildlife to luxury wellness and marine ecotourism.

The core of the event featured intensive one-on-one B2B matchmaking sessions, allowing Hungarian travel buyers to negotiate directly with Indonesian suppliers and destination management representatives. The Budapest event serves as the first leg of a three-nation European tourism promotion for the ASITA delegation, concluding today with a networking lunch to formalize new commercial partnerships.

Beyond fostering travel ties, the Embassy views this initiative as a stepping stone toward a more comprehensive cultural exchange. The Embassy plans to amplify this collaboration by integrating future tourism campaigns with gastro-diplomacy and cultural showcases across Hungary. To ensure continuous engagement, the Embassy will also serve as a dedicated information hub to assist Hungarian travel influencers, journalists, and content creators looking to feature Indonesia’s Super Priority Destinations in the local media.

World.title: PM Magyar: V4 to cooperate in EU budget talks
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar emphasised the Visegrad Group’s cooperation in connection with the talks on the European Union’s next seven-year budget, in a telephone interview with commercial news channel ATV on Tuesday evening after his visit to Berlin.

Magyar said Hungary, Czechia, Poland and Slovakia were presenting a united front on the EU budget, as were several other countries with an interest in upholding the importance of the Common Agricultural Policy.

Hungary, he said, was coordinating almost every position with the other V4 countries, adding that apart from a few exceptions, they shared similar views on nearly every issue.

Magyar said that just a few months after the strengthening and revival of Visegrad cooperation, it was already clear that this gave them substantive bargaining power in Brussels as well, since it involved more than 60 million people, and companies of defining weight. He said it was far easier to negotiate, whether with the president of the European Council or with other member states, in this manner than separately.

If you missed it: Hungary expands energy cooperation with Poland and Czechia in new regional agreement

The prime minister also touched on the Dublin summit to be held in the second half of the week, noting that the leaders of every European country will be present there. An informal EU summit follows on Friday, also in Dublin under the Irish presidency, where the EU budget and artificial intelligence will both be on the agenda, and many one-on-one meetings will be held with leaders of various countries, he added.

Magyar also touched on the political changes in Serbia. “We are proud that Hungary plays a stabilising role in the Western Balkans. I have already held talks with the leaders of all the countries concerned, and as soon as the new Serbian government is in place, I am ready to negotiate with its leader as well, either in Belgrade or in Budapest. Closer cooperation with the Western Balkan countries is as much in the EU’s interest as it is in theirs. We know from history how important it is that there be peace and prosperity in the Balkans too, and if the EU does not go there, other forces will, and those will certainly not be European,” he said.

As regards Hungary’s energy supply, the prime minister said the energy mix must be constructed so it is as cheap and as secure as possible. Hungary has interconnectors and cross-border capacities and can source gas from many directions, he added.

He stressed that the size of the transit fee is the most decisive element in choosing resources. “What comes from Russia is very cheap, but everywhere there is the exchange price, and Russian gas is also priced off the gas exchange, or the fee payable for the gas delivered to Hungary follows from that,” he said.

He also said he would negotiate with the Romanian prime minister about the Black Sea gas field, on which an agreement is already at hand.

“In Dublin, at the EU summit, we will also hold discussions with other international players. Transit fees are crucial factors everywhere, along with the volumes and the security of the supplies. It is in our interest that gas can come reliably from as many directions as possible. If that is the case, we can coordinate, and indeed bargain, over the transit fees,”

Magyar said. He noted that Hungary can purchase liquefied natural gas through northern as well as southern routes, and American, Norwegian and Azerbaijani gas can come via Turkiye, Romania and Russia.

World.title: Why Poland Has Spent a Decade Fighting Over Its Constitutional Tribunal
World.content:
The opposition, particularly the populist-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, denounced the move as a “coup”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s government portrayed it as another step towards restoring the rule of law.

It was the latest round in a decade-long fight that has drawn in the European Court of Human Rights, the Court of Justice of the European Union (ECJ) and the Council of Europe’s Venice Commission, all of which have questioned how the Tribunal is composed.

Most EU countries have a similar court; few treat it as a spectator sport. In a 2025 study of awareness of judicial independence in Germany, Poland, Hungary and the US, nearly half of German respondents said they were not very aware of their Federal Constitutional Court, despite its considerable power, compared with more than 80 per cent of Poles who said they were somewhat or very aware of theirs.

“I know this is shocking to people from other countries,” Anna Wojcik, a constitutional law researcher and journalist, tells BIRN. “I can’t think of another example of such a fierce political battle over a Constitutional Tribunal. Even in Hungary, disputes over the court have been more technical and legal in nature, rather than spilling into protests outside its doors.”

Part of the explanation lies in what the court can do in the very polarised politics of Poland: being able to rule on whether laws are compatible with the constitution, it is one of the few institutions able to overrule a parliamentary majority. Whoever controls it, or can stop it working, escapes one of the main checks on their power. Furthermore, it became central to the culture wars being fought in the country when it was the tool used by the previous PiS government in 2020 to further restrict abortion rights.

Anna Materska-Sosnowska, a political scientist at the University of Warsaw, sees two things converging in the current crisis: the long erosion of constitutional review, and everyday party rivalry.

“Electoral calculations matter, but reducing the whole conflict to a fight for votes obscures what is really at stake: who can effectively limit political power, and on what terms,” she tells BIRN.

Wojcik puts it more bluntly. “I think there is a strong sense in Polish politics of ‘it’s our turn now’ – a majoritarian view of democracy,” she says. “Ultimately, it’s all about power.”

World.title: Turkey ‘Hiding Weak Climate Record’ Behind Hosting of COP31
World.content:
“The time for words is over. Now is the time for implementation,” declared Turkey’s Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Minister Murat Kurum, who is heading this year’s United Nations climate conference, presenting COP31 as a moment to turn years of pledges into action.

But as the world’s biggest climate-related gathering takes place in Antalya this week, Turkey’s own environmental record raises questions.

Turkey became Europe’s largest producer of coal-fired electricity in 2024 and remains a major destination for European plastic waste. It continues to pursue fossil-fuel projects, including new petroleum and natural-gas infrastructure in Antalya itself.

The contrast has sharpened scrutiny of whether Turkey’s COP31 presidency reflects a genuine shift in its climate policy or is primarily an exercise in winning international prestige.

Environmental expert and climate activist Koray Dogan Urbarli says the contrast between Turkey’s climate diplomacy and domestic policies goes to the heart of its COP31 presidency.

World.title: From Behind Bars, Tirana Mayor Turns on Albania’s PM Rama
World.content:
On October 26, the day after Serbian leader Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led movement in a momentous election, Tirana mayor Erion Veliaj took a veiled swipe at Albania’s own leader, in power for almost as long as Vucic.

“Congratulations to the students for toppling the Machiavellian and populist from Belgrade!” Veliaj wrote on Facebook from behind bars.

“Student movements and protests do not signify the ‘end of the world’ but rather the end of ‘a world’. The sooner we as citizens and policymakers grasp this, the better equipped we will be to respond to the needs and expectations of this generation.”

Veliaj’s message, written from the prison cell where he awaits trial on corruption, money laundering and concealment of wealth charges, was widely interpreted as a dig at Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama, who is facing down daily anti-government protests in which students have assumed a prominent role.

World.title: Serbian Ex-Minister Arrested for Suspected Abuse of Office
World.content:
Former Serbian Economy Minister Rade Basta. Photo: Serbian Economy Ministry.

Former Economy Minister Rade Basta was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of defrauding public utility company Beogradske Elektrane (Belgrade Powerplants) of around 120,000 euros during his tenure as its director, the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade confirmed.

It is claimed that the money was improperly channeled to various sports clubs and associations while he headed Beogradske Elektrane from 2020 to 2022. Basta has not commented publicly on the allegations so far.

Basta was Serbia’s Economy Minister in the government led by Aleksandar Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party from 2022 to 2023. He was dismissed after calling on the government to impose sanctions on Russia because of “its aggression against Ukraine”. He subsequently founded the European Way movement.

He had been appointed minister as a member of United Serbia, a party that subsequently demanded his removal from all positions to which it had nominated him following his remarks on Russia.

Basta recently applauded the Serbian Progressive Party’s defeat in last month’s parliamentary elections. He told Serbian Times that he has long believed that “the moment would come when citizens would no longer accept a policy of fear, pressure and control over institutions”.

According to the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office, the other suspects in the case against Basta include the executive director of Beogradske Elektrane and legal representatives of various sports clubs to which the money was allegedly channelled.

The prosecutor’s office said Basta was charged with abuse of his official position while the Beogradske Elektrane director was charged with abuse of official position in aiding and abetting the offence. The other suspects were charged with money laundering.

“The suspects will be held in custody for up to 48 hours, during which time they will be brought in for questioning,” the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office said.

World.title: Croatian MP Seeks to Ban Anti-Abortion Prayers Near Hospitals
World.content:
Anka Mrak Taritas. Photo: Anka Mrak Taritas/Facebook.

Parliamentarian Anka Mrak Taritas, from the Civic Liberal Alliance, GLAS, said on Wednesday that she is seeking amendments to the Public Assembly Act to prohibit gatherings of people praying outside hospitals, which have become a common occurrence in Croatia.

She said the proposed ban would apply to all gatherings, regardless of size, including a single person, within 100 metres of a hospital entrance.

Taritas explained that the ban would apply to all forms of expression, “when such acts attempt to influence a female patient’s freedom of choice, exert pressure on individuals seeking healthcare services or on healthcare professionals, infringe upon patients’ privacy, or hinder free and unimpeded access to healthcare”.

The ban would protect women from pressure, harassment and violations of their dignity and privacy at a particularly vulnerable moment, specifically when they arrive at hospitals for pregnancy termination, she said.

Taritas noted that several European countries, including Ireland, have already introduced such bans. Spain, she added, had gone further by introducing a specific criminal offence of the harassment of women and medical staff outside clinics where pregnancy terminations are performed.

“The situation in Croatia is somewhat different because, unfortunately, a culture of violence against women is fostered here. Therefore, we do not expect this proposal to be met with any receptiveness,” she said.

She said the “public call by those praying for the subjugation of women, taking place on the first Saturday of every month”, constitutes institutional violence by a state that fails to protect women from violence.

She was referencing the gatherings held on the first Saturday of every month, when ultra-conservative Catholics meet in city squares to pray for “the restoration of male authority within the family”.

Taritas argued that these meetings expose vulnerable women to further trauma.

“All of this is part of that culture of violence and is an everyday reality for women in Croatia – a reality that persists under the auspices of the government,” Taritas said.

Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic sees women as “insignificant”, she claimed. “They only become ‘important’ in the lead-up to elections, even though they should be considered important all the time,” she added.

World.title: Bosnian Police Seize 150kg of Drugs, Targeting Organised Crime
World.content:
Drugs seized in Wednesday’s raids. Photo: POSKOK.

Fifteen people were arrested on Bosnia and Herzegovina on Wednesday in a major police operation targeting two organised crime groups suspected of drug trafficking and money laundering.

The operation formed part of a months-long investigation in which around 150 kilogrammes of drugs have been seized alongside 83 litres of amphetamine oil.

Operation “Vrtlog” was carried out by the Federation entity police and the Zenica-Doboj Canton Interior Ministry in cooperation with Bosnia’s Intelligence-Security Agency, OSA.

The 15 people arrested from Sarajevo and Zenica are suspected of organised crime, unauthorised production and trafficking of narcotics and money laundering.

During Wednesday’s searches of people, residential properties, auxiliary buildings and vehicles, police seized around 58 kilogrammes of a substance suspected to be cannabis and 39 kilogrammes of suspected amphetamine.

Police also seized 83 litres of amphetamine oil, which they estimate could be further processed to produce between 600 and 700 kilos of amphetamine.

They also confiscated firearms, mobile phones, equipment used for weighing and packaging drugs and other items of evidence.

“During today’s searches, more than 100,000 KM [over 50,000 euros in cash], nine passenger vehicles, one motorcycle, firearms and equipment for weighing narcotic drugs were seized,” said POSKOK, the Special Department for Combating Corruption, Organised and Inter-Cantonal Crime of the Federation Prosecutor’s Office, in an earlier statement.

Among those arrested are Muharem Smajlovic, Edib Dzedzibeg and Selma Bogucanin, the wife of Amel Bogucanin, who is currently in custody already on suspicion of attempted murder and murder during a gang-related shooting earlier this year. Ajdin Ribo was also arrested, according to media reports.

Smajlovic and Bogucanin are already known to law enforcement. Dzedzibeg and Amel Bogucanin were previously arrested together in 2022 during a police operation codenamed “Hornet”, which stemmed from the crackdown on the Sky ECC app used for encrypted communication.

The investigation is also reportedly linked to the arrest of Ibrahim Handanovic, an employee of Zenica prison who was detained on October 22 after a police chase in Zenica. He allegedly threw a bag containing more than a kilogramme of cannabis out of a car window during the pursuit.

The arrested suspects will be taken to police for questioning and criminal processing before being handed over to POSKOK.

The operation was conducted across Bosnian capital, Sarajevo, the Zenica-Doboj and Central Bosnia cantons, as well as in Bosnia’s Republika Srpska entity. under the supervision of POSKOK and on the basis of orders issued by the Federation Supreme Court.

World.title: Politics and Pay: Albanian Govt Locks Horns with Judges, Prosecutors
World.content:
A simmering pay dispute between Albania’s government and the country’s judges and prosecutors is becoming increasingly political.

Prime Minister Edi Rama has vehemently opposed the demands of judges and prosecutors for substantially higher salaries, claiming such hikes would make them better paid than their counterparts in richer countries such as Romania, Greece and Slovenia.

Rama says judges and prosecutors have no right to challenge the established practice by which the government sets salaries, conditional on parliamentary endorsement.

World.title: North Macedonia ‘Losing Ground’ on EU Accession as Neighbours Advance: Analyst
World.content:
North Macedonia has been waiting to join the European Union for more than two decades, having applied for membership in 2004 and received candidate status in 2005.

After years of delays, the EU finally opened accession negotiations in 2020. The first EU-Skopje intergovernmental conference followed in July 2022, but the process has yet to move forward.

The main obstacle remains a veto by its neighbour, Bulgaria. Amendments to North Macedonia’s constitution, designed to include Bulgarians among the country’s constitutive peoples in the preamble, were agreed as part of a 2022 EU-sponsored compromise to lift the veto. But their adoption – which is still a condition for moving forward – has yet to occur.

The European Commission’s latest progress report, published last week, records this impasse. While North Macedonia has advanced in preparing the benchmarks for opening the first negotiating “cluster”, known as “the Fundamentals”, it has made no progress on adopting the required constitutional changes.

World.title: Bulgaria’s Trakia Motorway tragedy: Recriminations and compensation
World.content:
Recriminations, including opposition calls for the Prime Minister to resign, and a Cabinet decision to award a strikingly large sum to the families and heirs of the deceased, have followed the November 10 chain crashes on Bulgaria’s Trakia Motorway in which 11 people died and 86 vehicles collided.

On November 10, Daniel Mitov, an MP for Boiko Borissov’s opposition coalition GERB-UDF, called for Prime Minister Roumen Radev and the “ministers responsible for the tragedy on the Trakia Motorway” to resign.

“Those in power have become accustomed to lying,” Mitov said.

“Today, (Interior) Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev announced that one of the reasons for the tragedy is that there is no connection between the Road Infrastructure Agency, the Ministry of Interior and the toll administration systems,” he said.

GERB MP Nikolai Nankov said that the section of the motorway where the accidents occured was “a skating rink” and for the first time in the past 30 years, as of November 10, there was still no announced winter maintenance system for the Trakia Motorway.

Kalin Stoyanov, an MP for the opposition Movement for Rights and Freedoms and a former interior minister, called for the immediate resignations of “all those responsible” for the November 10 chain crashes.

However, on November 11, a day after his party called for resignations, Borissov said that a law should be passed to prevent politicians commenting for at least 24 hours after such accidents.

Borissov went on to criticise the government for its lack of moral responsibility after the tragedy. He said that those responsible will not remove anyone, but will put the blame elsewhere.

“I removed three ministers for much smaller disasters, I removed Parliament Speakers for much smaller offences, this is a moral responsibility,” Borissov said.

On November 11, Parliament opened its sitting with a minute of silence for those who died in the chain crashes the day before. The ruling majority voted down opposition proposals for hearings of senior officials in connection with the Trakia Motorway crashes.

Road engineer Iliya Zapryanov told Nova Televizia on November that the Trakia Motorway is designed for a much lower load of heavy lorries.

Zapryanov said that the share of heavy good lorries among the vehicles in chain accidents on the Trakia Motorway is significantly higher than assumed when designing the highway.

He estimated that out of a total of 86 vehicles involved in the accidents, 22 were heavy goods lorries, or about a quarter. The motorway was designed to accommodate five to seven per cent of heavy goods vehicles.

According to Zapryanov, one of the quick solutions to relieve traffic on the motorway is to redirect lorries from Bourgas, Stara Zagora, Sliven and Yambol to Sofia along the Sub-Balkan Road , which is less congested.

“Drivers are worried about the lorries breathing down their necks . When you are moving at 90, 85, 95 km/h, the lorry behind you does not keep distance and bothers you,” Zapryanov. Said.

He also raised the issue of the lack of signs that specify a minimum distance between vehicles.

“Have you seen this road sign installed anywhere in Bulgaria? Who controls it? Where is the traffic police? Where is the Road Infrastructure Agency?” he said.

On November 11, the Cabinet decided to allocate 8000 euro each to the families and heirs of the 11 deceased.

This amount is unprecedented . It is the highest assistance to the relatives of the deceased that the state has ever paid.

Typically, such extraordinary financial support is provided to families of victims of natural disasters.

By comparison, during the floods in Tsarevo municipality in September 2023, the cabinet allocated 15 000 leva (about 7669 euro) each to the legal heirs of the four deceased.

The same amount of aid was also determined for the heirs of the four people who died in the floods in the Bourgas region on October 3 and 4 2025.

There is no other case where the government has provided financial assistance of this type to the relatives of people who died in road accidents.

In the bus accident near Svoge in August 2018, when 20 people died, the Social Assistance Agency announced that the families of the deceased and injured were legally entitled to receive a one-time benefit of up to 375 leva.

Meanwhile, the Romanian lorry driver whose vehicle reportedly was the first vehicle involved in the crash has been detained and questioned, but according to Bulgarian National Television, the Prosecutor’s Office will not press charges.

World.title: Remembrance Day 2026 observed in Bulgaria’s capital Sofia
World.content:
November 11, Remembrance Day, was observed in Bulgaria’s capital city Sofia with commemorations at the British and Commonwealth, German, Italian and French war graves.

This year, in addition to the traditional observances, speeches and prayers also honoured Bulgaria’s national day of mourning for the victims of the November 10 chain crashes on Trakia Motorway.

Remembrance Day commemorates and honours the dead in the wars of the 20th century. The November 11 date arises from the anniversary of the Armistice at the close of the First World War.

As is traditional, proceedings began at the Commonwealth War Graves section, with an address by British ambassador Nathaniel Copsey, a service led by Father Patrick Irwin, and with poetry reading by Irish ambassador Catherine Bannon and by William Gladstone school pupils Anna Filipova, Evelin Vassileva and Yana Borissova.

Floral tributes were laid by ambassadors and diplomatic representatives of several countries, Bulgaria’s defence and foreign ministries, Nato and military veterans from Britain and South Africa.

World.title: Bulgaria’s exports in January – September 2026 up 11.3%, imports up 14.5% y/y
World.content:
In January – September 2026, the total value of all the goods exported from Bulgaria amounted to 35 599.3 million euro, 11.3 per cent more than in January – September 2025, the National Statistical Institute (NSI) said on November 11, citing preliminary data.

In September 2026, total exports of goods added up to 4 422.5 million euro, an increase of 21.4 per cent compared with September 2025, the NSI said.

The total value of all the goods imported into Bulgaria in January – September 2026 was 44 565.2 million euro (at CIF prices), 14.5 per cent more than in January – September 2025.

In September 2026, the total imports of goods increased by 14.3 per cent compared to the same month of the previous year, adding up to 5 314.7 million euro.

Bulgaria’s total foreign trade balance (exports FOB – imports CIF) was negative in January – September 2026, amounting to 8 965.9 million euro.

In September 2026, the total foreign trade balance (exports FOB – import CIF) was also negative, adding up to 892.2 million euro, the NSI said.

World.title: Death toll in 86-vehicle chain crashes on Bulgaria’s Trakia Motorway is 12, with final figure pending
World.content:
The known death toll in the November 10 double chain crashes near Yambol on Bulgaria’s Trakia Motorway is 12, with 48 people seriously injured, according to Prime Minister Roumen Radev, while the Health Ministry cautioned that this may not be the final figure for the death toll.

The chain crash involved a succession of two accidents, according to the Interior Ministry, which said that on a section of the motorway in the direction of Bourgas, a lorry blocked the path of a bus carrying a group of people.

Subsequently, there was a collision involving a lorry carrying wheat, and a passenger car crashed into it, the Interior Ministry said.

The ministry said that 86 vehicles were involved in the incident in both directions of the motorway – 63 that had been travelling towards Bourgas and 23 towards Sofia.

Acting Interior Ministry chief secretary Lyubomir Nikolov said that all those who died had been travelling in the lane towards Bourgas.

A probable cause for the serious accident was sharp and dense fog, the ministry said.

According to witnesses, visibility was initially about 70–80 metres, but at a certain point it sharply decreased to about 10 metres.

The ministry said that it is assumed that the accident in the lane for Sofia occurred in a similar way, and it is possible that the drivers’ attention was diverted by the serious accident in the opposite lane.

Two pre-trial proceedings have been initiated, as the traffic accidents occurred in both directions of the highway.

The Health Ministry said that a total of 46 people had been admitted to hospitals in Sliven, Yambol and Bourgas.

Among the injured in Bourgas is a patient in serious condition who is in the operating room, as well as a patient with severe chest trauma.

Hospitals in Stara Zagora, Plovdiv, Haskovo and Sofia remain ready to accept injured people if necessary, the Health Ministry said.

It is possible that the death toll will rise after the cleanup is complete, the ministry said.

A medical helicopter took off from Sliven but was unable to land due to thick fog. The air ambulance teams were transported to the scene in police cars and joined the rescue operation. They remain on standby, the statement said.

It said that half of the area has been cleared so far. The most difficult stage of the operation is ahead – cutting up and clearing the cars that are piled up on top of each other, it said.

Sufficient quantities of blood have been provided in all medical facilities where injured people are being treated. Additional quantities will be provided if necessary.

The Bulgarian government information service said that Radev had cancelled events on his programme in Varna following his meeting with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The November 10 meeting of the Cabinet also was cancelled. The agenda for the Cabinet meeting had included amendments to the Road Traffic Act.

Radev said that news of the crash had reached him while he was on the government aircraft on the way to Varna.

“Immediately after landing, I ordered the Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev to leave on the government plane for Bourgas so that it could transport the wounded to hospitals in Sofia,” Radev said.

Two Spartan military transport planes immediately landed at Bourgas airport with stretchers and medical teams, he said.

At the moment, the information from the incident is about 12 dead and 48 injured, Radev said.

Since the concentration of the injured is in the hospitals in Sliven and Yambol, Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov ordered the military transport planes to be re-based from Bourgas to the Bezmer airport in Yambol.

“We remain fully prepared for the evacuation of the injured from Sliven, Yambol and Bourgas to the hospitals in Sofia,” Radev said.

He said that the government would declare November 11 a day of national mourning.

President Ilana Yotova cancelled a trip to Paris that had been scheduled for November 10.

(Photo: Interior Ministry)

World.title: VDL: EC proposes dedicated funding of 50 million euro for Black Sea maritime security hub
World.content:
The European Commission (EC) is proposing dedicated funding of 50 million euro for the Black Sea maritime security hub, which is to be brought into operation by Bulgaria and Romania, EC President Ursula von der Leyen said in Varna on November 10.

The EC also is to provide an additional 10 million euro for the search and rescue authorities in Bulgaria.

Von der Leyen visited Romania on November 9 and Bulgaria on November 10, against the background of the attacks – generally blamed on Russia – on merchant shipping in the Black Sea.

The EC president visited the Nikola Vaptsarov Naval Academy and held talks with Bulgarian Prime Minister Roumen Radev.

Speaking at a joint news conference with Radev, Von der Leyen said: “Europe stands with Bulgaria, in these testing times. Because Black Sea security is European security”.

“We have witnessed together this year and specifically in the last month an increase in the number of threats, attacks and incursions into Bulgaria, which is EU territory,” Von der Leyen said.

“Now, drones are sinking commercial ships, setting vessels ablaze and killing civilians. Lives are lost at sea, navigation is disrupted, and the cost of insurance is skyrocketing,” she said.

“And the intention of these attacks is clear: Russia wants to spread fear and uncertainty in Europe. We know the playbook. And we are building resilience against it. So you can count on a strong and united European response.”

“In a wider context, we need to operationalise the Black Sea Maritime Security Hub, conducted by Bulgaria and Romania. In this context I welcome the closer maritime cooperation between Bulgaria, Romania and Türkiye,” Von der Leyen said.

“It is important to have it now up and running, and therefore we want to have clear timelines for its completion, and we want to offer a dedicated funding of 50 million euro to this Black Sea maritime security hub. We need it now.”

Radev, who along with his government opposes military equipment assistance for Ukraine, said that Bulgaria’s efforts to support Ukraine “have never ceased”.

“Especially here in Varna people know very well that we have been providing support for thousands of Ukrainian citizens free of charge and this is significant,” Radev said.

“You see that we are putting we are investing and putting in not only the material but also the human efforts and support for the protection of Ukrainian citizens at sea and you know that the Chelsea 3 vessel a significant part of the crew was Ukrainian citizens,” he said.

“We continue our support for Ukraine also with the export of electricity and power and energy towards Ukraine. We continue also with our efforts at bringing back into use the energy and electricity plants and also in the maintenance and re-establishment of the railway infrastructure.”

Radev said that in terms of financial support, Bulgaria was in an excessive deficit procedure, “so we do experience we are supporting in the financial capabilities that we have and respective to our financial capabilities but I would like to say that Bulgaria is in no way blocking the decisions at the council level that are being taken in unity for everyone to support as they can”.

Asked about the origin of the attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea, Radev said: “The attacks are a result of the escalation of the war between Russia and Ukraine in the Black Sea. This is the reason for the attacks. As far as the details are concerned, we are continuing to work”.

“The international teams that we have announced are still in Bulgaria. They are working hard. We are keeping in touch with them but they still have not been able to identify the perpetrator,” Radev said.

“We base our claims against the third country on facts and not on preliminary conclusions. They clearly stated that these attacks are the result of an escalation of the military aggression of the war that Russia initiated against Ukraine. This is the origin, this is the reason.”

Radev said: “We would like to receive further data and specific facts as to who was the perpetrator in terms of the work that is still ongoing from the international teams. We are still continuing and working hard in order to be able to clearly state supported by the facts what the origin is”.

“Unfortunately, I would like to say that we would prefer to stick to the facts and not to any preliminary presuppositions and expectations,” Radev said.

(Photo via Von der Leyen’s page on X)

World.title: Bulgaria’s Foreign Ministry warns of public sector strike in Ireland planned for November 12
World.content:
A strike by public sector trade unions is planned for Ireland on November 12, Bulgaria’s Foreign Ministry said.

Local authorities are warning of protest marches and rallies in the time range of noon to 2pm, which will cover the entire country.

Marches and rallies are reportedly planned for the capital Dublin, they will pass through O’Connell Street and are expected to head towards government buildings; and the cities of Cork, Limerick, Galway, Waterford, Sligo, Tullamore and Letterkenny will also be affected by the protest marches.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs recommends that Bulgarian citizens located or residing in Ireland inform themselves and monitor current developments, including possible restrictions on certain public services, the ministry said.

(Photo: Gareth Jones, via Wikimedia Commons)

World.title: EU extends EU Military Assistance Mission supporting Ukraine for further two years
World.content:
European Union ministers adopted a decision on November 9 extending the mandate of the European Union Military Assistance Mission in support of Ukraine (EUMAM Ukraine) for a further two years, until November 15 2028, with a budget allocation of nearly 300 million euro for this period, a statement by the Council of the EU said.

The decision follows the recent strategic review of EUMAM.

In this context, the Council also decided to establish a presence in Ukraine to ensure direct and effective coordination with the Ukrainian military authorities, the UAF and like-minded international partners, thus ensuring that the EU training continues to evolve in line with the UAF’s needs.

The mission’s mandate is also enriched so as to focus on lessons learned from the battlefield and on strengthening military training in support of Ukraine’s defence agenda.

EUMAM Ukraine will continue to coordinate closely with other like-minded international partners such as the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada and Norway.

It will also cooperate with the Coalition of the Willing, as well as with Nato within the framework of the Nato Security Assistance and Training for Ukraine (NSATU) command.

EUMAM Ukraine is a key tool for the EU’s military support to Ukraine, with its core objective of contributing to enhancing the military capacity of Ukraine’s Armed Forces, the statement said.

The mission has trained more than 100 000 soldiers since it was established in October 2022 at Ukraine’s request.

World.title: German Christmas Market in Sofia’s City Garden to open on November 14
World.content:
Sofia’s now-traditional German Christmas Market in the City Garden opens in 2026 on November 14 and continues until December 21.

Bulgaria’s capital city’s oldest German Christmas Market (Deutscher Weihnachtsmarkt ) was first held in 2011, in its location in Alexander Battenberg Square near the Ivan Vazov National Theatre.

It features food and drink including mulled wine, crafts on sale, and fun for the children.

(Photo via the event’s Facebook page)

World.title: Vis Archipelago Retains Status as UNESCO Global Geopark
World.content:
November the 12th, 2026 – The Vis archipelago has successfully retained its status as a UNESCO Global Geopark for another four years as all 10 recommendations from the previous evaluation have been fulfilled.

The above was confirmed on the 4th of November at the 11th session of the UNESCO Global Geoparks Council, held at UNESCO headquarters in Paris. The Geopark Vis Archipelago has been part of the UNESCO Global Geoparks Network since 2019.

Morski reports that the re-validation, which is carried out every four years, included a review of documentation and a field mission by international evaluators from the 22nd to the 27th of June 2026.

During their stay on the Vis archipelago, the evaluators visited numerous geological sites, geotrails and visitor centres, and held talks with representatives of the local community, institutions, scientific organisations and partner organisations.

The international evaluators praised the way the sites are presented to visitors, the cooperation with schools and scientists, and the support given to local producers. They also highlighted how the geopark has connected Vis and Komiža in caring for the heritage of the entire archipelago.

World.title: New Dawn for Luxury Tourism in Kaštela With High-End Hotel Brand
World.content:
November the 12th, 2026 – A new dawn for luxury tourism in Kaštela is beginning with the arrival of one of the world’s most recognisable brands in the high-end hotel segment.

It’s genuinely no exaggeration to say that a new tourism dawn of sorts in Kaštela is now beginning. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that the international Odien Group, headquartered in Prague, is bringing Sofitel, one of the world’s most recognisable brands in the luxury hotel segment, to Kaštela and Croatia. The contract with Accor, one of the world’s leading hotel groups that includes the Sofitel brand in its portfolio, was formally signed at the Renaissance Vitturi Castle in Kaštel Lukšić.

high-end tourism

Sofitel Kaštela, which will be constructed on the site of the former Zeničko resort in Kaštel Stari, is expected to open its doors in 2029 and will be managed by Odien Hotels, the hotel division of the Odien Group. The hotel will have 137 rooms and apartments, including spacious junior suites and higher-category accommodation units with private balconies or terraces overlooking the sea. Guests will have access to several restaurants and bars, a spa centre, indoor and outdoor pools, a beach club, and spaces for business meetings and various events. It goes without saying that this is an important milestone for Croatian tourism, and especially for Kaštela, which with this project is positioning itself on the international map of luxury hospitality. For the Odien Group, Sofitel represents much more than a new hotel project. It is an important part of the group’s long-term investment strategy aimed at developing Kaštela into an internationally recognisable tourist destination.

a luxury hotel brand blends with heritage

Kaštela will get an internationally recognisable luxury hotel brand, as well as an intimate heritage hotel located in a Renaissance building.

“Our ambitions go beyond the mere construction of luxury hotel facilities. We want to contribute to creating a destination with a strong international identity, recognised for quality, authenticity and the experiences it offers. Kaštela has exceptional potential: a rich history, valuable architectural heritage, an authentic Mediterranean character and an ideal location between Split and Trogir. Combining all these qualities with the international recognition and reputation of the Sofitel brand, which is synonymous with quality, will undoubtedly open a new chapter in the city’s tourism development,” said Mike Saran, owner of the Odien Group.

“Croatia has become one of the most attractive European tourist destinations, recognised for its unique combination of natural beauty, rich culture and authenticity. We are proud that, through this exceptional project with the Odien Group, we are bringing Sofitel to the Croatian market as the first international luxury hotel brand in the country. Sofitel Kaštela will embody the elegance of French luxury while embracing the spirit, heritage and lifestyle of the Adriatic coast, creating a unique destination for travellers from around the world,” said Maud Bailly, CEO of the Sofitel, Sofitel Legend, MGallery and Emblems brands. The arrival of this prestigious hotel brand is part of the Odien Group’s long-term development strategy and commitment to Kaštela. As part of that strategy, the group will, through its companies Odien Hotels and Odien Real Estate, invest more than 100 million euros over the next five years. In addition to the new Sofitel Kaštela hotel project, the company this year also purchased the historic Štafileo Castle in Kaštel Štafilić, which it plans to renovate and convert into a luxury heritage hotel.

These two projects bring two different but harmoniously connected hotel concepts: an internationally recognisable luxury hotel brand and an intimate heritage hotel located in a historic Renaissance building, which will offer guests an authentic experience of local heritage. Together with the group’s existing hotel operations in Croatia, these projects are part of its long-term vision of creating new tourism content and value in Kaštela and throughout Dalmatia.

international luxury tourism for Kaštela

“These projects give the Kaštela the opportunity for a significant step forward in the segment of international luxury tourism. The city’s growing recognition as a tourist destination, its rich cultural and historical heritage and its geographical location form solid foundations for the development of a tourism offer that goes beyond the framework of traditional seasonal tourism,” said Denis Ivanović, Mayor of Kaštela.

“This is an extremely important moment for Kaštela. The arrival of an international luxury hotel brand and the Odien Group’s investments in our city confirm that Kaštela has the potential to become a recognisable high-end tourism destination. It is particularly important to emphasise that this is not just about one hotel project, but about a series of investments that can contribute to the development of the city, open new jobs, strengthen the local economy and extend the tourist season. For us, it is of key importance that this development takes place in parallel with the preservation of Kaštela’s identity and in close cooperation with the local community,” the mayor added. The Odien Group has otherwise been present in Croatia since 2015, when it took over the Le Méridien Lav Split resort in Podstrana.

World.title: Zagreb-Podgorica Direct Flights Coming on November the 26th
World.content:
November the 12th, 2026 – New Zagreb-Podgorica direct flights are coming on November the 26th, with the two capitals being linked in this way after several years.

Travel between Croatia and Montenegro will soon become significantly faster and simpler. Index reports that Montenegro’s national airline Air Montenegro has announced the introduction of a new direct route between Zagreb and Podgorica, with the first flight scheduled for the 26th of November this year.

The flight between the two capital cities will last only 50 minutes, allowing passengers faster and simpler travel without transfers. The new route will operate three times a week, and the flights will be operated by Embraer E195 aircraft, which can accommodate 118 passengers. The introduction of this route is part of Montenegro’s Public Service Obligation (PSO) programme, whose aim is to improve Montenegro’s international transport connectivity and enable more regular air links with important European destinations.

the upcoming flight schedule

According to the announced timetable, aircraft will operate between Zagreb and Podgorica on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays. From Zagreb, these flights will depart at 08:50 and are expected to arrive in Podgorica at 09:40. In the opposite direction, departure from Podgorica is planned at 07:20, with arrival in Zagreb scheduled for 08:10. All departure and arrival times are given in local time, and the schedule is of course subject to change.

the price

One-way ticket prices start at around 50 euros, depending on the direction of travel and the chosen date. On the official Air Montenegro website, the currently listed price for the first flight from Zagreb on the 26th of November is 58.30 euros. The ticket price includes all mandatory fees, as well as one piece of hand luggage weighing up to eight kilograms and one piece of checked luggage weighing up to 23 kilograms. The final price will depend on the travel date, seat availability and the time of booking.

The new air route could also be interesting for travellers who want to get better acquainted with Podgorica, the capital and largest city of Montenegro. Located in the area where the Morača and Ribnica rivers meet, Podgorica combines modern city life, historical sights and natural beauty. One of the places worth visiting is Stara Varoš, the historic city quarter that preserves traces of the Ottoman past. There you will also find the Clock Tower (Sahat-kula), one of Podgorica’s recognisable landmarks. A walk through this part of the city is an opportunity to get to know traditional architecture and local culture.

Among the best-known modern symbols of the city is the Millennium Bridge, which stretches across the Morača River. Visitors can also walk to the place where the Ribnica flows into the Morača and view the old stone bridge on the Ribnica. Nature lovers can head to Gorica hill, after which the city is named, which is a popular place for walking and recreation. Near Podgorica there are also waterfalls on the Cijevna River, known as the Montenegrin Niagara, which are especially impressive when the water level is high. For those who want to explore the surroundings of the city as well, an interesting choice can be Lake Skadar, known for its rich plant and animal life, picturesque landscapes and opportunities for boat trips.

World.title: Invasive Asian Giant Mantis Sighted in Mljet National Park
World.content:
November the 12th, 2026 – An invasive Asian giant mantis has been seen within Mljet National Park, with more favourable weather conditions for this particular species causing them to spread.

This insect is a species of praying mantis belonging to the family Mantidae, one of the largest families within the order of praying mantises. As we all know, the weird and wonderful family of praying mantises earned their name from the characteristic position of their front legs, which they hold raised and folded, resembling hands clasped in prayer.

Index reports that the authorities at Mljet National Park have noted that changes in weather conditions are creating increasingly favourable conditions for the survival of this species across Europe. They add that, as a result, the Asian giant mantis has spread across the eastern Mediterranean in recent years, including Croatia.

we’re unsure what the consequences of their arrival will be yet

They also explained how this invasive species can be distinguished from the native common praying mantis (Mantis religiosa). The Asian giant mantis has a significantly larger body and is recognisable by a white or yellowish spot on its front wings. Unlike the native species, it tends to stay high up in the tree canopies. Its body is mostly green, but it can also have brown or yellow shades, according to the park. They emphasise that this species feeds on other insects, but warn that its long-term impact on local populations of other species is not yet known.

As they point out, only in the coming period will it be possible to determine what consequences the presence of the Asian giant mantis may have on the local ecosystem, if any.

World.title: Bilić and Kovačić Promise a Different Croatia Against England at Wembley
World.content:
Croatia take on England at Wembley on Thursday at 20:45 CET (19:45 local time) in the fifth round of the Nations League, and Slaven Bilić heads to London with a depleted squad. Injuries, illness and suspensions have ruled out several key players, and Croatia arrive on the back of three straight defeats, including the 7-0 loss to England in Rijeka last month.

Bilić named his final 25-man squad on Saturday, but new problems

emerged over the weekend. Josip Šutalo injured his hamstring playing for Napoli against Lazio and will miss both November matches. Dinamo center-back Niko Galešić has been called up in his place, his first senior international call-up.

Kristijan Jakić is also a concern after injuring a knee ligament in PAOK’s match against Olympiacos. The midfielder has joined up with the squad but needs further medical tests. Bilić admitted the situation does not look good, though he hopes the injury is not serious.

Luka Sučić is also a major doubt. The Real Sociedad midfielder has come down with a fever, and Bilić said he is 99 percent certain to miss the England match. Lovro Majer, who was on the preliminary list but missed the cut for the original 25, has been called up as cover.

Ivan Perišić will also miss the England match. The veteran winger is suspended after his red card against Spain last month, but unlike the injured Šutalo, he will be available again for Sunday’s game against Czechia.



Kovačić opened the press conference.

“It’s a big and special game, as it always is against England. We need to be 100 percent focused. We need to be aggressive and give everything, especially after that tough defeat to England last month,” he said.

“I’m healthy and training, and that’s the most important thing. We have a big motive. We want to show who we really are and that we are still Croatia. That game against England in Rijeka was like a blackout.”

Kovačić, who played under Thomas Tuchel at Chelsea, was asked about the England head coach.

“I had a really great relationship with Tuchel. He helped me a lot and has a special place in my career and in my heart. It’s hard to tell the difference between Southgate’s England and Tuchel’s England. Both are aggressive and both are tough. We know England are always one of the top national teams.”

“We always give everything. What happened against England is something we still can’t explain. We had a really tough night in Rijeka, and that defeat still doesn’t sit well with us. We are motivated, and we want to prove it was only a blackout and that we are who we are.”

Bilić then addressed the media.

“We didn’t have time to train in this window. We only got together on Monday,” he said. “Last month’s game against England is still in my head. We showed against Spain that we are who we are, and we want to show that last time was just a bad day.”

“It’s very important for us to stay in League A of the Nations League. If we finish third in the group, it’s great for the Euro 2028 qualifiers.”

“I told the players that the way we played against Spain last month is our standard. That is how we want to play, with togetherness, aggression and everything else. We will see tomorrow whether we show that.”

“The young players were called up for a reason. They’re all in competition for tomorrow. They all bring something to this team. We have enough players to cover for the ones we’re missing. Tomorrow we have a chance to show that what happened in Rijeka was just a collective bad day.

I told the players after the game and again when we went to Split that the game against England was so bad that we need to remember it, to use it as motivation. The game against Spain is our absolute standard.”

World.title: Croatian Unemployment Rate Continued to Fall in October 2026
World.content:
November the 11th, 2026 – The Croatian unemployment rate is continuing to drop, with the figure having fallen by 15% in October this year compared to October 2025.

In October this year, 20,075 persons or 30.2 percent of the total number of unemployed used state monetary benefits. Poslovni reports that back at the end of October this year 66,425 unemployed individuals were recorded at the Croatian Employment Service (HZZ), which is 11,400 persons or 14.6 percent less than in October 2025, HZZ data published this week revealed.

a mixed bag

Compared to September the number of unemployed increased by 6.1 percent or 3,830 persons. According to HZZ daily data, currently 67,308 unemployed are registered at the service, and 13,099 free job positions have been advertised. During the month of October, a total of 16,792 new persons were registered in the unemployment register, which is 7.1 percent less than back in October last year. In this sum, the majority came from an employment relationship, that is 12,476 of them or 74.3 percent.

1,746 people from regular education (10.4 percent of the total number) and 2,570 persons from inactivity (15.3 percent) also entered into the unemployment register in the past month. The latest HZZ data shows that 12,962 persons left the unemployment register, which is 12.5 percent less than in October 2025. Of that 7,554 persons were employed, namely 7,029 persons or 93.1 percent on the basis of establishing an employment relationship and 525 persons or 6.9 percent on the basis of other business activities.

manufacturing reigns strong

The most frequent employment was established in the manufacturing industry. This October, 1,128 persons or 16 percent were employed in this sector. Wholesale and retail trade followed relatively closely with 983 individuals or 14 percent. This was followed by people coming directly from education, with the number totalling 903, or 12.8 percent. In October, 5,408 persons were removed from the unemployment register due to other reasons, e.g. leaving the force corps (retirement, inclusion in regular education), non-compliance with legal provisions (not actively seeking a job, unavailable for work), personal de-registration from the register and others.

Looking at the situation on a county by county basis, employment was led by Split-Dalmatia County (986 persons or 14 percent of the total number of those employed by establishing an employment relationship), the City of Zagreb (984 persons or 14 percent) and Osijek-Baranja County (736 persons or 10.5 percent). Split-Dalmatia County is also currently the home of the largest number of registered unemployed persons – 10,657 or 16 percent of the total number in all of Croatia. Looking at the situation based on the number of registered unemployed persons, the City of Zagreb (9,013 or 13.6 percent) and Osijek-Baranja County (7,757 or 11.7 percent) follow next.

In October this year, 20,075 persons or 30.2 percent of the total number of unemployed used the monetary benefit. The number of monetary benefit users decreased compared to the same month last year by 1.8 percent or by 374 persons. In October, 13,886 job positions were advertised through HZZ, through which the requirement for 21,519 employees was expressed. The number of sought workers decreased by 6.1 percent compared to the same month last year, the latest HZZ data shows.

World.title: Pantheon Data Centre Boss Refuses to Say How Much Water it Will Consume
World.content:
November the 11th, 2026 – The Pantheon data centre boss has refused to reveal just how much water the giant, guzzling centre will actually consume in Topusko. Criticism of the planned centre in Topusko is growing louder and louder.

The project manager of the data centre in Topusko has openly rejected claims that the enormous consumption of electricity and water would endanger the public or raise their bills. Poslovni reports that Pantheon project manager Mario Gudelj appeared on HRT’s Dnevnik, stating that the data centre’s investors plan to invest more than 500 million euros in new electricity infrastructure, including around 300 kilometres of brand new transmission lines and a new substation.

“If we were to connect to the existing system, then that would be an overload. We’re building new infrastructure, 300 kilometres of new transmission lines and a new substation, and we’re handing all of that over into the ownership of HOPS,” Gudelj said. HOPS had earlier confirmed that the project requires the construction of four new 400-kilovolt transmission lines with a total length of around 300 kilometres and that the investor would bear the connection costs.

one gigawatt – a massive consumer

Pantheon has been conceived as a data and AI campus of one gigawatt power, or 1,000 megawatts. This is an exceptionally large new consumer. HOPS representative Igor Šumonja at the end of October said that the current load of the Croatian electricity system ranges between 2,000 and 3,000 megawatts and that connecting Pantheon by itself would increase the load by approximately a third. Back in July, HOPS initially accepted the study of the optimal technical connection solution, and the investor and the network operator expect the conclusion of the connection contract. The start of construction is planned for 2027, and the investors want to put the first computing capacities into operation in 2029.

“electricity won’t be more expensive” gudelj claims, but topusko locals aren’t having it

One of the main criticisms of the project relates to the question of whether such a large new consumer can increase electricity prices. Gudelj just keeps on claiming that this will not happen. According to his words, the construction of the new network infrastructure will enable the connection of approximately five gigawatts of new renewable energy sources, whose production should be greater than the needs of the data centre itself.

“I don’t know on the basis of what someone made calculations that the price of electricity will rise because of us. I think that those calculations were impossibly made in the way they are presented to the public,” he said. In doing so he also reacted to an earlier statement by a HOPS representative that the operator cannot predict how the project will affect electricity prices. Gudelj emphasised that HOPS manages the transmission network and does not determine market electricity prices.

“we won’t take water from the public water supply” – but refuses to reveal what the water consumption will actually be

The second major question relates to the amount of water needed for cooling the data centre. Gudelj said that Pantheon will not connect to the public water supply system of Topusko or Sisak-Moslavina County. The investors, according to his words, are researching their own wells from which they would draw water, and the final quantity will depend on the results of the research. He did not, however, specify what the total water consumption of the data centre will be. That is quite telling.

criticism and protest against harmful data centres are growing louder and louder…

In more recent weeks, the contested Pantheon project has been encountering increasingly strong opposition from part of the political parties, local initiatives and environmental organisations. Green Action (Zelena akcija) has warned of the possible consumption of large quantities of energy and water, noise, electronic waste and the impact on the local environment. From that organisation they consider that Croatia before approving a project of such proportions needs to determine a national strategy for the development of large data centres. Criticisms have also been expressed by individual SDP deputies and local initiatives from Topusko, who are seeking additional information on the impact of the project on water, the energy network and the local population.

Gudelj, of course, rejects such claims. None are in his interest.

“Those are well-placed untruths that have no basis in anything. Our project will in no way affect things the way it is being pushed through public opinion,” he claimed for HRT. It will be interesting to see how those claims hold up when we take the likes of what happened in Ireland and Finland into account.

Despite Gudelj’s assurances, the project has not yet passed all the procedures necessary for construction. Sisak-Moslavina County has launched amendments to the spatial plan and the procedure of strategic environmental impact assessment. A main assessment of the acceptability of the intervention for the ecological network is also planned. Gudelj himself earlier said that the project cannot start construction before the completion of the spatial planning procedures and the acceptance of the necessary environmental studies. Therefore the final impact of Pantheon on water, the environment and energy infrastructure cannot for now be considered established.

Gudelj also commented on the accusations due to his earlier function in HOPS. He said that he left the executive function of president of the HOPS Management Board in 2019, after which until 2023 he remained an adviser, when he left the company at his own request. He rejected claims that due to his previous work in the transmission system operator he finds himself in a conflict of interest. Gudelj also considers that the current resistance to large data centres in Europe and the USA will not in the long term stop their development, but he expects that future projects will have to invest significantly more in their own energy infrastructure.

World.title: Zagreb Airport Attraction Wins Yet Another Prestigious Award
World.content:
November the 11th, 2026 – Zagreb Airport has an attraction that has won yet another prestigious award. The Museum Zone took home silver and has done very well in attracting passengers.

The Museum Zone at Franjo Tuđman Airport, a commendable project realised in cooperation between the Croatian History Museum and Zagreb International Airport, has won the silver the! Award in the multi-stakeholder and multi-sectoral cooperation category at the KoMference of the Croatian Public Relations Association. Poslovni reports that this is otherwise the second professional recognition for that particular project, which in the spring of this year took home the Grand PRix.

The Croatian History Museum, located in Zagreb’s Upper Town (Gornji grad) palaces, was severely damaged in the March 2020 earthquake, because of which it could no longer use its space for exhibiting its museum holdings. On the initiative of the Val Group, cooperation between the Croatian History Museum and Zagreb International Airport began. It was then that the Museum Zone was formally established, within which the exhibition “Stars of Croatian History – The Sky Is Their Limit. Get to Know Them!” was officially opened.

The exhibition presents 24 important figures from throughout Croatian history who, with their work spanning four areas – science, culture, politics and society, and sport – contributed to the development of Croatia and left a mark on the European and global level. “We’re pleased that a project that connected a heritage institution with Zagreb International Airport has been awarded and that this has been recognised as a very good model of communication,” said Minister of Culture and Media Nina Obuljen Koržinek at the KoMference.

Director of the Croatian History Museum Matea Brstilo Rešetar emphasised that when they entered that project they wanted to prove that heritage can meet the public even outside museum walls. According to her words, the Museum Zone has become the second most visited exhibition space in all of Croatia. President of the Management Board of Zagreb International Airport Huseyin Bahadir Bedir said that passengers have been given the opportunity to get to know Croatian history and cultural heritage in an interesting and accessible way, turning the time spent at the airport into an educational experience.

World.title: Expert: Europe is making a big mistake by trading on its security architecture
World.content:
Estonian experts and leaders consider it dangerous that a review of Europe's security architecture is being made a condition for ending the war in Ukraine.

Europe must be at the table in any talks on ending the Ukraine war, they add, in the wake of this week's Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.

"What exactly are the men in Abu Dhabi doing — negotiations, talks, or something in between? "Another round of talks, which we have seen very many times. And no result has come from it," Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) told "Aktuaalne kaamera".

In Abu Dhabi, European representatives practically sat with their ears against the door from outside. Tsahkna said discussing European security without European participation is dangerous — but that this is not what is happening. What is dangerous is if Russia talks about arms control and the others take the bait. "That can be sold to the world. Look what a good thing — both sides will start controlling their weapons and troop positions. But we know, and the Americans know too, that Russia does not comply with arms control agreements," the minister went on.

Presidential security adviser Rainer Saks meanwhile said Europe is setting itself up for a major mistake if it lets its security architecture be set as a condition for ending the Ukraine war. But above all, Europe has to represent itself, come what may.

"We saw representatives of five countries there, or was it four. Plus an EU Commission representative and a NATO representative. You cannot negotiate like that. Europe has to do its homework," Saks said.

Marek Kohv, program director at the International Center for Defense and Security (ICDS), meanwhile said Europe has to get its foot in the door to have a say. The Baltic states, though, must not let themselves be silenced.

"Here we can recall how all of Europe started to acknowledge at the beginning of 2022 — we have always said that Russia is a threat. And now, on the other side, we see from the American side this desire to quieten us, so that we no longer talk about things as they are," Kohv said.

Kohv noted, against the backdrop of Russian leader Vladimir Putin's demand that NATO keep clear of Russia's borders, that the alliance is internationally represented in the Baltics and has defense plans.

International talks are taking place in Abu Dhabi aimed at finding solutions to end the war in Ukraine. The process is made critical by the fact that a review of the broader European security architecture has been set as a condition for achieving peace. Although the talks directly concern Europe's future, Europe lacks strong and unified representation at the table — only four or five countries, the European Commission and NATO are represented, leaving Europe in rather the role of observer.

Tsahkna has said the best the Abu Dhabi talks can achieve is a ceasefire, and that he does not personally believe one will be reached because Putin wants to divide the West. Reform MP Marko Mihkelson, chair of the Riigikogu foreign affairs committee, went further, calling the meeting a "diplomatic special operation" aimed at imposing Russia's terms, and noting that Lavrov said outright Russia has no interest in a ceasefire because it does not want to give Europe time to regroup. Liis Mure of the ICDS meanwhile pointed out that every mechanism the Americans are now proposing — dialogue formats, confidence-building measures, arms control — existed before in the OSCE and the NATO-Russia Council, and Russia dismantled or withdrew from almost all of it.
